stories.title: 3 rebel Samajwadi MLAs set to get BJP tickets:Party organisation opposes strongman Abhay; Nishad quota complicates Vinod’s Kalpi seat
stories.summary: Three of the seven rebel Samajwadi Party MLAs are likely to get BJP tickets. They include Manoj Pandey, the MLA from Unchahar, who has been made a minister in the Yogi cabinet. The BJP has appointed Chayal MLA Pooja Pal as its state vice-president. Rakesh Pratap Singh joined the BJP on October 14. Along with him, MLA Abhay Singh and MLA Vinod Chaturvedi also joined the BJP. However, amid internal differences within the party, uncertainty remains over whether they will contest the Assembly elections. Two other rebel MLAs are Ashutosh Maurya and Rakesh Pandey. Both are still trying to find their place in the SP and have not joined the BJP yet. First, let’s look at the constituencies from which the three MLAs who rebelled against the SP could get BJP tickets. Manoj Pandey is considered one of the prominent Brahmin faces in the Awadh region. He won the Unchahar seat even during the strong BJP waves of 2017 and 2022. After rebelling against the SP in 2024, the BJP promptly made him a cabinet minister in the Yogi government, assigning him the Food and Civil Supplies portfolio, considering his political stature. Two factors are working in his favour for a BJP ticket. First, he is a prominent Brahmin leader. Second, he has a strong hold across the Awadh region. Considering his cadre and political influence, he is widely expected to contest the Unchahar seat on a BJP ticket. Rakesh Pratap Singh has been elected MLA from the Gauriganj seat in Amethi three consecutive times, in 2012, 2017 and 2022. He is an influential Thakur leader. Gauriganj has a sizeable Brahmin and Dalit population, while the Thakur community has long held political dominance in the constituency. Two factors are working in Rakesh’s favour for a BJP ticket. First, he is a prominent Thakur leader with a strong political presence. Second, he has an unblemished image. The path to securing a ticket is also considered almost clear for him within the BJP organisation. Pooja Pal, the MLA from the Chayal seat, belongs to an extremely backward community. The Pal community has a significant population across Prayagraj, Kaushambi, Bundelkhand and the Awadh region. This is why Pooja Pal was given a key post as the BJP’s state vice-president. Her husband, Raju Pal, a BSP MLA at the time, was publicly murdered by the Atiq Ahmed gang in 2005. Two factors are working in her favour for a BJP ticket. First, she is a prominent woman leader. Second, the BJP wants to build political momentum in eastern UP and Bundelkhand by giving her a ticket. Political analyst Ratanmani Lal says these three leaders won on SP tickets in the 2022 Assembly elections despite the difficult circumstances and the BJP wave. By giving them tickets, the BJP can not only increase its seat tally but also directly capture constituencies that have long been strongholds of the SP. Ticket prospects of these two rebel MLAs hang in the balance 1. Abhay Singh faces Khabbu Tiwari; deadlock over Gosainganj seat A tussle continues between Abhay Singh, a strongman MLA who switched from the SP to the BJP, and Indra Pratap Tiwari, popularly known as ‘Khabbu Tiwari’, a traditional BJP cadre leader, over the Gosainganj seat. During the 2022 Assembly elections, Khabbu Tiwari was in jail, so his wife, Aarti Tiwari, contested on a BJP ticket. Abhay Singh defeated her by 13,079 votes. UP Transport Minister Dayashankar Singh has openly backed Abhay Singh. Meanwhile, several senior leaders, including national general secretary Harish Dwivedi, support Khabbu Tiwari. Ignoring Khabbu Tiwari could prove costly for the BJP as it seeks to retain the support of Brahmin voters in the Ayodhya region. The party is also deliberating over Abhay Singh’s strongman image. It is possible that both leaders could be accommodated in two different Assembly constituencies in Ayodhya district. 2. Vinod Chaturvedi’s seat caught between Nishad Party’s claim and local opposition Kalpi MLA Vinod Chaturvedi has joined the BJP, but his path ahead is not easy. The Kalpi seat was part of the seat-sharing quota of the Nishad Party, an NDA ally. In 2022, Vinod Chaturvedi defeated Nishad Party candidate Chhote Singh Chauhan by just 2,816 votes. Nishad Party president Dr Sanjay Nishad wants to reclaim the seats his party lost. If the Kalpi seat goes to the Nishad Party, Vinod Chaturvedi will have to contest on its terms. Another challenge for Vinod is that the BJP’s local cadre and Chhote Singh’s supporters are opposing his candidature, calling him an outsider. Will the remaining two MLAs join the BJP or return to the SP? Rakesh Pandey, Jalalpur (Ambedkar Nagar): During the 2024 Rajya Sabha elections, he cross-voted in favour of BJP candidate Sanjay Seth. The SP has still not expelled him. Rakesh Pandey wants his son, Ritesh Pandey, to enter the Assembly through the SP. This is why he has not joined the BJP yet. Ashutosh Maurya, Bisauli (Badaun): After rebelling, Ashutosh Maurya met SP chief Akhilesh Yadav and apologised. After receiving Akhilesh Yadav’s forgiveness, he has remained active in the SP. However, he won the 2022 election by a margin of just 1,834 votes. If the SP does not give him a ticket, he could switch sides. BJP wants to regain lost ground in Awadh and Bundelkhand The question now is why the BJP is focusing so much on these seven rebel SP MLAs. There are three major reasons. First, the BJP lost high-profile Lok Sabha seats such as Faizabad (Ayodhya), Amethi and Kaushambi in the 2024 elections. The party is banking on these influential local leaders to strengthen its lost foothold in these areas. Second, the rebel MLAs include prominent Brahmin leaders such as Manoj Pandey and Vinod Chaturvedi, Thakur leaders such as Rakesh Pratap Singh and Abhay Singh, and an extremely backwards-class leader like Pooja Pal. By bringing these leaders on board, the BJP wants to consolidate the vote banks of these communities and strengthen its position in the Awadh and Bundelkhand regions ahead of the 2027 elections. Third, these leaders managed to win their respective seats on SP tickets in the 2022 Assembly elections despite the BJP wave. The BJP believes that bringing them into its fold could not only increase its seat tally but also help it make direct inroads into the SP’s strongholds. SP MLAs rebelled after cross-voting In February 2024, elections were held for 10 Rajya Sabha seats in Uttar Pradesh. The contest became complicated as 11 candidates were in the fray for the 10 seats. The BJP fielded Sanjay Seth as its eighth candidate, while the SP did not have enough votes to win all three seats contested by its candidates. On polling day, seven SP MLAs- Manoj Pandey, Rakesh Pratap Singh, Abhay Singh, Pooja Pal, Vinod Chaturvedi, Rakesh Pandey, and Ashutosh Maurya- defied the party whip and cross-voted in favour of BJP candidate Sanjay Seth. As a result, all eight BJP candidates won, while the SP’s third candidate lost the election.

stories.title: Judge throws pen after sentencing Muskaan and Sahil to death:Orders them hanged by neck until dead; quotes Mahabharata verse
stories.summary: In the high-profile murder case of Merchant Navy officer Saurabh Rajput, who was killed by his wife, Muskaan Rastogi, and her lover, Sahil, a Meerut court sentenced both accused to death on Wednesday. The brutal murder had shocked the nation. Meerut District Judge Arvind Kumar Mishra pronounced the verdict at 4.22 pm. As soon as the sentence was announced, Saurabh’s mother and brother, who were seated in the courtroom, broke down. His mother folded her hands and thanked the court before wiping away her tears with the pallu of her sari. Quoting a Hindi rendering of a verse from the Mahabharata, the district judge said, Punishing those who commit wrongdoing is also a duty of righteousness. When the people sleep, the court delivers punishment. The judge immediately threw into a dustbin the pen he had used to write the death sentence for Muskaan and Sahil. Read what happened, and when, inside the courtroom on Wednesday, the day Muskaan, who cut Saurabh’s body into five pieces and packed them in a blue drum, and her lover Sahil were sentenced… Muskaan joined the courtroom with her daughter in her lap 20 minutes before the sentence 4 pm: The Meerut district judge’s courtroom was packed with people waiting to hear the verdict in the sensational blue drum murder case. Saurabh’s mother, Renu Devi, and his elder brother, Rahul alias Bablu, were seated on chairs. Several senior and junior lawyers were also present. After 4 pm, Muskaan and Sahil were connected to the courtroom from jail through a video conference. Muskaan was wearing a blue kurta and a black dupatta. Her 10-month-old daughter was in her lap. Sahil was wearing a white T-shirt. Muskaan looked towards Sahil, with tears in her eyes. Sahil also looked at Muskaan one last time. After looking at each other, both lowered their eyes. Muskaan repeatedly wiped her tears with her dupatta. Muskaan began crying loudly as soon as she saw the judge District Judge Arvind Kumar Mishra arrived and took his seat. He looked at Muskaan and Sahil on the computer screen. As soon as Muskaan saw the judge, she began crying loudly. Her cries could be heard throughout the courtroom. Sahil, who had been looking down, also began sobbing after seeing Muskaan. The judge said, “Muskaan and Sahil Shukla, both of you have murdered Saurabh Rajput.” As soon as the district judge said this, silence fell over the packed courtroom. The lawyers representing Muskaan and Sahil, who were standing in front, appeared tense. Their eyes filled with tears as they waited to hear what punishment the judge would announce. As soon as the district judge declared, “The court sentences both of you to death for the brutal murder of Saurabh Rajput,” Muskaan and Sahil began crying intensely. The district judge also imposed fines on both of them. Muskaan told the court in the morning, ‘Please look after my daughter’ 10.30 am: Meerut District Judge Arvind Kumar Mishra entered the courtroom and took his seat. The courtroom was empty, with only prosecution lawyer DGC KK Chaubey, defence lawyer Rekha Jain and a few senior advocates present. Muskaan and Sahil were connected to the courtroom from jail through video conferencing. Muskaan was wearing a light blue kurta and a black dupatta. She kept her eyes lowered, as did Sahil, who was wearing a white T-shirt. Muskaan briefly glanced at Sahil before lowering her eyes again. The judge said, “Muskaan and Sahil, both of you have murdered Saurabh Rajput.” He then asked them one by one about their names, ages, education, addresses, and family details. Both answered his questions. After this, the judge first asked Muskaan, “Do you have anything to say about your sentence?” Sobbing, Muskaan replied only, “Please look after my daughter, who is with me in jail.” The judge then asked Sahil, “Sahil Shukla, do you have anything to say about your sentence?” Sahil kept his head bowed and did not respond. The judge then said, “All right, we will announce your sentence later.” As soon as he said this, both were disconnected from the video conference. Saurabh’s lawyer says, ‘The minimum sentence should be the death penalty’ After this, Vijay Bahadur Singh, the lawyer representing Saurabh’s family, began his arguments. He strongly presented his case by connecting the statements of all 22 witnesses in the Muskaan-Sahil case with the various pieces of evidence. He urged the court to award both accused the death penalty as the minimum punishment. After hearing the arguments of all three lawyers, the district judge announced that the sentence would be pronounced after lunch and rose from his chair. Saurabh’s mother said tearfully, ‘We received justice very peacefully’ Muskaan-Sahil’s lawyer says, ‘They have two young daughters; award a lesser sentence’ After this, Rekha Jain, the lawyer representing Muskaan and Sahil, began her arguments and presented their case. Rekha Jain said that Muskaan and Sahil had not committed the murder as part of any premeditated plan. Muskaan has two young daughters, and there is no one to look after and raise them. Her parents are elderly and unwell. Therefore, the court should consider the responsibility of raising the children. Sahil is also a student, and his entire future depends on the court’s decision today. The future of a young person is at stake. Therefore, I request the court to award a lesser sentence to both of them. Based on the evidence and witness testimonies as well, Muskaan and Sahil deserve the minimum possible sentence, she argued. Saurabh’s lawyer says, ‘The minimum sentence should be the death penalty’ After this, Vijay Bahadur Singh, the lawyer representing Saurabh’s family, began his arguments. He strongly presented his case by connecting the statements of all 22 witnesses in the Muskaan-Sahil case with the various pieces of evidence. He urged the court to award both accused the death penalty as the minimum punishment. After hearing the arguments of all three lawyers, the district judge announced that the sentence would be pronounced after lunch and rose from his chair. Saurabh’s mother said tearfully, ‘We received justice very peacefully’ After Muskaan and Sahil were sentenced to death, Saurabh’s mother broke down in tears. She said, “We received justice very peacefully.” Saurabh’s brother, Bablu, said, “We were hopeful that we would get justice. From the beginning, we had only one demand: the death penalty. We are very happy that both have been sentenced to death. If Muskaan and Sahil appeal or take any further legal action, we will also approach the court.” Muskaan’s parents tell court in writing, ‘We have nothing to do with our daughter’ No one from Muskaan’s or Sahil’s family appeared in court. On Wednesday morning, Muskaan’s parents wrote a letter and sent it to the court through the police. In the letter, they stated that they had no concern about whatever punishment Muskaan received. They would never meet her again and wanted nothing to do with her young daughter either.

stories.title: Vindhyachal Dham is Siddhpeeth, not Shaktipeeth:'Trikone Parikrama' fulfills wishes; complete guide from reaching Mirzapur to temple darshan
stories.summary: If you are planning to visit Vindhyachal Dham in Mirzapur during Navratri for darshan, you must know about the 'Trikon Yatra'. According to beliefs, until you complete the Trikon circumambulation, the pilgrimage is considered incomplete. The first stop of this pilgrimage is the Maa Vindhyavasini Temple. The second stop is the Ashtabhuji Devi Temple. The third stop is the Kali Khoh Temple. Whether you are coming to Vindhyachal by train, bus, or in your own vehicle and wish to have an easy darshan while avoiding heavy crowds of devotees, this simple route map will prove very useful to you. How to Reach the Shrine by Bus, Car, or Train By Train: To reach the Vindhyachal Temple, you will need to alight at Mirzapur Railway Station. The distance from Mirzapur Station to Vindhyachal Dham is approximately 8 to 9 kilometres. From here, it takes 20 to 30 minutes to reach by auto-rickshaw or e-rickshaw. Vindhyachal Railway Station is also located near the shrine, but only a few express and passenger trains halt there. By Bus or Car: UP Roadways buses to Vindhyachal are easily available from Varanasi, Prayagraj, and nearby districts. Vindhyachal Dham is connected by road from all four directions. If you are arriving by car, take these routes: East: To come from Varanasi, you can reach Vindhyachal via NH-19 (old GT Road) through Aurai and by crossing the Shastri Bridge (over the River Ganges). You can also come directly via the Varanasi-Mirzapur route (Kachhwa Road). West: The most direct route from Prayagraj is NH-135 (Prayagraj-Mirzapur Highway), which connects to Vindhyachal via Naini, Meja, and Manda. Another option is coming via Handia-Gopiganj from NH-19. North: Passengers coming from Jaunpur and Bhadohi can reach Vindhyachal via Aurai directly through the Shastri Bridge route. South: Devotees coming from Rewa or the Madhya Pradesh border can arrive directly at Vindhyachal via NH-135 (Drummondganj route) or through Lalganj. By Air: The nearest airport is Lal Bahadur Shastri International Airport, Varanasi (Babatpur), which is approximately 75–80 km away from Vindhyachal. From there, Vindhyachal can be reached by taxi or bus. After reaching Vindhyachal Dham, separate parking arrangements are available for parking buses and cars. After parking your vehicle here, you can begin your 'Trikon Yatra'. Near the temple lies 'Pakka Ghat', the most prominent and famous ghat where devotees take a holy dip. You, too, should begin your pilgrimage with a bath in the Ganges. After that, proceed for the darshan of Maa Vindhyavasini. Thanks to the recently constructed grand Vindhya Corridor, reaching the temple directly from the Ganges ghat has become extremely convenient. This temple is considered a 'Siddhapeeth' rather than just a Shaktipeeth. It is believed that the Goddess herself resides here in person. Entry into the sanctum sanctorum remains closed during peak crowd hours on Navratri or regular days, and darshan is allowed only through the viewing window (Jhankhi). In the temple, the Mother Goddess is adorned in different forms (Shringar) and worshipped with Aarti four times a day. Temple priest Ashish Pandey explains—arriving during the morning Mangala Aarti is the best time for darshan. The doors for darshan remain closed for about 30–45 minutes during the afternoon Shringar Aarti and the main night Aarti. Immediately after offering prayers to Maa Vindhyavasini, step out of the temple premises and visit the Kaal Bhairav Temple located near Kotwali. According to beliefs, visiting Kaal Bhairav after the Vindhyavasini Temple is mandatory. The unique aspect of this temple is that Bhairav and Bhairavi are enshrined together here. Reach the Ashtabhuji Devi Temple, situated on the hills about 3 kilometres away from the Vindhyachal Temple. This is the second major stop of the Trikon Yatra. Ashtabhuji Devi is considered an incarnation of Goddess Saraswati and Yogamaya. Devotees can climb 108 steps to reach this hilltop temple for darshan. A ropeway facility is also available for elderly and infirm devotees. According to the Shrimad Bhagavata Mahapurana, when Kansa attempted to dash the newborn baby girl of Yashoda against a stone, mistaking her for the 8th child of Devaki and Vasudeva, the child suddenly slipped from his hands and flew into the sky. She made a celestial announcement saying, 'The one who will kill you has already been born in Gokul.' Following this, Yogamaya vanished upon reaching this very Ashtabhuji hill. During Navratri, the temple remains open 24 hours for darshan. The doors are closed for a short duration at night for special rituals and cleaning. During the Trikon Yatra, the best time to visit the Ashtabhuji temple is between 6:00 AM and 11:00 AM, or after 4:30 PM in the evening. After seeking blessings at the Ashtabhuji Devi Temple, visiting the nearby Batuk Bhairav Temple is also considered auspicious. Proceed further from the Ashtabhuji Temple to reach Kali Khoh, which is the final and third main stop of the Trikon Yatra. The Kali Khoh Temple is located about 3 kilometres from the Vindhyachal Temple and approximately 2 kilometres away from the Ashtabhuji Temple, nestled in the hills. Here, the Goddess is worshipped in her Mahakali form. This site is world-famous for Tantric rituals and special worship of Mahakali. Devotees who perform sattvic worship offer symbolic sacrifices of lemons and nutmegs along with coconuts to appease the Mother Goddess. After seeking the blessings of Maa Mahakali, it is considered mandatory to visit Anand Bhairav (Lal Bhairav) located within the temple complex. Seeking the darshan of Anand Bhairav completes your holy 'Trikon Yatra'.

stories.title: Livestock recruitment scam:Minister’s signatures on files, arrest likely; rules changed for arbitrary appointments, EOW awaits govt’s signal
stories.summary: Raj Kishor Singh, who served as the Animal Husbandry Minister during the Samajwadi Party (SP) government, may face arrest. On October 14, the Economic Offences Wing (EOW) arrested retired Principal Secretary Yogesh Kumar. The case pertains to the 2014 recruitment for 1,198 posts of Livestock Extension Officers. At that time, Raj Kishor Singh was the minister, while Yogesh Kumar served as the Principal Secretary in the department. The EOW has been investigating this scam since December 2017. In 2022, permission was sought from the government to prosecute the former minister and the principal secretary. While sanction was granted for Yogesh Kumar, the EOW has yet to receive any indication regarding former minister Raj Kishor Singh. Under these circumstances, the EOW is awaiting a signal from the government. Read the full report to find out how the former Samajwadi party minister got entangled in the scam… DG EOW Jai Narayan Singh told Dainik Bhaskar that the Animal Husbandry Department had initiated the recruitment process for 1,198 posts of Livestock Extension Officers across 17 divisions of the state. For this, a written examination was conducted on 2 February 2014. Irregularities in the recruitment examination occurred at three levels. Let us understand this: 1. Recruitment for the post of Livestock Extension Officer was to be conducted at the divisional level by an officer of Additional Director Grade-2 rank. However, without government permission, rules were altered to strip divisional selection committees of their authority. 2. After approval at the ministerial level, the examination process was centralised after its conduct. This meant recruitment started at the divisional level but was completed at the state headquarters level. A file was moved for this, bearing signatures from the bottom up—including the Deputy Director, Additional Director, Director, and Principal Secretary, along with the then-minister Raj Kishor Singh. 3. Changes to the rules were made without obtaining permission from the government. The written examination was conducted for 80 marks instead of 100, reserving 20 marks for the interview. Subsequently, evaluation of the OMR sheets was not carried out according to the rules, and they were tampered with at the headquarters level. Evaluation Done at Raebareli Institute, Arbitrary Marks Awarded DG EOW Jai Narayan Singh explains: To evaluate the answer sheets (OMR sheets) of the recruitment exam, officials fabricated two excuses. First—a shortage of funds. Second—difficulty in evaluating answer sheets at every district or divisional level. Citing these reasons, they altered the rules. Instead of having the answer sheets evaluated fairly at different locations, all answer sheets were handed over to the 'Feroze Gandhi Institute'. It is also alleged that prescribed rules were not followed while assigning the task to the institute, and contracts were backdated. The investigating agency also suspected that arbitrary selections were made through manipulation during evaluation and scoring. The DG EOW stated that owing to the case being old, the entire recruitment process was not cancelled. Consequently, individuals who secured jobs through foul play are still working. The government's stance regarding them remains unclear. Rajkishore in BJP, Hence Permission for Case Withheld The EOW has gathered evidence against Raj Kishor. Permission was subsequently sought from the government to prosecute both individuals. Recently, the government granted approval against Yogesh Kumar, but Raj Kishor's case was kept pending. Had the government granted permission to proceed with the case, Raj Kishor would also have been arrested. Departmental sources state: 'Raj Kishor is currently with the BJP.' After the SP government fell in the 2017 elections, he joined the Congress just ahead of the 2019 Lok Sabha elections. During this period, he contested the election from Harraiya but lost. In 2024, Raj Kishor left the Congress and joined the BJP. He has not been given any post in the organisation, but he is preparing to contest elections once again. Action Before Assembly Elections: What Will Be the Political Advantage? The recruitment took place during the tenure of the Samajwadi Party government. The Yogi government has consistently alleged irregularities and favoritism towards a specific group in recruitments held under the Akhilesh government. Coming ahead of the elections, these arrests naturally put the SP and Akhilesh Yadav on the back foot, which could give the BJP political leverage. However, since Raj Kishor Singh is currently with the BJP, if permission to prosecute him is withheld despite the presence of evidence, it will raise questions about the government as well.

stories.title: Crocodile devours boy alive in UP:Drags him into the Ganga by jaws, leaving no trace of his nose, ears or mouth
stories.summary: A 16-year-old boy bathing in the Ganga in Bulandshahr was mauled to death by a crocodile. He had gone back into the water because he insisted on taking one more dip. The crocodile dragged him into the river. It did not spare the boy's ear, nose or mouth. He was found trapped in the river barricading. After receiving information about the incident, the police and the boy's family took him to hospital, where doctors declared him dead. Anupshahr Sub-Divisional Magistrate Manish Kumar also reached the hospital and questioned Forest Department officials. The incident took place at 1 p.m. in the Ahar area. Two photographs related to the incident... The family finished bathing and came out; son went back into the river Mukesh Kumar lives with his family in the Ramgarhi locality of the Jahangirabad Kotwali area. He had come to bathe at the Avantika Devi Ganga Ghat with his 16-year-old son Anuj and other family members on Wednesday morning. The family members came out after bathing, but Anuj got back into the Ganga and began bathing again. The family did not notice. Meanwhile, a crocodile emerged from the water and dragged Anuj into the river. About half an hour later, Anuj was found clinging to the barricading in a seriously injured condition. Anuj was the only brother among three sisters After seeing Anuj hanging in the barricading, people nearby also reached the spot. With their help, his family members pulled Anuj out of the water. He was taken to Anupshahr CHC for treatment, where doctors declared him dead. Anuj was the only brother of three sisters. His mother and sisters are inconsolable after his death. Anupshahr Sub-Divisional Magistrate Manish Kumar and Tehsildar Priya Devi reached the hospital. Anuj's uncle Mahendra said, "A jagran was held at our home at night. After that, around 40 people travelled by tractor-trolley to Avantika Devi Ganga Ghat to bathe. Everyone had finished bathing and come out. Then Anuj said, 'Uncle, I am going for one more dip.' Around half an hour later, Anuj was found trapped near the barricading installed in the Ganga." SDM Manish Kumar said, "An aquatic animal attacked the boy. Forest Department officials have been instructed to investigate the matter." CO Shashank Srivastava said, "The boy was bathing inside the barricaded area." The body has been sent for a post-mortem examination. An investigation is under way. The Forest Department team is also looking into the matter.

stories.summary: The Allahabad High Court has ordered that panchayat elections be held in Uttar Pradesh within three months. However, the court has upheld the validity of the government order under which the administrators were appointed. This means the administrators will remain in office for the next three months. Earlier, during a hearing on 5 August, the Lucknow Bench of the High Court had said: The state government is bound to conduct panchayat elections within six months. This period will end in November 2026. The question now is: Is it possible to hold panchayat elections within three months? Could the assembly elections be postponed in such a situation? We will find out in today's UP Explainer... Question 1: Why were the panchayat elections not held on time? Did the government do this deliberately? Answer: The terms of gram panchayats, kshetra panchayats and zila panchayats in UP were ending in May. However, instead of holding elections before then, the heads of the panchayats themselves were appointed as administrators. The UP government cited two administrative reasons for this before the Allahabad High Court... 1. The State Election Commission published the final electoral roll for the panchayat elections on 10 June, so the elections could not be held as scheduled. 2. The reservation system for the panchayat elections is determined on the basis of the report of the commission formed for the reservation of seats for the Other Backward Classes. It will take around six months for the report to be submitted. Political analysts, however, cite three reasons for this... 1. Risk of the BJP suffering losses in the Assembly elections 2. Risk of a split in the BJP alliance 3. Risk of factionalism at the grassroots level Question 2: What is the current status of the panchayat elections? Answer: Question 3: So, could the panchayat elections be held before the 2027 Assembly elections by postponing the latter? Answer: No... stories.title: UP High Court orders panchayat polls within three months:Will Assembly elections be postponed?
stories.summary: The Allahabad High Court has ordered panchayat elections in Uttar Pradesh to be held within three months. It also dismissed petitions challenging the decision to appoint outgoing village heads as administrators, which alleged that the move was illegal. In its verdict on Wednesday, the court said the current village heads would continue as administrators until the elections are held. This means they will remain in the role for the next three months. A division bench of Justice Ajit Kumar and Justice Garima Prasad delivered the verdict after a three-hour hearing. The court directed the state government to complete elections to all panchayati raj bodies within three months. It ruled that the government order under which administrators were appointed was entirely valid. The court said the OBC Commission would continue its work without any hindrance, but the election process would not depend on the commission’s work. Elections will be held under the existing rules and framework, with the provision for 27% reservation being followed. The High Court’s order has raised the question of whether the Uttar Pradesh Assembly elections will now be held after the panchayat elections. Panchayati Raj Minister Om Prakash Rajbhar welcomed the High Court’s verdict, but said the government had the option of approaching the Supreme Court. What options does the government have after the court’s order? 1. It can challenge the verdict in the Supreme Court If the government believes it is not possible to conduct elections within three months, it can challenge the High Court’s order in the Supreme Court by filing a Special Leave Petition (SLP). The government can ask the Supreme Court to stay the High Court’s order or grant additional time to conduct the elections. It may cite issues such as a shortage of security personnel, the triple-test process for OBC reservation or the voter list not being ready. However, the Supreme Court will decide whether to extend the deadline based on the facts and applicable legal provisions. 2. It can also seek an extension from the High Court Instead of approaching the Supreme Court, the government can apply to the High Court for an extension. It can seek a modification of the order or file a review petition. The government may request that the three-month deadline be extended to four to six months. It may cite difficulties arising from preparations for the Assembly elections, the deployment of security personnel and board examinations. However, whether these grounds justify an extension will depend on the court’s decision. Petitioners say government and Election Commission must hold polls within 3 months Lead petitioner Imtiaz Hussain said several petitions had been filed before the Lucknow Bench challenging the appointment of administrators. These were also clubbed with their petition before the Allahabad High Court. However, the court dismissed those petitions today. The High Court has now set a deadline, but it remains to be seen whether the elections can be held within three months. Panchayat election petitioner Rai Sahab Yadav said the government had argued that the commission’s report was not yet complete and that it was therefore not ready to conduct the elections. The government had also failed to complete the process of revising the reservation system. The court has directed that a decision on reservation be taken within six months and that panchayat elections be held within three months. Now understand the full case - Lead petitioner and lawyer Imtiaz Hussain had asked the court to direct the State Election Commission to issue a detailed schedule for completing the entire panchayat election process within a fixed timeframe, before the current panchayats’ terms ended. - The petition stated that the panchayat elections should have been held by 26 May 2026 or earlier. The High Court had sought an affidavit from the State Election Commission, asking whether it was in a position to conduct the elections in accordance with Article 243E of the Indian Constitution and why the polls could not be held within the stipulated timeframe. - The court said the State Election Commission was expected to finalise the complete election schedule and place it on record before the date of the next hearing. - Petitioner Imtiaz Hussain argued that, under Article 243E of the Constitution, a panchayat’s term cannot exceed five years from the date of its first meeting. Therefore, elections must be held on time. - The State Election Commission argued that, under Section 12-BB of the Uttar Pradesh Panchayat Raj Act, 1947, it is the state government’s responsibility to issue a notification specifying the date for general or by-elections for the post of village head. The notification is issued in consultation with the State Election Commission. High Court reprimanded the OBC Commission During the hearing on 9 October, the High Court expressed displeasure and dissatisfaction with the OBC Commission’s report. It said it appeared that the commission had prepared the report while sitting in its office rather than conducting field visits. The High Court also questioned the process of collecting data for OBC reservation. It noted that Agra district has an OBC population of more than 3 lakh, yet only 179 people approached the commission despite newspaper s. Statements were recorded from just 29 people.

stories.title: Complaint to PMO over missing gold at Kashi Vishwanath:Temple denies it, says 'Kalash' broke due to monkeys jumping around
stories.summary: Gold has reportedly gone missing from the golden pinnacle of the Kashi Vishwanath Temple. Lawyer Nityanand Rai has filed a complaint with the Prime Minister's Office (PMO). S. Rajalingam, chairman of the temple executive committee and Varanasi commissioner, rejected the allegation. He said a small golden finial had fallen during monkeys' jumping and scrambling. On the instructions of the Chief Minister's Office, the temple administration is also conducting an internal inquiry into the matter. IIT Madras has been contacted to assess the strength of the golden pinnacle and carry out repairs. The finial will be reinstalled after its report and assessment. Golden finials went missing from 2 places Advocate Nityanand Rai, a resident of Teliyabag, sent a complaint to the Prime Minister's Office and the Chief Minister's Office through the divisional commissioner on 29 September. He has claimed that gold finials have gone missing from two spots above the temple's northern gate. According to Nityanand Rai, he sought information from the temple administration about the missing gold, but received no response. He also said that the temple's website contains no information about gold being removed from the golden spire. The complaint also raised concerns that small gold patches fitted to other parts of the spire may have gone missing. Referring to claims that the gold plating has become loose in some places, it warned that it could fall. Lawyer says details of temple's gold and silver should be made public In his complaint, Nityanand Rai referred to previous incidents of gold and silver theft at the temple. Along with demanding an investigation, he called for a detailed account of the use of gold and silver on the temple premises to be made public. The complainant said that a white paper should be issued on the matter and its details made available on the temple's official website. He said this would bring clarity about the condition of the golden spire and the security of the metals. Now read what the administration said in the report The temple administration said in the report that a golden finial installed above the northern gate had fallen in recent days as monkeys jumped around it. It has been kept safe in the storeroom. Reinstalling the finial without a technical examination would not be appropriate. For this reason, the administration contacted IIT Madras. The institute's team has conducted a preliminary survey of the golden spire and recommended that the entire spire be repaired. Commissioner says-Part of finial fell, gold completely safe Divisional Commissioner S. Rajalingam said, "The information that gold has gone missing from the temple's golden spire is incorrect. Around three months ago, during a hailstorm, part of the finial built over the temple entrance fell. The temple administration has kept it safe." IIT Madras has been given the responsibility of assessing the structural strength of the spire. Payment for this has also been made. The institute's team will visit the temple at the end of October. Repair work will be carried out after the report is received.

stories.title: Mayawati seeks contractual staff inclusion in 1 lakh government jobs:Urges regularisation of NRHM workers serving for years
stories.summary: Amid the announcement that one lakh government jobs will be provided in Uttar Pradesh over the next six months, BSP supremo Mayawati has demanded the regularisation of NRHM contractual workers. She said the government should consider giving permanent jobs alongside making new recruitments to employees who have been working temporarily in government departments for years. Mayawati said the BSP was opposed to the system of appointments through outsourcing and contractual employment in the government machinery. The party has demanded that all contractual workers who have been continuously serving under the National Health Mission (NRHM) for a long time be regularised in the Health Department. Contractual workers staging a sit-in at Eco Garden Mayawati said that NRHM contractual workers had been staging a protest near Manyavar Shri Kanshi Ram Ji Eco Garden in Lucknow for the past several days over their demands, including regularisation. She appealed to the government to consider the workers' demands. The BSP supremo's statement has brought the issue of regularising employees who have been working on contract for a long time, alongside government recruitment, back into focus.

stories.summary: Three rebel Samajwadi Party MLAs — Rakesh Pratap Singh, Abhay Singh and Vinod Chaturvedi — have joined the BJP. At a membership ceremony held in Amethi, all three dialled the BJP’s toll-free number to become primary members of the party. State president Pankaj Chaudhary then welcomed the three MLAs by draping them with party scarves in the presence of national general secretary Smriti Irani. Targeting the Congress, Smriti Irani said, “You can bring together as many parties as you want and try to turn your prince into an emperor, but the truth about Uttar Pradesh is that the Congress has lost nine consecutive Assembly elections. Amethi bears witness to the fact that if that family of the Congress cannot contest elections in this region on its own, how can it lead the nation on its own?” After joining the BJP, Abhay Singh said he was hurt by the Samajwadi Party’s failure to protest when the Ramcharitmanas was burnt, which led him to decide to leave the party. Rakesh Pratap Singh said: “I have not joined the BJP to become an MLA; I have joined to help make others BJP MLAs.” All three MLAs had won the 2022 Assembly elections on Samajwadi Party tickets. However, during the Rajya Sabha elections in February 2024, they cross-voted in favour of the BJP candidate, going against their party line. See the pictures… 7 SP MLAs rebelled during Rajya Sabha elections In February 2024, seven Samajwadi Party MLAs — Manoj Pandey, Pooja Pal, Rakesh Pratap Singh, Abhay Singh, Vinod Chaturvedi, Rakesh Pandey and Ashutosh Maurya — rebelled during the Rajya Sabha elections. All seven had won the 2022 Assembly elections on SP tickets but defied the party line and cross-voted in favour of BJP candidates.

stories.title: UP Police Constable recruitment results out:Merit list released for 32,679 posts; check cut-off marks
stories.summary: The final results for the UP Police Constable Recruitment 2025 have been declared. The merit list of candidates who cleared the written examination, physical test, medical examination and document verification has also been released. A total of 6,685 candidates from the General category, 18,210 from the OBC category, 7,136 from the SC category and 648 from the ST category have qualified. Of these, 4,481 are women. The Uttar Pradesh Police Recruitment and Promotion Board (UPPRPB) also released category-wise cut-off marks on Wednesday. Candidates have been selected based on their normalised marks and the preferences they submitted. Those who participated in the recruitment process can check their results and cut-off marks on the board’s official website. The recruitment process, announced on 31 December 2025, was conducted to fill a total of 32,679 vacant posts. The written examination was held on 8, 9 and 10 June 2026 across all 75 districts of Uttar Pradesh. A total of 28.86 lakh candidates applied for the examination, including 19.62 lakh men and 9.24 lakh women. Around 21.92 lakh candidates appeared for the written examination. Police Constable Recruitment 2025 Result How to check the result on the website 1. Constable Civil Police (Male/Female) – 10,469 Posts 2. Constable PAC / Armed Police (Male) – 15,131 Posts 3. Constable Special Security Force (Male) – 1,341 Posts 4. Female Battalion (Lucknow, Badaun, Gorakhpur) – 2,282 Posts 5. Constable Mounted Police (Male) – 71 Posts 6. Jail Warder (Male) 3,279 Posts 7. Jail Warder (Female) 106 Posts Understand the entire recruitment process 1. On 31 December 2025, the Yogi government issued a notification for direct recruitment to 32,679 posts. These included positions in the Civil Police, Provincial Armed Constabulary (PAC), Special Security Force (SSF), women’s battalions, mounted police and jail warders. 2. A total of 10,469 posts were advertised for male and female candidates in the Civil Police. The recruitment also included 15,131 posts for men in the PAC and 1,341 vacancies for male candidates in the UP SSF. 3. The written examination was conducted over three days in six shifts. Since the examination took place in different shifts, marks were normalised. The merit list was prepared based on normalised marks and the state’s reservation rules. 4. According to a notice issued on 31 July 2026, around 2.33 times the total number of vacancies—76,184 candidates—were called for the next stage. Document Verification (DV) and the Physical Standard Test (PST) were completed between 17 and 31 August. 5. Candidates who cleared the DV/PST underwent the Physical Efficiency Test (running). The test was qualifying in nature, with candidates marked only as pass or fail; no separate marks were awarded. It was conducted between 1 and 11 October 2026. 6. Final selection does not guarantee joining immediately. Appointment will be confirmed only after certain mandatory checks. The department will conduct medical examinations, which candidates must pass. Documents will be verified again, and character and police records will also be checked.

stories.title: Shiva and Shraddha’s chats surface:Model allegedly warned ‘Something bad will happen to you’; changed phone numbers 4 times
stories.summary: Wanted model Shraddha Dubey remains out of police reach five days after the murder of 28-year-old businessman Shiva Sharma in Lucknow. Meanwhile, chats between Shiva and Shraddha have emerged. In them, Shraddha had told Shiva, "Something bad will happen to you." Meanwhile, police have intensified the search for Shraddha. Her location was traced to Nepal. A police team has been sent there. The investigation so far has revealed that Shraddha had been made a VVIP guest at Lucknow's biggest Dandiya festival, which begins on 16 October. The investigation has also revealed that Shraddha used to change her mobile number after achieving her blackmailing target. She had changed four numbers so far. Shiva's family, meanwhile, has alleged that the accused have not been arrested because of their influence. Shiva's mother, Ranjana, said the accused must be arrested first. She said nothing would be acceptable to them without this. "We are in constant contact with the police. We are co-operating with the investigation." Earlier, on Tuesday, a reward of ₹25,000 each had been announced for information leading to the arrest of Shraddha Dubey, her sister Rashmi Dubey and driver Tanveer Ali alias Danish. See 3 pictures... On Snapchat, Shraddha told Shiva, ‘A heartfelt curse’; read it verbatim Shraddha: Seriously, I curse you from the bottom of my heart. Just as you used me and changed your behaviour... I hope something happens to you that leaves you incapable of using anyone. You used to keep pestering me by calling repeatedly. What has happened now? Have you got cancer or are you about to die? Shiva: Look, my behaviour hasn't changed, and my love hasn't diminished either. Shraddha: Just see, Shiva, the more irritated I am becoming... Shiva: It's just that I'm dealing with some problem. Shraddha: Something really bad will happen to you. Shiva: It's just that I'm dealing with some problem. Shraddha: What problem are you dealing with? (The chat ends here.) MLA had described Shraddha as his niece According to sources, in January 2026, Shraddha accused her driver, Imran, of molesting her at Hazratganj police station in Lucknow. The police also registered a case under sections related to molestation and other offences. During this period, an MLA from Prayagraj district spoke up for Shraddha, describing her as his niece. Audio of girl threatening him surfaces An audio recording of Shiva and Shraddha has also surfaced. However, Dainik Bhaskar has not verified it. In it, the girl objects to the boy being with his friends. She says, "You want to go around having fun, but you do not want to earn money. I turn everyone down." During the conversation, the girl accuses him of theft. The boy says, "Please do not accuse me of theft." As they discuss partying, the girl threatens the boy, saying, "You are triggering me. I will write your full name and send it to Sanjay sir." The audio ends after this. It is being claimed that the girl's voice is Shraddha's and the boy's voice is Shiva's. Now read what the entire case is about... On 9 October, Shiva Sharma died after falling from the fourth floor of Awadh Green Apartment in Hazratganj, Lucknow. Shiva had been living with Shraddha in a live-in relationship for the past four months. After the incident, he was wearing only underwear. There was lipstick on his face. Several cigarette-burn marks were also found on his body. Shiva's mother, Ranjana Sharma, has filed a murder case over his death against five people, including Shraddha, her sister Rashmi and their driver Adil. It is alleged that Shraddha pushed Shiva from the fourth floor. Hazratganj police station in-charge Vikram Singh said, "Police teams have been deployed. The accused will be arrested soon."

stories.title: Another FIR against Azam Khan:ED files fraud and corruption case after questioning him in jail for eight hours
stories.summary: Another FIR has been registered against Samajwadi Party leader Azam Khan. The Enforcement Directorate (ED) has had the FIR registered over financial irregularities linked to the Jauhar Trust and Mohammad Ali Jauhar University. The FIR was registered at the Azeem Nagar police station in Rampur by Piyush S. Throt, the deputy director posted at the ED's Lucknow office. The Azeem Nagar station house officer said the FIR contains allegations of misuse of official position, fraud and large-scale corruption. Besides SP leader Azam, who is lodged in Rampur jail, it names the Jauhar Ali Trust, two companies involved in the construction of buildings at Jauhar University-SSS Enterprises and SK Chike Pvt. Ltd.-and one unidentified person, taking the total to five accused. Earlier, an ED team of three officers that arrived from Lucknow questioned Azam for around 8 hours on Tuesday in barrack No. 1 of the jail. The ED has obtained permission from the PMLA (Prevention of Money Laundering Act) court in Lucknow to question Azam for four days. The questioning will continue until 16 October. According to sources, on the first day, Azam was questioned about irregularities at Jauhar University and the Maulana Mohammad Ali Jauhar Trust. He was asked where the donations had come from. Azam Khan initially kept citing illness as an excuse. Later, he answered some of the questions. 3 officers arrived from Lucknow and went straight to Azam's barrack Azam showed ₹78 crore but spent ₹494 crore SP Anil Singh Sisodia said, "CO Tanda Pankaj Pant will investigate the case registered against Azam Khan." According to the SP, the FIR alleges that government contracts for the construction of Jauhar University were awarded to favoured companies by understating the actual construction cost. These people showed an expenditure of ₹78 crore on the construction of Jauhar University in the name of the Jauhar Ali Trust, while the investigation revealed that ₹494 crore had been spent. The FIR stated that Jauhar University is Azam's dream project. Most members of the Jauhar University Trust are also his close associates and family members, including his wife, Tanzeen Fatima, his son and his sister. Over the past two weeks, the Enforcement Directorate (ED) summoned Samajwadi Party MLA Naseer Khan, Azam's son's friend Anwar Salim and others to Lucknow and recorded their statements. It was only after these statements that Azam Khan was questioned in jail. The case was registered only after satisfactory answers were not received. SP MLA was questioned in October On 6 October, the ED questioned Naseer Ahmad Khan, the SP MLA from Rampur's Chamraua Assembly constituency, for seven hours. Naseer has previously served as the joint secretary of the Jauhar Trust. The ED summoned the SP MLA to Lucknow for questioning. During the interrogation, he was questioned about decisions taken in the trust, donations and his role in the construction work at Jauhar University. Raids were conducted at 10 locations in August On 19 August, the Enforcement Directorate raided 10 locations in Rampur, Saharanpur and Delhi linked to the Jauhar Trust, the university and Azam Khan. During the operation, documents related to financial transactions, donations and construction work were examined. The agency then questioned people connected with the case and took the investigation forward. Know about Azam's Jauhar University and its controversy

stories.title: 'Avnish was forcing Samreen to marry him':Mother demands justice from CM Yogi; daughter died after falling from Lucknow hotel
stories.summary: The family of Samreen, who died after falling from the 10th floor of a hotel in Lucknow, has alleged that Avnish Jaiswal had been pressuring her to marry him for the past four months. Her family has accused him of murder and demanded justice. Samreen's mother, Sufia Bano, made an emotional appeal to Uttar Pradesh Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath, saying, “Yogi ji, if it were someone else, a bulldozer would have been sent by now. Please protect a mother's dignity and deliver justice. We want that boy's blood.” Bano said she had been widowed for 16 years and had raised her seven children on her own. She alleged that the man killed her daughter after she said something unpleasant to him. “If he loved my daughter so much, he could have married her. What had my daughter done to him that he took her life?” she asked. The allegations are yet to be established, and the case is under investigation. Avnish had Samreen's name written on his palm According to details shared by the family, Avnish had written Samreen's name on his palm with a heart symbol and had applied mehendi bearing her name. He had also allegedly created an Instagram account named ‘Deer’ to communicate with her, while Samreen reportedly used an account named ‘Alpha’. Their friendship had developed through Instagram. A photograph that has surfaced shows the two with half-heart symbols drawn on their palms, which together form a complete heart. See three pictures... Samreen's phone switched off after she was asked to share location According to the family, Samreen's elder sister, Sheeba, and a friend contacted her at around 3 pm. Samreen was reportedly frightened and told her sister that the man, whom she knew as Dev, was not letting her leave. She asked for help booking a Rapido cab, following which her sister asked her to share her location. However, Samreen's phone was switched off shortly afterwards, and the family could not contact her again. The family said they learnt about the incident at around 10.30 pm. They also said Samreen rarely travelled alone more than one or two kilometres from home, raising questions about how she ended up at the hotel. Family alleges threats over marriage According to her family, Samreen had left home with Sheeba to visit a market nearby. After they had travelled around a kilometre, Samreen went to speak to Avnish for what the family described as their final conversation. She reportedly wanted to tell him that a relationship between them was not possible, after which her elder sister left for work. The family alleged that Avnish, who introduced himself as Dev, had been harassing Samreen for four months and pressuring her to marry him. They said the family was unwilling to agree to the marriage because the two belonged to different religions. The family further alleged that he repeatedly threatened to visit their home if Samreen refused to marry him. Police officials said three teams had been formed to investigate the case and trace the accused. The police have also detained some of the accused's associates for questioning.

stories.title: "Is hoisting Tricolour and chanting ‘Bharat Mata Ki Jai’ crime?":Sanjay Singh hits out over Saurabh Das and Ashutosh Ranka’s arrests
stories.summary: Extending his support to the youth-led Cockroach Janta Party (CJP), Aam Aadmi Party (AAP) Rajya Sabha MP Sanjay Singh questioned whether hoisting the Tricolour and raising the slogan ‘Bharat Mata Ki Jai’ had become crimes in India. In a video posted on X, Singh questioned Prime Minister Narendra Modi over the arrests of Saurabh Das and Ashutosh Ranka in connection with the flag-hoisting incident. He accused the government of trying to suppress the voices of young people and warned that confronting the country's youth would prove costly for the government. Singh said Das, Ranka and their associates had brought pride to the country by hoisting the Tricolour and raising ‘Bharat Mata Ki Jai’ slogans at Jantar Mantar. He claimed that the two had been sent to jail for five days in connection with the incident. Singh asserted that young people would continue to hoist the national flag and raise ‘Bharat Mata Ki Jai’ slogans. Sanjay Singh targets RSS over Tricolour The AAP MP also targeted the Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh (RSS), alleging that the organisation had not hoisted the national flag at its Nagpur headquarters for 52 years. Singh said the government might have a problem with the Tricolour being hoisted and slogans of ‘Bharat Mata Ki Jai’ being raised, but young people would continue to do both. Accuses Modi government of weakening democracy Singh also accused the PM Modi-led centre government of weakening democracy and coming to power through the alleged buying and selling of governments, MLAs and MPs. He claimed that the government's authoritarian rule was nearing its end and said attempts to silence young people would face a response. Calling the arrests of Das and Ranka a major mistake by the government, Singh said the Prime Minister would soon realise the consequences. He concluded his statement with the slogans ‘Jai Hind’, ‘Inquilab Zindabad’ and ‘Bharat Mata Ki Jai’.

stories.title: CHO protest continues in Lucknow:Health workers reach minister’s residence, demand direct talks with him
stories.summary: The protest by Community Health Officers (CHOs) continued in Lucknow on Wednesday, with demonstrators reaching the residence of Deputy Chief Minister and Health Minister Brajesh Pathak to demand direct talks with the government. The protesters alleged that the government had not taken any concrete decision on their demands or service-related issues. During the demonstration, police attempted to put the CHOs on buses and take them to Eco Garden. The CHOs are seeking a direct meeting with the government to find a permanent solution to their grievances. What are the CHOs demanding? Their key demands include regularisation of services, the issuance of permanent appointment letters, the inclusion of Performance-Based Incentives (PBI) in regular salaries, and implementation of a Grade Pay of 4,800. The CHOs said they play an important role in delivering healthcare services in rural areas, but their service-related concerns remain unresolved. They urged the government to consider their demands seriously and take a decision soon.

stories.title: 50,000 NHM workers from 75 districts gather in Lucknow:Posters target Ambani and Adani as protesters demand permanent jobs
stories.summary: More than 50,000 National Health Mission (NHM) workers from all 75 districts of Uttar Pradesh gathered at Eco Garden in Lucknow on Wednesday, demanding permanent jobs instead of contractual employment. The protesters carried posters and banners with slogans, including one targeting industrialists Mukesh Ambani and Gautam Adani. They said they had been working in the state's healthcare system for years but their demands remained unaddressed. The protest began on October 8 and includes Community Health Officers (CHOs), Auxiliary Nurse Midwives (ANMs), nursing officers, doctors and other contractual healthcare staff. The workers said their agitation would continue until their demands were met. See four pictures of the protest... Workers demand equal pay for equal work ANM Neetu Pathak said employees had been protesting since the 21st, but the government had not responded to their demands. She said ANMs were responsible for vaccinating children from birth to the age of 16, creating ABHA and Ayushman Bharat health IDs, and entering information on the e-Kavach portal, among around 32 online tasks. She demanded equal pay for equal work and an end to the contractual employment system. Kunti Singh, an ANM from Hardoi, said contractual workers performed duties similar to those of permanent employees but received significantly lower salaries. She claimed permanent employees received around ₹60,000 a month, while some contractual workers earned only ₹12,000. Atal Bihari, who came from Kushinagar, said some workers had been serving for 15 years or longer. He demanded equal salaries and benefits for employees performing similar duties. Contractual nursing officers highlight salary gap Mohan Lal, a contractual nursing officer from Mirzapur, said contractual staff received around ₹20,000 a month, compared with approximately ₹1 lakh for permanent employees. He said contractual staff worked in outpatient and inpatient departments, emergency wards, intensive care units and tuberculosis wards. They also served during the Covid-19 pandemic but did not receive additional benefits, he claimed. Lal said the protest had affected the admission of tuberculosis patients and delivery services, although emergency services continued. Doctors also seek pay parity Dr Afroz Alam Ansari said he was appointed alongside MBBS doctors in 2009, when both groups had a grade pay of 24. He claimed that MBBS doctors now earned around ₹1 lakh a month, while his salary remained ₹51,375. He said his duties included fieldwork, outpatient services, emergency shifts and responsibilities at sporting events and ministers' programmes. He demanded equal pay for equal work. Dr Nilesh Kumar Jaiswal, an AYUSH doctor posted at a community health centre in Bhadohi, called for regularisation or equal pay. He said he had performed duties during the Covid-19 pandemic but received neither an incentive nor a certificate of appreciation. Workers say low salaries make it difficult to support families Ashok Kumar Pandey, a contractual district general secretary of the JNHM-NHM association from Gorakhpur, said contractual MBBS doctors earned ₹40,000–₹45,000 a month, compared with ₹1.5 lakh–₹2 lakh for permanent doctors. He cited similar salary gaps among other categories of healthcare workers and said monthly earnings of ₹10,000–₹25,000 made it difficult for many employees to support their families, particularly when they also had to pay rent and commuting costs. The protesters said they would continue the sit-in and boycott of work until their association issued further instructions.

stories.title: Retired IAS officer Yogesh Kumar arrested in Lucknow:Action in recruitment scam involving 1,198 Livestock Department posts; recruitment took place in 2014
stories.summary: Retired IAS officer Yogesh Kumar has been arrested by the Economic Offences Wing (EOW) in connection with alleged irregularities in the recruitment of 1,198 Livestock Extension Officers in Uttar Pradesh in 2014. Kumar was arrested from Gomti Nagar in Lucknow after investigators found evidence allegedly linking him to the irregularities, EOW Director General JN Singh said. Further legal proceedings are under way. The recruitment process began during the Samajwadi Party government led by Akhilesh Yadav. An examination for the 1,198 posts was held on February 2, 2014. Allegations of large-scale irregularities emerged during the selection process. At the time of recruitment, Yogesh Kumar, an officer of the 1980 batch, was the Principal Secretary of the department. What did the investigation reveal? According to the investigation, recruitment rules were allegedly bypassed. The OMR answer sheets were evaluated at a single location, which investigators suspected could have allowed marks to be manipulated. The powers of committees responsible for selection at the district and divisional levels were also withdrawn, according to the report. Why was Yogesh Kumar arrested? Kumar was the Principal Secretary of the Animal Husbandry Department when the recruitment took place. The investigating agency said it had found evidence linking him to the alleged irregularities. Who was the minister at the time? Raj Kishore Singh was the Animal Husbandry Minister when the recruitment process took place. He was removed from the ministerial post in 2016 and joined the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) in 2024. According to the report, a file concerning possible legal action against Singh was awaiting government approval. No conclusion about his legal liability can be drawn from this alone.

stories.title: Controversy over ‘Muslim women will get 72 men’ remark:Huda lashes out at Maulana, says he must be harassing wives and daughters
stories.summary: YouTuber Huda Jariwala has lashed out at Deobandi clerics in Saharanpur. She said, "Aren't you ashamed? As Muslims, you are defaming your own Muslim sister. Be ashamed. Surely, you must harass your wives, sisters and daughters. Men like you are a disgrace to Islam." Huda made these remarks in a message sent to Maulana Qari Ishaq Gora on Facebook. The Maulana himself posted screenshots of the messages on Facebook on Wednesday. He wrote, "A respected woman's statement on houris has come into the spotlight. We received some messages from an ID bearing her name, asking us to delete the post and warning of legal action." Huda had recently said in an interview that if Muslim men could receive 72 houris in paradise, women would also receive 72 men. Deobandi cleric Qari Ishaq Gora raised questions about this on Tuesday. He said it was necessary to have accurate information before speaking on religious matters. She had said that religion cannot be understood on the basis of one's own thinking or assumptions. If one does not have knowledge of a subject, there should be no harm in acknowledging it. One should avoid making comments without thinking them through. First, find out where the controversy began... Now read the conversation between Huda and the maulana in detail... Huda said, "Allah will never forgive you; He will destroy you" In a message sent to the maulana, Huda Zariwala wrote, "You people disappear when it comes to the martyrdom of mosques. Why do you become frightened then? Which institution are you from? I will inform your boss. You will have to apologise for defaming me. People like you are the height of shamelessness. You are a blot on the name of Islam. Allah will never forgive you; He will destroy you." "I'll deal with you. You have incurred the curse of an orphaned girl. I will make a post against you explaining how you target Muslim women. I will also file a complaint with the police. We will meet in court. I have even had the channel remove the video. You are not deleting the post because you want to use footage from my video for free." Maulana's response-Admit your mistake and apologise to Muslims Responding to Huda's messages, Qari Ishaq Gora said, "If you are threatening me, go ahead and do as you please. You keep saying that your reputation has been damaged, but you are not clearly admitting your mistake. If you really want this video deleted, first admit your mistake, apologise to all Muslims and release a public video doing so." Until you publicly admit your mistake, these threats and talk of filing complaints appear to be merely a way of exerting pressure. Our intention is not to insult anyone, but to bring the truth before everyone. If you have an objection, respond with arguments, not pressure. Who is Huda Jariwala? Find out now Huda Jariwala has been a spokesperson for the Aam Aadmi Party. She has also worked at BBC London. She currently describes herself as a social activist and YouTuber. Huda's maternal uncle, Dr Aziz Qureshi, was a senior Congress leader. He had served as the Governor of Uttarakhand, Uttar Pradesh (additional charge) and Mizoram. During his tenure as Governor, he approved the bill granting minority status to Azam Khan's Jauhar University.

stories.title: Roli helps begging women find work:Started free coaching for 11 children in Varanasi, now teaches 120; rebuilt life after divorce
stories.summary: Children used to go to school, but after school, they would follow in their families' footsteps and turn towards substance abuse and gambling. So, we started providing free evening coaching to these children. Our classes began with 11 children and now have 120. These are the words of Roli Singh Raghuvanshi, a Varanasi resident who has been involved in social work since 2007. She initially worked with women and children who begged on the streets with begging bowls. Today, she works with women as well as children who attend school but struggle with their studies. Roli provides free evening coaching to these children, with her sister, Diksha Singh Raghuvanshi, also helping them with their studies. The two sisters run an organisation called Khula Aasman, which focuses on children's education and women's empowerment. Women associated with the organisation take responsibility for teaching children, preparing food and helping other women find employment. Wanted to move to the US as a child, but changed her mind Roli says her desire to contribute to society began in childhood. Her grandfather belonged to a landowning family, and she believes the values instilled by her family inspired her to work for others. She says people should give back to society what they have received. She once dreamt of moving abroad, obtaining citizenship there, contesting elections and opening an orphanage in India. However, her outlook began to change when she joined Banaras Hindu University (BHU). Seeing young children begging on the streets troubled her. She began wondering how they could be helped to escape their circumstances. Roli visited various institutions and worked with children. Later, she and her sister, Diksha, began visiting settlements and interacting with children and their mothers. Their approach was to build trust with the children first, gradually encouraging their families to support their education and development. It took years to help women move away from begging Roli says persuading women to give up begging and take up work was not easy. She had to visit them repeatedly and explain that they could earn a living through their skills. Khula Aasman now works to train women in tailoring and connect them with employment opportunities. According to Roli, a team of around 10 to 15 women helps run the initiative. Some women stitch clothes, while others assist with cooking and childcare. One woman also drives an electric vehicle. The organisation works with government departments to help women obtain sewing machines. Its team first identifies women in need and then facilitates the process of providing them with machines, enabling them to earn through tailoring from home or independently. Work began near Ravidas Ghat Khula Aasman's work began near Ravidas Ghat in Varanasi. Roli says substance abuse was a concern in the area, and persuading families to send their children to the organisation was initially difficult. The sisters had to repeatedly speak to parents and encourage them to bring their children to the centre. When children did not turn up, they followed up with their guardians. Along with academic coaching, the organisation offers activities such as dance, drama and other creative pursuits to make children feel comfortable and encourage them to participate regularly. Roli and Diksha believe that simply asking children to attend classes is not enough. They also need an environment where they feel safe, welcome and free to explore their interests. Children face challenges at home Roli says every child associated with the organisation has a different story. Several families struggle with domestic violence or substance abuse. In some cases, parents are unwilling to take responsibility for their children, while in others, children are caught between separated parents. Helping these children continue their education while providing a supportive environment is a major challenge. Roli also recounted a serious family dispute involving a girl who reportedly wants to live with her mother. According to Roli, the mother does not want to keep the child and has spoken of selling her to the father for ₹7 lakh. These are allegations shared by Roli based on her experience. They would require independent verification and responses from the relevant parties before publication, particularly given the child's safety and privacy. The organisation provides children with notebooks, pencils and other educational supplies. It also encourages them to participate in activities suited to their interests and needs. Roli believes spending time with children is essential to understanding their circumstances and identifying the support they require. Government school students receive support to pursue their interests Diksha also works closely with the children. She says most of them attend government schools and come to Khula Aasman after classes. Alongside academic support, the organisation encourages children to develop other talents. Some learn cricket, taekwondo and other activities. According to Diksha, some children associated with the organisation have progressed to playing cricket professionally, while others are pursuing undergraduate studies at BHU and Harishchandra College. She says every child has different interests, and the organisation tries to provide opportunities for those who want to develop skills beyond academics. The organisation also attempts to provide the materials and resources children need to pursue their education and extracurricular activities. Roli rebuilt her life after divorce two years ago Roli also spoke about the challenges she faced in her personal life. She says continuing her social work after marriage was difficult, and she remained in the marriage for around five years before deciding that she could no longer continue under those circumstances. She got divorced around two years ago. Roli describes that period as feeling like being trapped in a closed room, unable to see the sky. That experience also influenced the idea behind the name Khula Aasman, which translates to “open sky”. For her, moving forward meant not only rebuilding her own life but also creating opportunities for other women and children. It took years to gain her parents' support Roli says her family took time to accept her work. Her father worked in a bank and initially worried about her working among people who begged and in disadvantaged settlements. According to Roli, it took around 20 years for her family to understand the importance of her work and begin supporting her. Despite these challenges, she continued working with women and children. Today, around 10 to 15 women perform different roles in the organisation, including teaching, cooking and tailoring. One woman also drives an electric rickshaw. Roli wants women to find work suited to their abilities and become financially independent. Working with children helped the organisation reach women Diksha says the sisters initially focused on connecting children with education and extracurricular activities. As the children began attending regularly, their mothers started accompanying them to and from the centre. This created opportunities for the sisters to interact with the women and understand their difficulties. The organisation gradually expanded its work to include women's empowerment and livelihood opportunities. Women now play an active role in teaching children, preparing food and managing other activities at the centre. Roli says financial independence is important, but women also need a supportive environment where they can discuss their problems without hesitation. The sisters hope to help children progress through education and skills while enabling women to earn a living with dignity. What began as a coaching initiative for 11 children now reaches 120, and they plan to continue supporting families who need help.

stories.title: 434 dengue cases reported in Lucknow, hospitals on alert:September saw highest cases; separate wards set up in 4 hospitals, including KGMU
stories.summary: Dengue cases are rising in Lucknow, with 434 people testing positive between January and October 12, according to health department data. September recorded the highest number of cases, with 193 patients testing positive. Another 130 cases were reported in the first 12 days of October. Following the rise in cases, the health department has stepped up precautions. King George’s Medical University (KGMU), Dr Ram Manohar Lohia Institute of Medical Sciences, Balrampur Hospital and Civil Hospital have set up separate wards for dengue patients. Two new cases were reported on Tuesday, with one patient from Chandernagar and the other from Indiranagar. Three children among five dengue patients admitted to Civil Hospital Dr Devesh Chandra Pandey, chief medical superintendent of Shyama Prasad Mukherjee Civil Hospital, said dengue cases had been reported regularly over the past few days. Five dengue patients are currently admitted to the hospital, including three children and two men. Their condition is stable, he said. Two patients were admitted on Tuesday, while three were already undergoing treatment. Patients report pain behind the eyes According to Dr Pandey, patients are experiencing symptoms such as fever, headache, pain behind the eyes and muscle pain. He said patients were getting relief with medication after receiving initial treatment. The hospital has reserved 12 beds for male dengue patients, six beds for female patients and five beds in the children's ward. Mosquito numbers rise after rain and flooding Lucknow Chief Medical Officer Dr NB Singh said waterlogging after the rains had led to an increase in mosquito breeding. Stagnant water in coolers, flower pots and discarded tyres on rooftops can provide breeding grounds for dengue-carrying mosquitoes. Health department teams are conducting fogging operations and checking for mosquito larvae to control their spread. Health department advises against self-medication Dr Singh has urged residents to prevent water from accumulating in and around their homes. He also advised people to wear full-sleeved clothing and use mosquito nets to reduce the risk of mosquito bites. He cautioned people against taking medicines without medical advice if they develop a fever and urged them to visit the nearest health centre for consultation. Month-wise dengue cases in Lucknow According to health department figures, Lucknow recorded 49 dengue cases in August, followed by 193 in September. Another 130 cases were reported between October 1 and 12, taking the reported total to 434 since January 2026.
