stories.title: CM Yogi to visit Varanasi for two days from today:Rally in support of graduate-teacher MLC candidates; reviews air show preparations
stories.summary: Uttar Pradesh Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath will visit Varanasi for two days starting Wednesday. During his visit, he will address a teachers’ and graduates’ convention at Sampurnanand Sanskrit University in support of BJP candidates contesting the Legislative Council elections. He will also hold a review meeting with officials to assess the law and order situation, ongoing development projects and preparations for an upcoming air show in the city. The administration has begun preparations for the Chief Minister’s visit. Yogi Adityanath will also offer prayers at the Baba Kaal Bhairav Temple and Shri Kashi Vishwanath Temple. He is expected to review the progress of development works and discuss security arrangements with officials. Teachers and graduates from eight districts to attend The convention at Sampurnanand Sanskrit University is scheduled to take place in the afternoon. Teachers and graduate voters from eight districts of the Varanasi division are expected to attend. The event is being organised in support of BJP candidates contesting the teachers’ and graduates’ constituencies of the Uttar Pradesh Legislative Council (MLC). Polling for the Varanasi division’s teachers’ and graduates’ MLC seats is scheduled for October 23. The constituencies cover districts in the Varanasi and Mirzapur divisions, as well as Ballia. The Chief Minister’s visit ahead of polling is significant for the party’s campaign. Through the convention, the BJP aims to reach out to voters and seek support for its candidates.

stories.title: All shops in Chatori Gali to remain shut today:Traders angry over entry-point barrier not being removed, say business is suffering
stories.summary: Traders at Chatori Gali, a popular food and shopping spot in Gorakhpur's Golghar area, have announced that all shops will remain closed on Wednesday to protest against the municipal corporation's failure to remove barricades and bollards blocking access to the street. The traders claim that their business has declined by 50-60% over the past one-and-a-half years because the route has remained closed in the name of beautification and façade construction. They say the restrictions have reduced customer footfall and made it difficult for people to reach their shops. According to the traders, they have repeatedly approached the municipal commissioner, district magistrate, mayor and other officials, but the issue remains unresolved. They also claim that the district magistrate had directed officials to reopen the route, but the barricades have not been removed. The traders have warned that their protest will continue until the obstructions on both sides are removed and normal movement is restored. Meeting with municipal commissioner fails to resolve issue A delegation led by Nitin Kumar Jaiswal, president of the Samast Vyapar Mandal, met Municipal Commissioner Ajay Jain on Tuesday to demand the removal of barricades at both ends of Chatori Gali. Jaiswal said the municipal commissioner told them that further action would be considered after discussions with the traffic police superintendent and the administration. The traders said they had submitted memorandums and met officials several times, but no concrete action had followed. Their frustration has grown as a result, and they have decided to shut their shops to press for a resolution. Traders say restrictions have hit business for 18 months Chatori Gali is a prominent commercial area in Golghar, with food outlets and other businesses. According to traders, the municipal corporation installed barricades and bollards at both ends of the street as part of beautification and façade construction work, restricting access. They claim that the restrictions have reduced their business by 50-60%, leaving shopkeepers struggling as fewer customers visit the area. The traders said beautification work should improve the city without harming local businesses. They have called for an arrangement that allows the work to continue while restoring public access to the market. Traders announce shutdown after repeated complaints The traders said they had repeatedly submitted memorandums to the municipal commissioner, district magistrate, mayor, councillor and other officials over the issue. They claim that the district magistrate had also instructed officials to reopen the route, but the barricades remain in place. The traders said they had decided to close all shops on Wednesday because their complaints had gone unanswered. They warned that the protest would continue if access to Chatori Gali was not restored. Traders who took part in the protest The protest was led by Samast Vyapar Mandal president Nitin Kumar Jaiswal. Other traders who took part included Anil Agrawal, Aman Yadav, Digvijay Singh, Naveen Singh, Sushil Agrawal, Jishan Ahsan, Puneet Jindal, Pradeep Tekriwal, Rajkumar Gupta, Jamal Ahmed, Deepak Jalan, Israr Ahmed, Anil Singh, Anoop Singh, Zafar, Dhananjay Pandey and Ravi, along with other traders from Chatori Gali.

stories.title: Rain alert in 4 UP districts:Over 40,000 homes still flooded in Lucknow; water levels rising in Sitapur and Gonda
stories.summary: The weather in Uttar Pradesh is expected to change over the next 24 hours. A rain alert has been issued for 4 districts today. Meanwhile, 3 districts in the state are affected by floods, and 4 rivers are in spate. In Faizullaganj, Lucknow, more than 40,000 homes are surrounded by floodwater. Over 300,000 people have been affected. Boats are being used in streets and neighbourhoods, and people are leaving their homes to stay elsewhere. Meanwhile, dengue cases are on the rise in the city. A total of 34 cases have been reported in the past 24 hours. Patients are arriving at hospitals with symptoms such as colds, coughs and fever, and tests are confirming dengue infections. Patients are being admitted to Lohia, KGMU and Balrampur hospitals. In Sitapur, more than 20 villages have been surrounded by water after water was released from the Sharda-Banbasa Barrage. Roads are submerged, and government schools have 4 to 5 feet of water inside them. In Gonda, the water level of the Ghaghara River has started rising again, and erosion along its banks has intensified. Weather may change across the state from 15 October Manoj Srivastava, a meteorologist in Varanasi, said dry weather was expected to continue in Uttar Pradesh for the next 48 hours. There is no possibility of rain in any district of the state today or tomorrow. Clear skies and bright sunshine may cause a slight rise in daytime temperatures. However, night temperatures are expected to continue falling. Weather conditions may change again in some parts of the state from 15 October due to the activation of a new Western Disturbance.

stories.title: ‘Sons came from New Zealand and killed my only support’:Wife says both were at fault; they had eloped to marry
stories.summary: A 30-year-old businessman was shot dead at his shop in Uttar Pradesh's Rampur district on October 10, allegedly by his stepson and the latter's cousin. The victim, Navjot Singh, had married Kamaljeet Kaur, 40, who is 10 years older than him. Her two sons from her first marriage were reportedly opposed to the relationship. Police have arrested Navjot's stepson Avdeep, 20, and his cousin Rajan Deep in connection with the murder. An FIR has been registered against seven people, including Avdeep, his brother Joganpreet, 21, and Rajan Deep, following a complaint by Navjot's father, Nishan Singh. Speaking to Dainik Bhaskar, Kamaljeet said Navjot had supported her after the death of her first husband and that the couple had faced threats over their relationship. “Navjot supported me after my first husband's death. If we made a mistake, we both made it. We did what we felt was right. We kept running away out of fear after our marriage. My two sons and my in-laws threatened to kill us both. Things were gradually getting better when my sons killed my husband,” she said. She demanded strict punishment for those responsible for her husband's death. A Dainik Bhaskar team visited the family's home in the Milak Khanam police station area, around 35 km from the district headquarters, and spoke to the victim's wife and parents. What happened in Rampur? On Saturday, October 10, Navjot, a 30-year-old businessman, was sitting at his shop when two men arrived in a car at around 5 pm and opened fire, killing him. According to the report, Navjot's two stepsons live in New Zealand, where they work on dairy farms. Police arrested Avdeep and Rajan Deep on Monday, October 12, and sent them to jail after producing them in court. The police are also looking for other people allegedly involved in the crime. ‘My in-laws threatened to kill us’ Kamaljeet said she first began speaking to Navjot through messages on April 18, 2025, after he was released from prison. Navjot had been jailed for 16 months following allegations of harassment made by his first wife's family. His first wife died by suicide three months after their marriage in 2022. Kamaljeet's first husband died in 2021. She was living with her two sons at her marital home, which was opposite Navjot's house. She said the two began speaking regularly and eventually decided to marry. While Navjot's family had no objection, she alleged that her in-laws threatened to kill the couple if they went ahead with the marriage. On January 2, 2026, she left for Haldwani with Navjot, where they rented a room. The couple married at a gurdwara on February 27. Kamaljeet said she owned two acres of land at her former marital home. She alleged that her in-laws used the land as a pretext to call her to a police station on March 19 and forcibly took her away. Woman alleges forced abortion and police complaint Kamaljeet alleged that she was pregnant at the time and that her in-laws forced her to undergo an abortion. She also claimed that they took away her phone, preventing her from contacting Navjot, and pressured her into filing a police complaint against him. She said she eventually managed to get access to a phone and speak to Navjot. When he asked whether she was staying with her in-laws voluntarily, she told him that she had been taken there against her will. According to Kamaljeet, Navjot came alone on June 4 and took her away. The couple subsequently rented accommodation at a lawyer's house because they feared further threats. On August 22, Navjot brought her to his family home. Kamaljeet said threats continued, but she did not believe her sons would go as far as killing him. “I don't think they could have taken such an extreme step on their own. Someone must have encouraged them from behind,” she said. She added that she wanted the authorities to ensure the strictest possible punishment for her husband's alleged killers. ‘They took away our only support in old age’ Navjot's father, Nishan Singh, said his son was the family's only son and had become a source of support for Kamaljeet. “They shot him dead and took away not only her support but ours as well. He was our only hope for old age. Now we have lost that hope,” he said, demanding strict action against those responsible. Navjot's mother, Jagdish Kaur, also said her son had helped Kamaljeet after she lost her first husband. “He supported a woman who had been left without her husband. But her sons and in-laws could not accept it. They took away an innocent son from us along with her support,” she said. She appealed to the administration and Uttar Pradesh Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath to ensure that the accused were sent to prison and punished strictly. Police confirm arrests An Additional Superintendent of Police said the two men seen firing in CCTV footage had been arrested and sent to jail after being produced in court. Police personnel have been deployed at the victim's family home for security, the officer said, adding that efforts were under way to trace the other people allegedly involved in the incident.

stories.title: Flood victims in Lucknow rush to boats fearing theft:Refuse to leave homes, spend time under tarpaulins on rooftops
stories.summary: Lucknow’s Faizullaganj has been surrounded by floodwater for nearly two weeks. The situation has turned alarming as the water level of the Gomti River continues to rise. More than 50,000 homes have been flooded with water up to five feet deep. People living in single-storey houses are spending their days on rooftops covered with tarpaulins. Despite being surrounded by water, residents are struggling to get drinking water. Hand pumps have been submerged, while power cuts have left submersible pumps unusable. Small children are going without milk, and sick people are struggling to get medicines. Whenever a boat carrying officials or relief supplies appears, residents wave their hands in the hope of receiving help. The Dainik Bhaskar team visited the flood-hit area and witnessed the destruction, damage, and suffering of residents first-hand. The team also assessed the relief being provided by the administration. What did the flood-affected residents say, and what were the conditions on the ground? Let’s find out… A government truck loaded with relief supplies stopped in the Daudnagar area of Faizullaganj. Sacks of ration and other relief materials were unloaded from the truck and loaded onto a boat. Some local residents at the starting point wanted the supplies to be distributed there itself. However, the team firmly refused to distribute the supplies at that spot. When asked why, officials explained, “If we start distributing ration on the main road itself, we will not be able to deliver food and water to those stranded in the lanes and colonies.” Their reasoning was valid. We then boarded the boat loaded with relief supplies and headed towards the flooded areas. The boat was carrying around 25 ration kits, which included: Ration supplies: 10 kg of flour, 10 kg of rice, 2 kg of pigeon pea (arhar) dal, gram, sugar, mustard oil, spices, biscuits and soap. Other items: 2.5 kg of puffed rice, one plastic bucket and one jug. Drinking water: More than 150 bottles of water. The boat also carried food packets arranged by local MLA Neeraj Bora, along with bananas, biscuits and water bottles. Three volunteers from the MLA’s team, a revenue official (lekhpal) representing the administration, and a sub-inspector from the Uttar Pradesh Police for security were also on board. Drinking water is the biggest shortage amid the floods We sailed along Daudnagar’s 60-foot-wide main road towards Mama Colony. The entire road now looked like a deep river. After travelling about one kilometre, a woman called out from the rooftop of a house, “Brother, please give us a bottle of water before the food…” The woman lowered a bucket from the rooftop using a rope. Volunteers on the boat placed four bottles of water, food packets, and bananas in the bucket and sent it back up. At present, drinking water is by far the most sought-after essential in the entire area. Our boat then turned into a narrow lane. At the bend, we asked some people standing on a rooftop whether they had received a ration kit. They replied helplessly, “Sir, we are tenants. We haven’t received any kit.” Seeing their plight, the lekhpal and the police sub-inspector took an on-the-spot decision. They asked the tenants to show their Aadhaar cards. The boat had now reached Mama Colony, one of the worst-affected areas in the floods. In several places, the water was up to 15 feet deep. Around 60% of the houses in the area are single-storey buildings constructed over the past three to four years. At several spots, submerged signboards reading ‘Freehold Plot’ could be seen. Volunteers on the boat were blowing whistles and making announcements over a microphone, calling out, “Is anyone hungry or thirsty? Does anyone need food or water?” Just then, an elderly woman raised her hand from a rooftop to call them over. The boat moved close to the wall of her house. She tied a bucket to the end of her saree and lowered it. Volunteers placed water, food, and a packet of puffed rice in the bucket and sent it back up. When asked whether she had received a ration kit, she said she had not. The people on the boat wanted to give her a full ration kit, but lifting 10–12 kg of supplies to the rooftop using a saree or a thin rope was difficult. The water at that spot was around eight feet deep. It was also impossible to get off the boat and deliver the kit directly. With heavy hearts, the team had to move the boat forward. ‘My entire business is underwater. Where can I go if I leave my home?’ Leaving Mama Colony, our boat headed towards Shivpuram Colony. The entire area was submerged. As soon as people standing on rooftops spotted the boat, they began shouting for help. Here, we met Shabbir Ahmed. A year ago, he had spent around ₹2.5 lakh to set up a cake-making machine. He said, “Water started accumulating after the rains 20–25 days ago. Gradually, it turned into a flood. My house and machine are both submerged. The machine’s main chamber has been damaged, causing a direct loss of ₹65,000. I somehow managed to save the burner and move it to the rooftop. Now everything is submerged here. Where can I go if I leave all this behind?” Dozens of cars could be seen submerged in the lanes across the area. Initially, heavy rainfall prevented people from moving their vehicles out. Then the water rose so rapidly that everything was submerged. Woman says, ‘You are helping us… please have some tea’ While distributing relief supplies, the boat headed towards another neighbourhood in Daudnagar. On the way, we saw an elderly man walking through water up to his neck, with his shirt placed on his head. When asked, he said, “Boats don’t come to our area, so we have no choice but to cross the water like this to collect ration.” Further ahead, a woman on the rooftop of a two-storey house asked for water. The police sub-inspector arranged for bottles of water to be sent up to her. As she was observing a Navratri fast, she was also given bananas. After receiving the supplies, the woman smiled and said, “You have been working so hard since morning. Please stop for a while… I’ll make tea for all of you.” At a time when complaints were being heard everywhere, the woman’s words were enough to lift the spirits of the entire team on the boat. Tearful residents watch the boat move away after supplies run out The newly built 100-bed hospital in Daudnagar has also been submerged in floodwater. We reached the area behind the hospital, where an elderly couple was standing on a rooftop. When the woman lowered a bucket tied to a saree, the volunteers placed essential supplies inside it. Her husband called out from above, “Brother, please give this food packet to someone who needs it more. Just give us drinking water.” Even amid the disaster, people’s concern for others and their humanity remained alive. When the boat reached the next neighbourhood, hungry and thirsty residents came running towards it through waist-deep water. Women arrived carrying their young children in their arms. When we reached another turn in the same neighbourhood, a large crowd of women had gathered. Some had run out of cooking gas, while others did not have even a single grain of ration left at home. While some women openly spoke about their helplessness, others stood silently, hesitant and embarrassed to share their plight. All the supplies remaining on the boat were distributed among the women. However, the number of people in need was so large that nearly half of them had to return empty-handed. These disappointed residents stood amid the floodwater, watching the boat disappear into the distance, hoping that the next boat might bring them enough food for two meals and drinking water. Floodwater has become stagnant and foul; disease outbreaks feared after floods recede. Amid this devastating natural disaster, the administration is currently working at full capacity to deliver relief to those affected. Every day, more than 10,000 bottles of drinking water, around 2,000 ration kits, over 2,000 packets of cooked food, essential medicines, and other supplies are being distributed among affected residents. To coordinate relief operations in the Faizullaganj area, the administration has deployed more than 60 revenue officials (lekhpals) and over 100 police personnel. Several social organisations are also working to provide assistance. It is hoped that the water level will recede over the next week, bringing relief to residents from the floods. However, the challenges will not end once the water recedes. Water that has been stagnant for the past two weeks has turned black and foul-smelling. Septic tanks in homes have become clogged. There is also a risk of diseases spreading after the floodwater recedes. In such circumstances, carrying out rapid sanitisation across the entire area will be a major challenge for the administration.

stories.title: Restore name deleted from SIR at home in 10 minutes:Correct name and address online; BLOs visit homes, keep 3 documents ready
stories.summary: Complaints of names being deleted from voter lists have emerged across the country after the completion of the Special Intensive Revision (SIR). Political parties have taken to the streets over the issue, from Delhi to Lucknow. Many voters are asking whether they can still vote if their names have been deleted during the SIR exercise. The answer is yes, provided their applications are approved and their names are restored to the electoral roll. The process can be initiated from home without visiting a government office. The Election Commission provides three types of facilities: re-registering a name, correcting personal details or address, and seeking the deletion of a deceased person's name or raising an objection to a duplicate voter entry. Here is a step-by-step guide to applying online and offline; If your name has been deleted, apply online in 10 minutes 8. Fill in the self-declaration form prescribed for areas covered by the SIR exercise and submit the application. 9. A 12-digit reference number will be generated after submission. Use it to track your application status. Unable to apply online? Contact your BLO If you cannot fill out the online form or face server issues, contact your area's Booth Level Officer (BLO). Obtain Form 6 from the BLO or download and print it from voters.eci.gov.in. Fill in your name, address, date of birth, and details of your previous voter ID correctly. Attach a passport-size photograph and photocopies of your identity documents before submitting the form to the BLO. Make sure you collect an acknowledgement receipt bearing the BLO's signature and the date. If the application is not processed, you can use the reference details to raise a complaint by calling 1950. When will your name be added to the voter list? After the application is submitted, the BLO will visit your home for physical verification and check the address and identity documents provided. Based on the BLO's report, Election Commission officials will decide whether to approve the application. Once approved, your name will be added to the electoral roll, and a new Elector Photo Identity Card (EPIC) will be sent to your registered address by post. If the BLO refuses to accept your form or you encounter any problem with the application, call the Election Commission's national toll-free number 1950 to lodge a complaint. You can also file a complaint online through the ‘Register Complaint’ section on voters.eci.gov.in. BLOs to conduct door-to-door verification from October 10 to 25 The Election Commission has ordered fresh verification of voter lists in Uttar Pradesh. The exercise will run from October 10 to 25. Special drives will also be held on three Sundays — October 11, 18 and 25. BLOs will be available at polling booths from 10 am to 5 pm with Form 6. Mukesh Kumar Patel, a BLO in the Babaganj Assembly constituency of Pratapgarh, said fresh instructions had been issued for voter list verification. BLOs will visit homes to verify voters' details. Three categories of voters will be checked again: Special camps for homeless people and labourers The Election Commission has said camps will be organised at the booth level to help eligible people register as voters. Separate camps will also be held at night shelters, labour settlements and locations where homeless people live. After verification, BLOs will submit their reports to the Electoral Registration Officer (ERO). The booth-wise lists will subsequently be shared with political parties. The exercise aims to ensure that no eligible voter is left out of the electoral roll. Those who were previously excluded will get another opportunity to apply for inclusion.

stories.title: Blue drum murder case:Muskaan and lover Sahil sentenced to death; she tells Meerut court, ‘Take care of my daughter’
stories.summary: Muskaan, who murdered her husband Saurabh Rajput with the help of her lover in Meerut, has been sentenced to death. The court also sentenced her lover, Sahil, to death. While pronouncing the sentence, the judge said, Punishing wrongdoing is a matter of duty. Both of you, Muskaan and Sahil, brutally murdered Saurabh. Therefore, no leniency will be granted. Before the sentence was pronounced, Muskaan and Sahil, who are in jail, were connected to the court via video conferencing. Muskan Rastogi and Sahil broke down in tears. The judge asked Muskaan, “You have been found guilty of murdering your husband, Saurabh Rajput. What punishment do you want?” She replied, “Please take care of my daughters.” She then fell silent. When Sahil was asked the same question, he remained silent. After the sentence was announced, Saurabh’s mother broke down in tears. She said, “Justice has been delivered peacefully.” Saurabh Rajput was murdered on 3 March 2025. To destroy the evidence, Muskaan and Sahil cut his body into five pieces, stuffed them into a blue drum and then poured a cement mixture over them. Judge said, 'Both of you murdered Saurabh' During the hearing on 30 September, Judge Arvind Mishra said, “Considering all the evidence, it has been established that both of you murdered Saurabh. After the murder, you put his body in a blue drum to destroy evidence. Therefore, both of you are found guilty in the Saurabh murder case. However, we will allow you to present your statements. The sentence will be announced after 15 days.” The judge said such crimes create fear and insecurity in society and affect people’s thinking. If crime continues to increase in society, it is a matter of concern. The role of the justice system is to assure people of their safety. It must maintain people’s faith in the law. The court’s responsibility is not limited to punishing the crime and the accused; it must also consider the accused’s rights and the interests of society. District Judge Arvind Kumar Mishra is the third judge in this case. The trial in the Muskaan-Sahil case began during the tenure of then District Judge Rajat Jain. After his transfer, Sanjeev Kumar became the District Judge. Following Sanjeev Kumar’s transfer, Arvind Kumar Mishra will now deliver the verdict.

stories.title: Divya Mittal faces tough contest in Mirzapur:NDA poses stiff challenge, with two major hurdles ahead
stories.summary: Former IAS officer Divya Mittal is laying the groundwork for her political entry in Mirzapur. There is speculation that she will contest the 2027 Assembly election from here. However, winning as an independent candidate will not be easy. Political observers cite two major reasons for this. First – Lack of a strong booth-level team. Divya does not yet have a strong team with a presence in every area and booth. Popularity alone is not enough to win an election. Reaching voters at every booth and ensuring they turn out to vote are equally important. Second – No electoral experience. Divya has experience in administration and grassroots work, but not in electoral politics. In such a situation, securing support from different castes and communities could be a challenge for her. Divya has been in Vindhyachal since the first day of Navratri. When she arrived there on 11 October, people welcomed her with garlands. She stood in the queue like other devotees to seek blessings from Maa Vindhyavasini. Through this, she conveyed the message that she would remain Mirzapur’s daughter rather than present herself as a politician. She said she would make it clear where she plans to contest before Navratri ends. So, how much support could she get if she contests as an independent? What challenges would she face? Read this report to find out… Mirzapur district has five Assembly constituencies, Chhanbey, Chunar, Majhawan, Marihan and Mirzapur Sadar. The Sadar seat is considered suitable for Divya Mittal because of the large number of Vaishya voters there. However, she would also need support from other communities to win. She would have to secure votes from Brahmins, Yadavs, Binds, Nishads, Muslims and other communities. Vaishya community: Around 1.50 lakh voters, or approximately 30%, belong to the Vaishya community. Divya also comes from this community. Upper castes: Around 1 lakh voters belong to the Brahmin, Thakur and Kayastha communities. Other Backward Classes: There are between 80,000 and 90,000 voters from the Bind, Nishad, Yadav and Maurya communities. Muslims and Dalits: There are around 50,000 Muslim voters and more than 40,000 Dalit voters. If the BJP renominates its sitting MLA, Ratnakar Mishra, securing the support of Brahmin voters could become a challenge for Divya. Apna Dal, SBSP and Nishad Party could pose a challenge Political analyst Virendranath Bhatt says Mirzapur is the political stronghold of Apna Dal (S) national president and Union Minister Anupriya Patel. The Patel family has held considerable influence in the region for around 20 years. Moreover, other BJP allies, including the Nishad Party and SBSP, are also uncomfortable with Divya's entry into politics. Nishad voters have a significant presence in the Majhawan and Chunar areas, while Rajbhar leaders have already made their firm stance on Divya clear. Lack of an organisational structure and political experience In party politics, booth management is one of the biggest factors in winning elections. Parties such as the BJP, Samajwadi Party and Apna Dal (S) have teams of 10–15 workers at every polling booth. As an independent candidate, Divya has a team of some supporters from her administrative background, but she currently lacks a strong network to bring voters to polling booths in every village and ward. Connecting directly with the public while serving as an administrative officer is very different from asking people for votes during an election. There is a significant difference between getting things done through administrative orders and developing the grassroots understanding required in politics. Not a single independent candidate won in the 2022 election From 1952 to the 18th Assembly election in 2022, more than 500 independent candidates have won elections and become MLAs in Uttar Pradesh. In the early decades after Independence, a large number of independent candidates won because of defections, the fragmentation of political parties and their local influence. However, changes in party politics over the past few decades have reduced the number of independent MLAs. According to Assembly figures, not a single independent candidate won in the 2022 Assembly election. In the 2017 election, only three independent candidates made it to the Assembly. They were Raghuraj Pratap Singh, popularly known as Raja Bhaiya, from Kunda; his supporter Vinod Saroj from Babaganj; and Aman Mani Tripathi from Nautanwa, who won the election while in jail. If Raja Bhaiya backs her, she could get Thakur votes Political analyst Ratan Mani Lal believes Raja Bhaiya, president of Jansatta Dal Loktantrik, could support Divya Mittal. During the 2024 Lok Sabha election, political differences between Raja Bhaiya and Anupriya Patel came to the fore. Raja Bhaiya had opposed the Apna Dal (S) candidate. The administrative tensions between Divya Mittal and Anupriya Patel are also well known. If Raja Bhaiya supports Divya, it could help her secure support from a significant section of the Thakur electorate in Mirzapur. Divya will not lack resources; these groups could support her Divya's supporters say she resolved the drinking water problem in Lahuriyadih village while serving as District Magistrate. They cite her popularity and image of honesty as her biggest strengths. If she contests the election, traders, mining business owners, contractors and members of the Vaishya community from Mirzapur and Sonbhadra could help raise funds for her campaign. Divya Mittal's administrative background and popularity are certainly being discussed. However, political party organisations and caste equations play a significant role in Uttar Pradesh politics. Winning as an independent candidate would therefore be a major challenge.

stories.title: Two children die after family eats potatoes, rice in Agra:Five family members ate dinner and went to sleep but failed to wake up
stories.summary: Five members of a family in Agra ate potato and rice at night and then drank tea. They all went to sleep afterwards. When no one came out of the house on Tuesday morning, their neighbours became suspicious. Some people entered the house and found everyone unconscious. They were all taken to the CHC. As their condition was serious, they were all referred to SN Medical College. During this time, the five- and eight-year-old children died. Three members of the family are undergoing treatment in Jaipur in serious condition. The incident took place in the jurisdiction of Kiraoli police station. See 2 pictures Now read the full story Hussain, who lives in Ward No. 10, is originally from Dhanturi Mahoa in Rajasthan. He currently works as a labourer while living in rented accommodation near his in-laws' home in Kirawali. It is being reported that the family members watched a jagran taking place in a nearby neighbourhood on Sunday night. After returning home, they ate potato and rice and drank tea. Entire family found unconscious in the morning When no family member came out of the house for a long time on Monday morning and the door did not open, the neighbours became suspicious. They went inside and found all the members lying unconscious. Local residents then loaded them onto a trolley and took them to the Kirawali Community Health Centre. As their condition was serious, doctors immediately referred them to SN Medical College in Agra. Two children dead, three people undergoing treatment in Jaipur Earlier, Zeeshan alias Golu died at SN Medical College in Agra. Two hours later, his brother Ahil also died while undergoing treatment in Jaipur. The deceased's maternal uncle, Naushad, said, "The children's bodies have been taken to their ancestral village, Dhanturi Mahua. The remaining three people are being treated at a hospital in Jaipur." The superintendent of CHC Kirawali, Dr Raghavendra Singh, said that the case appeared to be food poisoning at first glance. As soon as the police received information about the incident, Kirawali police outpost in-charge Anurag reached the spot with police personnel. The police spoke to local residents and gathered detailed information about the incident.

stories.title: Rapido driver says, 'I’m drinking; I’ll come after I finish':Passenger complains in Varanasi, company deactivates his account and apologises
stories.summary: In Varanasi, a social worker cancelled a bike taxi ride after the Rapido driver said he was drinking alcohol. The social worker had booked the bike through the Rapido app. After booking, they asked the driver for his location. The driver replied, "I am drinking alcohol and will come after I have finished drinking." Hearing this, the social worker cancelled the ride. They filed a complaint about the matter with Rapido. Following the complaint, Rapido has suspended the driver's account. Read the full case now Social worker Ashutosh Tripathi lives in the Ashok Vihar Colony in Seer Govardhanpur, Varanasi. Ashutosh Tripathi said, "I left for Haridwar on the evening of 5 October 2026." I had booked an auto through Rapido to travel from Dafi to Banaras station. Even after around 10 minutes, the auto driver's location on the app was still showing in the same place. I called him and asked how long he would take to arrive. The driver replied, "I'm drinking alcohol right now; after I finish, I'll be there in just five minutes." I was shocked to hear this. I then cancelled the ride and booked another auto. Claim of having an audio recording After this, Ashutosh Tripathi complained to Rapido about the matter. He said that if the driver was found guilty in the investigation, strict action should be taken against him. Ashutosh claims that he has an audio recording of his conversation with the driver. He can make it available for investigation if required. Now read the conversation between the driver and Ashutosh Tripathi Rapido driver: Hello. Ashutosh: Yes, brother, where are you? Rapido driver: "I was drinking, brother." Ashutosh: "You are drinking?" Rapido driver: "Yes, brother." Ashutosh: "Then have your drink. How will you be able to go anywhere when you are drinking?" Rapido driver: "I am coming after drinking; it will take five minutes." Ashutosh: "No, no, you finish your drink, brother." Rapido driver: "Okay, brother." Rapido apologises, says captain's account suspended Rapido apologised for the incident and said, "The company regrets the trouble and inconvenience caused to the passenger because of the incident." The company acknowledged that the experience must have been disappointing and concerning for the passenger. It takes such complaints seriously. Action has been taken in the matter, and the account of the captain concerned has been suspended. The company is investigating the matter under its policies. Passenger safety and trust are its priorities. It is committed to ensuring a safe and reliable service for everyone. It also thanked the passenger for bringing the matter to its attention and for co-operating.

stories.title: Doctors in Lucknow block police vehicle in anger:'Run us over,' they say; Akhilesh urges them to raise fists and oust BJP govt
stories.summary: Doctors' anger boiled over in Lucknow on Tuesday as they stopped a police bus. Several women doctors tried to stop the bus by pushing it with their hands. Some doctors lay down in front of the bus and said, "Run over us; we will not move." They said the Deputy Chief Minister had forgotten his promise and that they had been protesting for 40 days. The incident took place at around 2 pm. Police forcibly removed the doctors from the Gandhi statue in Hazratganj and took them to the protest site at Eco Garden. The police dragged the doctors who resisted by their legs and put them on the bus. Bonded MBBS doctors from the 2018, 2019 and 2020 batches of government medical colleges are staging the protest. The doctors say they are being paid different salaries despite having the same degree, bond and service conditions. The doctors are demanding salary parity and payment of their outstanding arrears. They say Deputy Chief Minister Brajesh Pathak had assured them that their demands would be met and that a government order would be issued within 24 hours. The order has not been issued yet. Samajwadi Party chief Akhilesh Yadav criticised the government over this. Posting the photograph and video on X, he wrote: Raise your fists in revolution and overthrow the BJP government. Those who stole God's money and even cheated God-how would such BJP people spare doctors, the incarnations of God on earth? The BJP is loyal to no one but money. Take a look at two photographs from the protest... Deputy CM had given an assurance on 2 September According to the doctors, a protest was held for around one hour at the Gandhi statue in Hazratganj on 2 September. The doctors were raising slogans against pay disparity and remained firm on their demand to meet Deputy Chief Minister Brajesh Pathak. The Deputy Chief Minister reached the Gandhi statue while getting drenched in the rain and spoke to the doctors for around 20 minutes. The doctors said that during the conversation, the Deputy Chief Minister had told them that the file related to their demands had been completed. He had assured them that a government order fulfilling all their demands, including equal pay, would be issued by 2 p.m. the following day. The doctors then called off the protest, but they allege that the government order has still not been issued. ₹50,000 salary, ₹1.10 lakh for other doctors According to the doctors, they are required to complete two years of compulsory service under the bond service scheme or face a ₹10 lakh bond obligation. During this period, they are posted at CHCs, PHCs and other government health institutions in rural and remote areas. In return, they receive an honorarium of around ₹50,000 to ₹55,000 per month. Same degree, yet a difference in salaries Doctors claim that some doctors serving under bonds in government medical colleges are being paid up to ₹1.10 lakh per month despite having the same MBBS degree and undergoing the same bond, counselling and selection processes. Calling this a disparity in salaries, the protesting doctors are demanding the implementation of equal pay scales and payment of outstanding arrears. Deputy CM accused of failing to fulfil promise The doctors said that Deputy CM Brajesh Pathak had met them during their protest at the Gandhi statue. He had assured them that their demands would be fulfilled and a government order issued within 24 hours. The doctors allege that the government order has still not been issued. They said they were disappointed that the promise had not been fulfilled.

stories.title: Former BJP MP's convoy SUV hits divider:Head constable killed, policeman and driver seriously injured on Agra Expressway
stories.summary: A Scorpio vehicle travelling in the escort convoy of former BJP MP Subrat Pathak collided with a divider in Kannauj. One constable was killed in the accident. Another constable and the driver are critically injured. The accident took place near milestone 145 on the Agra-Lucknow Expressway at around 2 p.m. on Tuesday. As soon as the police received information about the accident, police and the expressway team reached the spot. They pulled the injured men out of the vehicle and took them to hospital, where the injured constable and driver are undergoing treatment. Former MP Subrat Pathak was travelling from Etawah towards Kannauj. Accident occurred 100 metres behind Subrat Pathak’s car Former MP Subrat Pathak’s car was travelling around 100 metres ahead of the Scorpio that crashed. As soon as he learned about the accident, Pathak stopped and informed the police by calling the Dial 112 emergency number. Pathak and others then struggled to rescue everyone trapped inside the vehicle. They took Head Constable Abhishek Tripathi (50), Constable Kunwarpal (51) and driver Sharad Prakash (32) to the Government Medical College in Tirwa in their vehicle. Doctors declared Abhishek Tripathi dead on arrival. He was a resident of Fatehpur. Constable Kunwarpal, who hailed from Etah, and driver Sharad Prakash, a resident of Auraiya, sustained serious injuries. Both have been referred to Kanpur in critical condition. SP Vinod Kumar also reached the medical college along with police personnel. Former MP says Scorpio crash was caused by tyre burst There were two vehicles in Subrat Pathak’s convoy. His car was travelling ahead, while the Scorpio behind it was carrying his security personnel — Head Constable Abhishek Tripathi, Constable Kunwarpal and driver Sharad Prakash. Former MP Subrat Pathak told Dainik Bhaskar over the phone that the Scorpio belonged to him and was used by his security personnel. The vehicle went out of control after a tyre burst and collided with the divider. At the time of the accident, Head Constable Abhishek Tripathi was seated beside the driver, while Constable Kunwarpal was in the back seat. Subrat Pathak’s father and uncle also died in an accident in 2019 Subrat Pathak’s family vehicle met with an accident on the Agra-Lucknow Expressway in 2019, in which his father and uncle died. On February 3, 2019, his father, Om Prakash Pathak, and uncle, Mahesh Chandra, were returning home from Delhi with three other family members — Ashok Kumar, Abha Tiwari and Jaishankar Tiwari. At milestone 192 in Kannauj, their SUV collided with the rear of a dumper parked on the roadside amid dense fog. A bus approaching from behind then hit the SUV. Om Prakash Pathak and Mahesh Chandra died in the accident, while Ashok Kumar, Abha Tiwari and Jaishankar Tiwari were injured. Subrat Pathak defeated Dimple Yadav but lost to Akhilesh in the next election Subrat Pathak came into the spotlight during the 2019 Lok Sabha elections when he contested against Dimple Yadav from Kannauj. He defeated Dimple by 12,353 votes. In the next Lok Sabha elections in 2024, Samajwadi Party chief Akhilesh Yadav contested from Kannauj himself. He defeated Subrat Pathak by a margin of 1.70 lakh votes.

stories.title: Murder accused model Shraddha seen in gangster’s lap:Used Mukhtar gang’s name to extort money; Lucknow police hunt several history-sheeters
stories.summary: A major revelation has emerged in the Shiva Sharma murder case in Lucknow involving accused model Shraddha Dubey. She was allegedly connected to several history-sheeters and politicians. A photograph of her with Samajwadi Party leader Shivpal Yadav has also surfaced. Shraddha allegedly befriended gangsters and used their names and networks to intimidate people. She reportedly threatened people by claiming links with the Mukhtar Ansari gang. She also allegedly got gang members to make phone calls to intimidate them. Shraddha is also accused of blackmailing people and extorting money. According to reports, she allegedly used photographs taken with people to blackmail them. However, her associations with gangsters reportedly did not last long, and they eventually drifted apart. Police may now question the history-sheeters who were in contact with Shraddha. See two photographs of Shraddha with gangsters... Shraddha's links with several history-sheeters in the city Police investigation has revealed that Shraddha was in contact with several leaders and a history-sheeter from the city. Shraddha was also found to be connected to Abhishek Singh, alias Babu, a history-sheeter from the Madiyaon police station area. His photograph is also available on social media. Babu Singh is said to be a henchman of Mukhtar Ansari. Babu has established a reign of fear in Madiyaon, Aliganj and the surrounding areas. Babu Singh's name came into the spotlight in 2020 The henchmen of Abhishek Singh alias Babu Singh, who was said to be close to strongman Mukhtar Ansari, went on a rampage in December 2020. They kidnapped tent businessman Vivek Kumar Rawat to arrange bail for Babu Singh, who was in jail. They held him hostage and brutally beat him with kicks and punches. They demanded ₹10,000 for Babu Singh's bail. During the assault, they even made him lick spit. They held him hostage and drove him around the city for around 2.5 hours. They then struck him with the butt of a pistol, released him and fled after threatening him to bring the money. Shraddha claimed she was connected to Mukhtar after befriending Babu Police sources said Shraddha befriended Babu Singh and used his entire network. On several occasions, she threw her weight around by claiming to be connected to Mukhtar Ansari. If anyone wanted to get away after becoming fed up with her blackmail, she used photographs to create fear. A police investigation has revealed a pattern of Shraddha's extortion. She would first befriend people and invite them to her home, then accuse them of theft and threaten to implicate them in a false case to extort money. She also made private videos of several prominent people and blackmailed them. Photograph with man accused of ₹5 crore fraud A photograph of Shraddha with a man named Zulfiqar, besides Babu Singh, has also emerged. Zulfiqar is reportedly accused of fraud involving ₹5 crore. In a video on social media, Shraddha can be seen with him. However, the date, location and full context of the photograph and video could not be verified. Watch some reels of Shraddha... History-sheeter Rishabh Rai's audio also becomes a talking point Following the murder of Shiva, a purported audio recording of history-sheeter Rishabh Rai has also become a talking point. The viral audio is said to contain threats allegedly issued by Rishabh Rai to Shiva. However, Dainik Bhaskar does not verify the authenticity of the audio. It is being reported that Shiva's mother had also lodged an extortion case against eight to 10 people, including Rishabh Rai. Police may now investigate all aspects linked to Shiva's death, the alleged threat, extortion and Shraddha's contacts. Now read what the whole case is about... Shiva Sharma died after falling from the fourth floor of Awadh Green Apartment in Hazratganj on 9 October. Shiva had been living with Shraddha in a live-in relationship for four months. He was wearing only underwear. Lipstick had been applied to his face. Shiva's mother, Ranjana Sharma, filed a murder case in connection with her son's death against five people, including Shraddha, her sister Rashmi and their driver Adil. She alleged that Shraddha had pushed her son from the fourth floor. There were marks on several parts of Shiva's body from cigarette burns.

stories.title: Women cops thrash 2 eve-teasers in Pratapgarh:Ask ‘Will you harass girls again?’; accused fold hands, apologise
stories.summary: In Pratapgarh, a woman constable beat two men who had harassed a female student and took them to the police station. She kept thrashing them with a baton for about one kilometre, repeatedly asking, "Will you harass more girls?" The men screamed and cried. They folded their hands and apologised, saying, "We made a mistake. It will not happen again." At around 2.30 p.m. on Monday afternoon, the student was returning home from college. That was when two men on a motorcycle began harassing her. They asked for her mobile number and behaved indecently with her. Distressed, the student went to a police outpost 100 metres away and, crying, said, "Two boys are harassing me." The police personnel present at the outpost went with the student, but by then the men had fled. The police questioned people in the area and examined CCTV footage, which led to the identification of the accused. The police arrested both of them late at night. On Tuesday morning, a women police team brought them to the spot where they had harassed the student to teach them a lesson. She took them to the police station by their collars, beating them with sticks. During this, people also slapped the miscreants from time to time and applauded the police action. A video of the entire incident has also emerged. The incident took place at Bhangwa Chungi crossroads in the City Kotwali area. First, take a look at two pictures of the harassment- Now, understand the full case in sequence- Now, see five pictures of the police action- City Circle Officer Ashutosh Mishra said that on Monday evening, the Anti-Romeo squad found two youths riding a motorcycle harassing a girl in the Nagar Kotwali area. A case was registered at Nagar Kotwali. Both accused were arrested on Tuesday. Further legal action is being taken in the matter.

stories.title: Yogi says mafias now wet their pants:Rioters celebrate Urs in jail; honorarium of 68,000 Gram Praharis increased
stories.summary: Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath said on Tuesday that riots used to break out in Bareilly whenever a festival or religious occasion approached. “Now, rioters are celebrating Urs inside jail. Anyone who starts a riot knows the price they will have to pay,” he said. He added that they would even lose the wealth inherited from their fathers and grandfathers. “Uttar Pradesh is now identified with celebrations. Those who used to intimidate others are now scared themselves. When they see a UP Police vehicle, mafias wet their pants. UP has become mafia-free,” he said. Yogi made these remarks while addressing a teachers’ conference attended by teachers from nine districts. He appealed to them to vote for Dr Hari Singh Dhillon, the candidate for the Legislative Council seat under the teachers’ constituency. Earlier, Yogi announced an increase in the honorarium of 68,000 village watchmen (gram praharis) across Uttar Pradesh at an event in Bareilly. Their monthly honorarium has been increased from ₹2,500 to ₹3,500. He also announced cashless medical treatment worth up to ₹5 lakh for the watchmen and their families. 6 key takeaways from Yogi’s address 1. ‘Chain snatchers are certain to be left limping at the next intersection’ Yogi said that those who were in power earlier were themselves involved in looting and corruption. “Who could be caught in such a situation? The very people who were supposed to protect the public were thieves themselves. But Uttar Pradesh has changed now, as there are no riots or disturbances. Mafias have been wiped out. Criminals must fear the law. If anyone tries to lay a hand on a girl, Yamraj prepares to send them to the afterlife at the next intersection. If anyone commits chain snatching, they are certain to be left limping at the next intersection,” he said. 2. ‘The state was facing a crisis of identity’ Yogi said a country or state is identified by its education system. Uttar Pradesh was once known for its education system. However, as successive governments moved education off their agendas after Independence, the consequences affected the state’s administration and law and order. “By 2017, the state had reached a point where it was facing a crisis of identity. The education system had been ruined,” he said. 3. ‘The previous government also moved at a snail’s pace’ Yogi said the board examination dates have been announced and the main exams will be completed in just 14 days. The results will be declared within the next 14 days. Earlier, the process used to take six months — three months for examinations and another three months for results. “The previous government also moved at a snail’s pace. It crawled like a tortoise. Now, we have a government that moves at bullet-train speed. It is a double-engine government, and its decisions are also taken at bullet-train speed,” he said. 4. ‘CBSE teachers will also get cashless treatment’ The Chief Minister said MLC candidate Dr Hari Singh Dhillon had raised the demand for cashless medical treatment for teachers. “When he said that our teachers should get cashless treatment facilities, I told him, ‘Is this even something that needs to be demanded? It is our responsibility. There will be no need to ask; we will provide it ourselves.’ Let the government continue, and we will extend this facility to CBSE teachers as well,” Yogi said. 5. Recounts an incident involving a Samajwadi Party education minister, leaving everyone laughing Yogi said that they used to organise events in Gorakhpur to mark the martyrdom day of Pandit Ram Prasad Bismil. The Samajwadi Party was in power at the time. Some people from Gorakhpur invited the party’s secondary education minister to an event. While the minister’s programme was taking place at one venue, Yogi’s programme was being held elsewhere. When the minister took the stage, he thanked the organisers and said they had done a great thing by inviting him to celebrate the birth anniversary of Ustad Bismillah Khan, adding that he had done great work. A businessman sitting in the audience pointed out, “Sir, he is Pandit Ram Prasad Bismil.” The minister replied, “It seems you are a BJP supporter; that is why you are calling him Pandit.” Yogi said, “If this is the kind of education minister a government has, where will it take education?” 6. ‘No curfew, no riots; everything is fine in UP now’ Yogi said that the poor and farmers were not invited to the Chief Minister’s residence earlier. Instead, he alleged, gangsters, rioters and people involved in extortion were invited. “That is why the Samajwadi Party is the most troubled whenever the government launches an anti-mafia campaign. When a mafia member dies, they visit his grave, offer fatiha and shed tears,” he said. Yogi concluded with the slogan: “No curfew, no riots; everything is fine in Uttar Pradesh now.”

stories.title: Woman who fell from Lucknow hotel's 10th floor was married:Divorce case pending; man staying with her fled after death
stories.summary: A 24-year-old woman fell to her death from the 10th floor of Lucknow's Hotel Celestial Manor. She had been staying with a young man, who fled after she fell. The incident took place at 6 p.m. on Monday in the Sushant Golf City police station area. The two had checked into the hotel at noon. Samreen was a resident of Lucknow, while the young man, Avnish Jaiswal, is from Sultanpur. Samreen worked at a hotel and was married. Divorce proceedings against her husband were under way. She was due to appear in court in the case on Monday, but did not do so. She had left home at 11 a.m., saying she was going to buy clothes for her sister Habiba. See three pictures- Both came to the hotel during the day; the girl fell in the evening According to the police, Avneesh Jaiswal, who lived in Dostpur, Sultanpur, had booked hotel room number 1037. Avneesh and Samreen reached the hotel at 12 noon on Monday. At 6 p.m., Samreen fell from the balcony. On seeing this, Avneesh ran into the lift. He then exited on the ground floor, took his bike from the parking area and fled. The police arrived some time later. They called the field unit and had the crime scene photographed and video-recorded. Evidence was collected, and the body was sent for a post-mortem examination. Samreen lived with her mother, five sisters and two brothers Samreen was the third of five sisters and two brothers. Her father, Mohammad Tajju, died in Mumbai seven years ago. Her elder brother Imran lives in Saudi Arabia and her younger brother Amir lives in Oman. Both do embroidery work on clothes. Samreen married a man who lived near the tobacco market in Chaupatiya six years ago. They had a child after the marriage, but the child died within six months. Disputes between Samreen and her husband began just a year after their marriage. Since then, Samreen had been living with her mother and sisters. Girl's maternal uncle said - The boy took her to the hotel by deceiving her Sameerin's maternal uncle, Mohammad Shakeel, said that Sameerin was a simple, innocent girl. The young man had been pursuing her for several months. He took her to a hotel by deceiving her. I have no information about what happened at the hotel. The family learnt about the incident at 11 p.m.

stories.title: BJP state secretary tied up, mouth taped in Kanpur:Locked in farmhouse bathroom as robbers stole cash and jewellery from locker
stories.summary: Ramesh Yadav, Uttar Pradesh state minister of the BJP Backward Classes Morcha, was robbed of ₹12 lakh in Kanpur after masked men tied his hands and feet. The robbers entered his farmhouse around midnight on Monday, held him hostage and looted the money before locking him in a bathroom and fleeing. The incident took place in the Sen Paschimpara police station area, 20 km from the city. Ramesh became the BJP Backward Classes Morcha’s state minister on 1 October. On Monday, after taking charge in Lucknow, he reached Kanpur at 12.30 am. He was staying alone at his farmhouse, 500 metres from his home. Four guards were deployed there. Police were informed about the robbery at 1.20 am. Additional Police Commissioner Dr Vipin Tada and DCP Dipendranath Chaudhary reached the spot with a police team. Investigators found no CCTV footage of the robbers entering the farmhouse. However, two of them were captured on camera while fleeing. Both placed their feet on a washbasin and jumped over a tin shed to escape. They were wearing black clothes. Ramesh has served as a block pramukh twice. His wife, Shashi, has also held the post. In 2022, he contested the Assembly election from the Bithoor seat on a BSP ticket.

stories.title: 9 arrested in Varanasi for selling Chinese manjha:137kg banned thread seized, raids conducted after trader's death
stories.summary: After 55-year-old Sunil Gujarati died in Varanasi due to Chinese manjha, police tightened enforcement across the city. On Monday, simultaneous raids were conducted in all police station areas, leading to the arrest of nine accused. Police seized more than 137 kg of banned manjha and registered eight cases in connection with the matter. Following the accident on the Kajjakpura flyover on 11 October, the police commissioner had directed officials to stop the sale and storage of illegal manjha. During the drive, shops, markets and suspected locations were inspected. In Ramnagar, 20 kg of manjha was found abandoned along the banks of the river. Raids at shops and suspected locations across the city Teams from the Varanasi Commissionerate police conducted simultaneous raids from Monday morning at all the city's major markets, shops selling kites and string, as well as suspected warehouses. The police commissioner had clearly instructed that the sale and storage of the deadly Chinese kite string must be stopped at any cost. During the entire drive, the police registered a total of eight cases. Arrests made in these police station areas According to figures released by the police department, the biggest success was achieved by the Dashashwamedh police station. Its personnel arrested one accused person and seized 56 kilograms of Chinese manjha from him alone. Meanwhile, the Kotwali police arrested two accused persons and recovered 37.873 kilograms of manjha. In addition, 20 kilograms of unclaimed manjha was recovered from the riverbank in Ramanagar. 10 kilograms of manjha found in Bhelupur Ten kilograms of China manjha have been recovered, with one arrest, from the Bhelupur police station area. Lalpur-Pandeypur police arrested one accused and recovered 6,500 grams of banned manjha. Sarnath police arrested two people and seized 3 kilograms 865 grams, Manduadih police arrested one person and seized 2 kilograms, while Lohta police arrested one person and seized half a kilogram of manjha. Action will be taken against station in-charge for negligence Following this major crackdown, the Varanasi Police Commissioner issued strict instructions to all station house officers (SHOs) and outpost in-charges. He ordered that the sale, storage and use of Chinese manjha in the city be effectively curbed completely. The Police Commissioner made it clear that any laxity or negligence in this work would not be tolerated at any level. If an accident involving Chinese manjha occurs in any area or illegal sales are found, the station house officer concerned will be held directly responsible and disciplinary action will be taken against them. Commissionerate Police has warned all kite traders and citizens in the city that selling, stocking or using banned Chinese kite string to fly kites is a serious and punishable offence. Strict legal action will be taken against those who do so under the Environment Protection Act and the relevant sections of the IPC.

stories.title: Floods hit Lucknow, boats ply through streets:34 dengue cases in 24 hours; 20 Sitapur villages submerged
stories.summary: Three districts in Uttar Pradesh are in the grip of floods, with four rivers in spate. In Lucknow's Faizullaganj, more than 40,000 houses are surrounded by floodwater, affecting a population of over 3 lakh. Boats are being used to navigate the streets and neighbourhoods. Many people have left their homes and moved to safer places. Meanwhile, dengue cases are rising in the city. As many as 34 cases have been reported in the past 24 hours. Patients are reaching hospitals with symptoms such as cold, cough and fever, with tests confirming dengue infection. Patients are being admitted to Lohia Hospital, KGMU and Balrampur Hospital. In Sitapur, more than 20 villages have been surrounded by water after water was released from the Sharda-Banbasa Barrage. Roads are submerged, while government schools have 4-5 feet of water inside them. In Gonda, the water level of the Ghaghra has started rising again, with erosion along the riverbanks intensifying once more.

stories.title: Two businessman brothers murdered, mother demands killers’ blood:Indiscriminate firing in Pilibhit also kills 20-year-old passer-by
stories.summary: Three people, including two businessman brothers, were killed in Pilibhit. One person is in critical condition. According to the police, the incident took place over donations for the Ramleela committee. At around 9:30 pm on Monday, the attackers reached the businessmen brothers' house. An argument broke out during this time. The attackers beat them with sticks before opening fire. Both brothers were shot. Two passers-by who were travelling along the road were also injured by gunfire. All four were taken to hospital, where doctors declared both brothers and one of the passers-by dead. Meanwhile, the businessman's brother was referred to Bareilly, where he succumbed during treatment. The incident took place in the Amaria police station area, around 20 km from the district headquarters. The deceased have been identified as businessman brothers Ankit Gupta (30), Mohit Gupta (38), and passer-by Kunal Srivastava (18). The injured passer-by has been identified as Rose Gupta (20). stories.title: Delhi-Gorakhpur-Bihar passengers get relief:Travel without reservation; festival special train to run from November 5
stories.summary: To manage the increased rush on trains during the festive season, the railway has decided to run an unreserved festival special train between Shakur Basti and Mansi for passengers' convenience. The train, which will run via Gorakhpur, will make eight trips in each direction in November. This will provide relief to passengers travelling between Delhi, western Uttar Pradesh, Purvanchal and Bihar. The train will have coaches of the general second class as well as sleeper class, but passengers will be allowed to travel in the sleeper-class coaches only with unreserved tickets. According to the railway, train number 04406 Shakur Basti-Mansi unreserved festival special will depart from Shakur Basti on 5, 6, 7, 10, 11, 12, 13 and 14 November. In the return direction, train number 04405 Mansi-Shakur Basti will operate on 7, 8, 9, 12, 13, 14, 15 and 16 November. Train will depart from Shakur Basti at 7:10 pm Return journey: departs Gorakhpur at 3:05 pm On the return journey, train number 04405 Mansi-Shakur Basti Special will depart from Mansi at 4:30 am. Via Khagaria, Begusarai, Barauni, Shahpur Patori, Hajipur and Sonpur, the train will pass through Chhapra at 10:30 am and Siwan at 11:35 am. After that, it will reach Deoria Sadar at 12:45 pm and depart from Gorakhpur at 3:05 pm. The train will reach Lucknow's Aishbagh and Unnao via Khalilabad, Basti, Gonda and Barabanki. It will then reach Shakurbasti at 11:30 a.m. the following day via Kanpur Central, Etawah, Tundla, Aligarh, Ghaziabad and New Delhi. Unreserved special train to run with 16 coaches According to information released by the Railways, a total of 16 coaches will be attached to this special train. These will include 14 general second-class and sleeper-class coaches, along with two SLR coaches. The sleeper-class coaches will also operate as unreserved coaches. This means passengers will not have the facility of reserved seats in these coaches. The special train is being operated keeping in mind passengers travelling to and from Purvanchal and Bihar from Delhi and surrounding areas during the festivals. Passengers are advised to obtain information about the train from the Railways' official enquiry service according to the relevant date and time before travelling.

stories.title: 5kg of drugs sent on Raksha Bandhan, ₹1.29 crore collected:Cash found in Scorpio’s secret compartment in Mandsaur; accused caught before returning to UP
stories.summary: ₹1.29 crore was recovered from a Scorpio-N in Barkheda Uda village in the Shamgarh area of Mandsaur. The cash had been hidden in a secret chamber built into the vehicle's body. A new disclosure emerged in the case on Thursday. Mohammad Islam and Suryaprakash, who had come from Bareilly in Uttar Pradesh, had arrived to collect outstanding money. It is being reported that around Raksha Bandhan, Bhawanishankar Meena had ordered approximately 5 kg of brown sugar from them. The two had come to collect the outstanding amount. They were about to return to UP when the police arrested all three. However, there has been no official confirmation of the transaction or the purchase and sale of brown sugar. Police raid house after receiving information about narcotics Acting on information received on Thursday about drug trafficking in Barkheda Uda village, a team from three police stations raided Bhawanishankar Meena's house under the direction of SP Vinod Kumar Meena. The team included Shamgarh police station in-charge Kapil Saurashtriya and Bhanpura police station in-charge Vinay Bundela. Bhawanishankar Meena (49), Bareli resident Mohammad Islam (47) and Suryaprakash (59) were found at the house. A Scorpio-N was also parked there. The vehicle had no number plate. A number plate bearing the words 'Gov. Of India' was found inside. ₹1.29 crore recovered from secret chamber The police took the vehicle to Shamgarh police station. It was thoroughly inspected with the help of a mechanic. A secret chamber made by welding was found in the body behind the back seat. When the vehicle's parts were opened, bundles of notes were found inside. It took around 1.5 hours to count the cash using a machine. The police seized ₹1 crore 29 lakh. The vehicle was identified as belonging to Mohammad Islam through its engine and chassis numbers. Cash source under investigation; Income Tax Department informed SP Vinod Kumar Meena said the police had received credible information about the purchase and sale of narcotics at the house. During the operation, cash hidden in the vehicle was found. The two people who had come from Bareilly and the owner of the house have been arrested. The Income Tax Department has been emailed to ascertain the source of the cash. The police are investigating the narcotics trade and the criminal records of the accused. One of those arrested also has a previous criminal record. Family linked to liquor trade According to sources, Bhawanishankar Meena's family is involved in the liquor trade. Liquence licences in Melkheda and Khadawada are in the name of his son, Arvind. Bhawanishankar's wife is the village sarpanch. He is said to be associated with the BJP. In 2025, Arvind was accused of attacking Sub-Inspector Avinash Soni, who was posted at Shamgarh police station, with a stick. The sub-inspector received 18 stitches to his head in the incident. The police are currently investigating the source of the cash, the role of the accused and their possible links to the narcotics trade.

stories.title: EC orders voter list revision in 17 states-UTs:List includes MP and UP; SSR vs SIR explained in 5 points
stories.summary: The Election Commission of India has directed 17 states and Union Territories, including Madhya Pradesh, Uttar Pradesh, Bihar and Rajasthan, to conduct a Special Summary Revision SSR of electoral rolls. The Commission has sent letters to the Chief Electoral Officers of the concerned states and Union Territories. Under the SSR, new names will be added to electoral rolls and errors in existing entries will be corrected. Young people who turn 18 in 2027 will also be able to apply for inclusion. The order comes amid controversy and protests over the Special Intensive Revision (SIR). What is the objective of SSR? According to the Election Commission, the objective of SSR is to keep electoral rolls up to date and ensure that no eligible citizen is left off the list. Special attention will be given to young people and first-time voters. Young people who turn 18 on 1 April, 1 July or 1 October 2027, in addition to those who turn 18 on 1 January 2027, will also be able to apply in advance. The Commission has directed officials to make efforts to receive applications from all eligible voters. SSR order does not mention a separate process to add names omitted during SIR The Election Commission’s order on SSR does not specify a separate procedure for adding the names of people left off electoral rolls during the SIR. However, under the SIR rules, anyone whose name is missing from the draft electoral roll can claim inclusion by submitting Form 6. The applicant must also provide the required documents. The name will be added only if the Electoral Registration Officer (ERO) accepts the application after verifying the applicant’s eligibility. Number and location of polling stations to be reviewed Officials’ posts must not remain vacant; transfers also restricted The Commission has directed the chief secretaries of states and Union Territories to ensure that Chief Electoral Officers (CEOs), District Election Officers (DEOs), Electoral Registration Officers (EROs), Assistant Electoral Registration Officers (AEROs) and Booth Level Officers (BLOs) are provided with adequate staff and resources during the SSR. The posts of CEOs, DEOs, EROs and AEROs must not remain vacant during this period. These officials cannot be transferred without the Commission’s approval. If a transfer is necessary, a proposal explaining the reasons must be submitted to the Commission. Under Section 13CC of the Representation of the People Act, 1950, officials involved in preparing, revising and correcting electoral rolls will work under the Election Commission’s control and supervision during this period. Voters’ addresses to be recorded in a standard format The Election Commission has directed officials to record voters’ addresses in a uniform format in electoral rolls. This will make it easier to identify voters’ homes and their respective polling areas. Assembly elections due in five states, including Uttar Pradesh, next year Uttar Pradesh, Uttarakhand, Punjab, Manipur and Goa are scheduled to hold Assembly elections in 2027. SSR will be conducted in all five states. The term of the Uttar Pradesh Assembly ends on 22 May 2027. The terms of the Assemblies of Manipur, which has 60 seats; Goa, with 40 seats; Punjab, with 117 seats; and Uttarakhand, with 70 seats, will end on different dates in March 2027. SSR schedule for these states and Union Territories to be announced later The SSR schedule for Andhra Pradesh, Arunachal Pradesh, Chandigarh, Dadra and Nagar Haveli, Daman and Diu, Haryana, Jharkhand, Karnataka, Maharashtra, Meghalaya, Mizoram, Nagaland, Delhi, Odisha, Sikkim, Tripura and Telangana will be announced later.

stories.title: Yogi renames Atiq’s Kasari-Masari area:Performs bhumi pujan; 602 flats to be built for poor on seized land
stories.summary: Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath announced that Kasari-Masari, the area associated with mafia don Atiq Ahmed, would be renamed Shri Krishna Puri. Speaking in Prayagraj on Thursday, Yogi said the name Kasari-Masari sounded like it was associated with butchers. He also performed the bhoomi pujan for the flats to be built on government land freed from the possession of Atiq and his henchmen. Yogi said: "The government is now building homes for the poor on land belonging to the mafia. The land on which mafia figures Atiq and Ashraf once set foot would become theirs. The state government used to bow before them." A 14-storey building will be constructed as part of the Prayagraj Development Authority's (PDA) 9,811-square-metre housing project. It will have a total of 602 flats. Each flat will have two bedrooms, a hall and a kitchen. Each flat will have an area of 56.45 square metres. The project will also include parking, rainwater harvesting and a solar system. Other facilities will include a swimming pool, community hall and commercial complex.
