stories.title: Judge known for death sentences orders BSA’s arrest:Muzaffarnagar CO told to act after officer skips summons
stories.summary: The Muzaffarnagar court has ordered the arrest of the district's BSA, Sandeep Kumar. Additional District and Sessions Judge Ravi Diwakar told the CO, "Arrest the BSA and bring him here on 12 October at all costs." The case concerns an assault after forcibly entering a woman's house. The dispute was over the ages of two accused people. The court had directed the BSA to appear with documents related to the ages of both accused, but he ignored the order. Judge Ravi Diwakar, who ordered the BSA's arrest, is also known as the judge who awards death sentences. Since November 2025, he has sentenced 23 convicts to death in Muzaffarnagar and has awarded the death penalty to 36 people over the course of his career. Woman was subjected to a deadly attack six years ago The case dates back to 2020. Some people forcibly entered the home of a woman living in a neighbourhood under the jurisdiction of New Mandi police station. They allegedly assaulted the woman and attempted to kill her in a deadly attack. Following the incident, the victim filed a case against the accused at New Mandi police station in Muzaffarnagar. Legal proceedings were initiated against a total of six accused in the case, including Monu, Krishnapal, Satyam and Bantu. Questions raised over the ages of two accused As the judicial process in the case progressed, a new twist emerged. According to Assistant District Government Counsel Kuldeep Kumar, the families of two of the six accused claimed in court that both accused were minors at the time of the incident. Following this claim, the court was faced with the question of determining the actual ages of the two accused. It became necessary to establish whether the two accused were minors when the incident occurred. In this connection, the court had summoned BSA Sandeep Kumar to give evidence and produce the necessary documents. BSA fails to appear in court despite summons being issued BSA Sandeep Kumar was to have his statement recorded in a case related to the accused's age. In accordance with the court's order, the summons had been personally served on him on 18 September. Despite this, he did not appear in court on Thursday. Judge Ravi Kumar Diwakar directed City CO Siddharth Kumar Mishra to issue a non-bailable warrant against BSA Sandeep Kumar. He also ordered that Kumar be arrested and produced in court by 12 October.

stories.title: Seeing officials, bribery-taking lekhpal ran into house:Burned the cash and flushed the ashes down a drain; team broke down door and arrested him in Lalitpur
stories.summary: In Lalitpur, the Anti-Corruption Team caught a revenue official while accepting a bribe of ₹15,000. At around 3 p.m. on Thursday, the team reached the revenue official's rented house. As soon as he saw the team, he ran inside and locked the door. He placed the notes he had received as a bribe on a gas stove and burnt them. He flushed the ashes down the sink drain. The team immediately broke down the door and caught the revenue official. His hands were then washed with water. The water turned pink when his hands were washed. When the team searched the room, it also found pieces of the burnt notes. The Anti-Corruption Team took the accused revenue official with it for questioning. The incident took place in Toria village, under the jurisdiction of Bar police station, around 30 kilometres from the district headquarters. Now, know the full details of the case Manoj Kumar (35), a farmer from Toriya village, said that lekhpal Vipul Tiwari had demanded a bribe of ₹20,000 from him to allow him to retain possession of his land. He was asked to pay ₹15,000 as the first instalment. Manoj said that he did not want to pay the bribe, so he complained to the anti-corruption team in Jhansi. The lekhpal first called him to Tuwan Crossing to collect the bribe, but did not take the money there. He then called him near Sharda Temple, but did not accept the money there either. At around 3 p.m. on Thursday, the lekhpal called Manoj outside his rented house in Sharda Vihar Colony, Azadpura. As soon as Manoj handed him ₹15,000, the anti-corruption team arrived at the spot. Team broke down the gate to enter the house As soon as he saw the trap team, the lekhpal ran inside his rented house and locked the gate. The team tried for a long time to get the gate opened, but the lekhpal did not open the door. The team then broke down the gate and entered the house. The room was filled with smoke because papers had been burnt. Ash from the burnt notes was lying in the kitchen sink. During the search, the team also recovered pieces of the burnt notes. The team then caught the lekhpal and had his hands washed with a chemical. After his hands were washed, the chemical turned pink. The trap team then arrested him. The accused lekhpal, Vipul Tiwari, is a resident of Amapur Patti village in the Ashpur Devsara police station area of Pratapgarh. He was currently living as a tenant in Aman Srivastava's house in Dumdum Colony, in the Kotwali police station area of Lalitpur. Land had already been measured in 2023 According to complainant Manoj, on 30 May 2023, the then revenue accountant measured his land and confirmed its boundary demarcation. He was subsequently given possession of the plot. Stones were also installed on the land, according to the field book. Manoj alleges that despite this, local revenue accountant Vipul Tiwari demanded a bribe from him, citing an application submitted by other account holders seeking action under Section 30(2).

stories.title: Yogi government to give sarees to 1.80 lakh Anganwadi workers:Free gas cylinder on Diwali; Yogi Cabinet meeting tomorrow
stories.summary: The Uttar Pradesh government will give one sari each to more than 1.80 lakh Anganwadi workers as uniforms. The proposal will be passed at the Cabinet meeting chaired by Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath on Friday. Ujjwala Yojana beneficiaries will receive one free cooking gas cylinder each on Diwali. Around 1.90 lakh people in the state will benefit from this. A Kia Carnival car will be purchased for Governor Anandi Ben Patel. Its on-road price is around ₹60 lakh. Chief Secretary S.P. Goyal issued the meeting agenda at around 6 p.m. on Thursday. It includes 31 proposals. Some proposals may also be brought to the meeting outside the agenda. Government may increase paddy MSP The policy for procuring paddy at the minimum support price (MSP) during the Kharif Marketing Year 2026-27 will be approved at the Cabinet meeting. The government may increase the MSP for paddy. Last year, the MSP was ₹2,369 per quintal for common-grade paddy and ₹2,389 per quintal for Grade A paddy. The paddy procurement target may also be increased this year. In addition, the policy for procuring coarse grains at the MSP during the Kharif Marketing Year 2026-27 will be approved. This includes maize, millet and sorghum. A proposal to procure bags allocated by the Government of India for the purchase of coarse grains may also be approved. Internship allowance for AYUSH students to be increased The rotational internship allowance for students who pass the BAMS, BUMS and BHMS examinations from government Ayurvedic, Unani and homoeopathic medical colleges, institutions and universities under the AYUSH Department will be increased. stories.title: Gangster shot dead while going to buy liquor:Left wife, child at home; released from jail 10 days ago
stories.summary: A gangster was shot dead three times in Rampur at 11 a.m. on Thursday. Three assailants who arrived on a motorcycle shot him and fled. The police immediately took the man to hospital, where doctors declared him dead. He had been released from jail just 10 days earlier. Shortly before the incident, gangster Sandeep was accompanied by his wife and six-month-old child. After dropping them home, he was riding his motorcycle to a liquor shop. More than 16 cases are registered against Sandeep. The SP has deployed a police team to solve the murder. The incident took place in the Bilaspur area. Sandeep worked at a rice mill Sandeep Chauhan, alias Sunny (30)), a resident of Sanga Farm in Dibdiba village, worked at a rice mill cutting packaging material. His family includes his wife, Shivani, their six-month-old son, Aditya, and their three-year-old daughter, Aaradhya. The rest of Sandeep's family, including his parents, lives in Mohammaganj village in Bareilly. Sandeep's wife, Shivani, said their six-month-old son, Aditya, was ill. This morning, she went with her husband to get medicine for their son. Near the liquor shop, they met Sandeep's friend, Brajesh. Sandeep began talking to him and sent me home with their son. Sandeep fell to the ground after being hit by 3 bullets Three attackers riding a motorcycle opened indiscriminate fire at Sandeep. He collapsed on the spot after being hit by three bullets. One bullet struck his back, while two hit the upper part of his head. Panic broke out at the scene as soon as the sound of gunfire was heard. The assailants fled the spot during the commotion. Acting on information from passers-by, Circle Officer Harshita Singh, Kotwali Station House Officer Jeet Singh and Eisanagar outpost in-charge Vishnu Kumar Sharma reached the spot with a police force. The young man was taken to the Community Health Centre, where doctors declared him dead. Superintendent of Police Anil Singh Sisodia also reached the spot. Wife says, ‘Husband had an ongoing feud’ Sandeep's wife, Shivani, said they had a long-standing feud with people from the company and Sardars. She did not know what the dispute was about. Shivani said that her husband had been released from jail just 10 days ago. More than 16 cases, including under the Gangsters Act, robbery, the Goonda Act, theft and firing, have been registered against Sandeep. He had opened fire in Rudrapur and Bilaspur. He had been released from jail in this case after around four months. Proceedings to open a history sheet against Sandeep were also under way. SP Anil Singh said, Sandeep, alias Saniya Thakur, has a criminal history. Several cases have been registered against him. He was murdered today while going to a liquor shop. The murder appears to have been the result of an old feud. The field unit, dog squad and police teams are working on the case. The incident will be solved soon.

stories.title: Maurya says SP candidates are backing BJP:Chanting PM Modi’s name; 80 already ours, 20 also divided
stories.summary: In Prayagraj, Deputy Chief Minister Keshav Maurya said that the Samajwadi Party's candidates were on the BJP's side. They were praising Prime Minister Narendra Modi on the completion of 25 years of his service. This makes it clear that there is a split even among the SP's winning candidates. Eighty out of 100 are already ours, and it appears that the remaining 20 are divided as well. Deputy Chief Minister Keshav said this on Thursday afternoon in connection with a post by SP Rajya Sabha candidate Dhanraj Nathwani. In fact, Dhanraj Parimal Nathwani, the Samajwadi Party's candidate for the Rajya Sabha election, had praised Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Wednesday. Nathwani wrote for the Prime Minister on X: 25 years of leadership. 25 years of commitment. 25 years of the 'resolve to serve'. Read the three things Keshav Maurya said... 1. BJP winning 8 of 10 seats, meaning ‘80 out of 100 are ours’ Keshav Maurya thanked Dhanraj Nathwani for praising the Prime Minister. He said, "This is also making the Samajwadi Party's position clear." Explaining the numbers for the Rajya Sabha election, he said that the BJP was winning 8 of the 10 seats in Uttar Pradesh. He described it in his own style as, "80 out of 100 are ours." Keshav said, linking the praise for Prime Minister Modi by the Samajwadi Party candidate, "If a candidate going to the Rajya Sabha with the Samajwadi Party's support is singing the praises of Modiji's 25 years of service, it means there is a split even among the remaining 20 per cent." 2. Everything is not well within the SP The Deputy Chief Minister said there was a split even among the winning candidates in the Samajwadi Party. He claimed that all was not well within the SP either. There is an internal tussle among the party leaders. These issues are coming out in the open during the Rajya Sabha elections. 3. 'The Congress-SP alliance is no longer what it was' The Deputy Chief Minister also targeted the Samajwadi Party chief over the INDIA bloc meeting. Asked why Akhilesh Yadav did not attend the meeting, he said, “The INDIA alliance has fallen apart. The political relationship between the Congress and the Samajwadi Party is not healthy. A sham fight is going on between the two parties. This alliance is no longer what it used to be. Infighting among the parties associated with it is continuously coming to the fore.” Dhanraj is president of the Gujarat Cricket Association Dhanraj Parimal Nathwani took over as president of the Gujarat Cricket Association in 2022, succeeding Union Home Minister Amit Shah. He had earlier served as the association's vice-president. He played an important role in the construction of Narendra Modi Stadium. He is also vice-president of the Dwarka Devasthan Committee. Dhanraj's father Parimal became a Rajya Sabha MP for the fourth time three months ago Election of 2 candidates certain; 12 more MLAs needed for the third The Uttar Pradesh Legislative Assembly has a total of 403 seats. At present, 7 seats are vacant, leaving 396 MLAs. The formula to be used for the election to 10 Rajya Sabha seats will be 396/11+1. In other words, 1 will be added to the number obtained by dividing 396 by 11. This means 37 first-preference votes will be needed to elect 1 member. The Samajwadi Party currently has only 100 MLAs. Of these, Ramakant Yadav is in jail, bringing the effective number down to 99. The SP will therefore need at least 12 more votes to win the third candidate's election. The party is looking for a candidate who can bridge this gap. BJP will need six votes to get its eighth candidate elected The BJP will need at least six votes to get its eighth candidate elected. In such a situation, the counting of second- and third-preference votes becomes important. Legislators are given proper training for this. They are told which legislator should be placed as the first preference for which candidate, and who should be placed as the second and third preference. Similarly, once a candidate reaches the prescribed quota during the counting, the candidate concerned is declared elected.

stories.title: Beautician wife kills husband with lover:Buries him claiming heart attack; body dug up after 10 days in Meerut
stories.summary: In Meerut, a beautician killed her husband with the help of her lover. She then called the family and told them that he had died of a heart attack. Believing it to be a natural death, the family buried the body. However, after the deceased's mobile phone was found on 5 October, the family began suspecting the wife. When they questioned her strictly, she confessed to the murder. The incident, which took place on 28 September, occurred in Zakir Nagar Colony in Lohiya Nagar. The deceased, Talib, worked as a mason, while his wife runs a beauty parlour. Ten days after his death, at around 11:30 a.m. on Thursday, the body was exhumed in the presence of a magistrate and sent for a post-mortem examination. According to the police, further action will be taken after the post-mortem report is received. Know the full story... Talib (30), the son of Zulfiqar, a resident of Rasulpur-Dabhedi village in Muzaffarnagar, married Ilma (27), Momin's daughter and a resident of Anjum Palace in Meerut's Brahmpuri area, four years ago. They have a three-year-old daughter. Talib worked as a mason. After the marriage, he lived with his wife in a rented house in Meerut's Zakir Nagar Colony. Ilma worked at the nearby Signature Style Beauty Studio. Death occurred on 28 September On 28 September, Talib returned home from work. At around 7 p.m., Ilma used Talib's mobile phone to call his family and informed them that he had died of a heart attack. As soon as they received the information, Talib's cousin Akram, who lived in Fatehullapur, was the first to reach the house. Ilma told Akram that Talib had suddenly fallen ill after returning from work. He lay down on the bed and died a short while later. That same night, Talib's family took his body to his ancestral village, Rasulpur-Dabhedi, in Muzaffarnagar. Ilma also reached the village with the family. On 29 September, Talib's body was laid to rest. During this time, Ilma continued to weep over her husband's death. On 30 September, she returned to Meerut from her in-laws' home. Suspicion deepened after Talib's mobile phone was found After Talib's death, his family did not find the claim that he had died of a heart attack entirely convincing. For this reason, on 1 October, Talib's maternal uncle's son, Rais, went to Ilma's home in Meerut. He asked Ilma for Talib's mobile phone, but she denied having any information about it. Rais then began searching for Talib's mobile phone in the room himself. During the search, he found it under a piece of Talib's clothing. Rais switched on the phone and looked at the messages and chats on it. The phone contained conversations between Talib and Aman. In the chat, Talib had told Aman not to speak to his wife. This deepened Rais's suspicion of Ilma. He then began questioning her in front of Ilma's mother. Ilma confessed to the murder during questioning During Rais's questioning, Ilma confessed to killing her husband, Talib. She said Talib frequently assaulted her. On 28 September, he assaulted Ilma after returning from work. Angered by this, she called Aman and asked him to come to the house. Aman arrived there with a friend. According to Ilma, Aman and his friend then assaulted Talib. During the altercation, the three of them overpowered Talib. Aman then killed Talib using Ilma's dupatta. Ilma said that after the incident, Aman told her not to tell anyone. He asked her to tell the family that Talib had died of a heart attack. According to Ilma, Aman had also promised to marry her after her iddat was over. Action to be taken on the basis of the post-mortem report Kotwali Circle Officer Sangram Singh said that Talib's grave was dug up and the body was exhumed in the presence of the administration. The body has been sent for a post-mortem examination. The report is expected by the evening. Further action will be taken on the basis of the report. A large police contingent, including SDM Bhupendra Singh and CO Gajendra Singh, was present during the operation.

The loco pilot promptly applied the emergency brakes and stopped the train. The collision was so severe that the front portion of the train was damaged. The cow died on the spot. As soon as railway officials were informed of the incident, a railway team reached the spot. Employees began removing the cow from the track. The track was also inspected and cleaned. The incident took place at around 2 p.m. near Nandana Crossing in the BKT area. Railway employees began clearing the track as quickly as possible to restore train services to normal. The train remained halted for half an hour. The Vande Bharat departed from BKT for Lucknow at 2:30 p.m.

stories.title: Yogi asks, ‘Do you want likes or real life?’:Joining letters given to 470 sportspersons, including 43 SIs, 427 constables
stories.summary: Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath distributed joining letters to 470 sportspersons recruited to the police and PAC at Lok Bhavan on Thursday. They include 43 sub-inspectors and 295 constables in the civil police, along with 132 PAC constables. Yogi said, “Earlier, a ‘Dubao Alliance’ was operating in UP. It created problems for the state’s youth and ‘robbed’ them of jobs. There were only two Ss — Saifai or sifarish (recommendation) — through which one could get a job. But now there is an NDA government. NDA means — we will give jobs.” Addressing the newly recruited sub-inspectors and constables, the CM said, Do you want likes or a real life? Don’t give up your practice. India is waiting for you. Read Yogi Adityanath’s key statements 1. ‘Your journey is from jersey to uniform’ Addressing the gathering, CM Yogi congratulated all the young sportspersons on becoming part of the UP Police. He said, “Your journey has now moved from the jersey to the uniform. I have come here myself, along with a Deputy CM and a minister, to honour this journey.” Yogi said the government expects them to deliver the same kind of performance in uniform as they did in their jerseys. In sports, they learned the importance of discipline and teamwork, channelled their strength and ability in the right direction and understood the value of time. Their routine begins at 4 am, and they continue practising even in extreme cold, rain or when resources are limited. 2. ‘A government job is not a favour; it is the result of your hard work’ The CM said they did not treat challenges or family problems as obstacles and turned their hard work into a solution. He said they would have to carry the same spirit after becoming part of the UP Police. “I was looking at the figures: out of 470, 303 are men and 167 are women. Among the sub-inspectors, 43 are men and 30 are women. I want to ask — during the process through which you received your appointment letters, did anyone ask you for money? Don’t just nod your heads, say it aloud. Did you need anyone’s recommendation? Remember, this is neither the government’s favour nor my personal benevolence. It is the result of the sweat of your hard work.” 3. ‘There was no provision for direct recruitment of sportspersons earlier’ Yogi said, “In 2017, there was no provision for recruiting sportspersons directly in UP. We were helpless. But later, we started giving jobs to sportspersons through direct recruitment. So far, we have given direct recruitment to 1,000 sportspersons. Appointment letters are being given to 470 today, and preparations are underway to give appointment letters to another 500 sportspersons.” 4. ‘Play without holding back, don’t worry about a job’ Yogi said, “Earlier, one family had control over government jobs. Today, no one has control over them — only hard work and talent determine who gets a job. Under PM Modi’s leadership, we have not just set records by winning elections, but also by winning medals. Indian sportspersons won 107 medals at the Asian Games — that is a record. “Play without holding back and set new records. Don’t worry about a job; you will get one. No one can stop your promotion. If someone tries to delay your promotion, they will be removed from the way. You don’t have to be afraid. Today, no award in the state will be given simply by praising the CM from the stage. Awards will come through hard work. If you work hard, the award will come to you.” Keshav says, ‘When athletes win medals and wave the Tricolour, our chests swell with pride’ Deputy CM Keshav Prasad Maurya said, “Today is an opportunity to hand over appointment letters to sportspersons who have brought honour to the country and the state. Many of these athletes have won medals for the country and the state. When they win a medal and wave the Tricolour, our chests swell with pride. “Because of their sporting talent, they have got an opportunity to join the police service. Now they have the opportunity to turn this into an even greater opportunity. You have the chance to serve and protect the public. Your sporting journey has not ended; the game is still on.” Keshav says, ‘Sportspersons were not given attention before 2017’ Keshav said, “Before 2017, during the governments of opposition parties, law and order remained in a poor state. But today, UP’s strong law-and-order situation is being discussed across the country. This is a matter of pride. When law and order is strong, the state develops. “Earlier governments also did not pay enough attention to sports and sportspersons, which is why we did not win medals. There are talented athletes in villages. If they get an opportunity, they can outperform any sportsperson in the world. Today, nutritional support is being provided along with coaches. A two per cent quota has been provided for sportspersons in government recruitment.” DGP says, ‘Sports and police are deeply connected’ DGP Rajiv Krishna addressed the programme first. He said, "The Chief Minister's leadership has played an important role in encouraging sporting talent and providing dignified opportunities. Today's event is an example of this. Today, 470 talented players are set to become part of the UP Police." "This is not merely a recruitment figure, but an example of recognising sporting talent and connecting it with public service. Sport and the police have a deep relationship. Sport and the police teach discipline, exercise, conduct, practice and patience. Your hard work is receiving a new identity today. Alongside being known as players, you will now be known as members of the UP Police." The DGP said, "This initiative shows that talent and hard work receive the right platform in Uttar Pradesh. Players have also been given out-of-turn promotions. Players from the UP Police have won a total of 1,105 medals over the past decade. Hockey player Lalit Upadhyay and Deepti Sharma have secured positions." Sports Minister says: Government gave 17 players direct jobs Sports Minister Girish Yadav said, "Under Prime Minister Narendra Modi's guidance and Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath's leadership, athletes are beaming with confidence. The Chief Minister has taken historic decisions for athletes and fulfilled their demands. He has given a special guarantee to athletes that any player who returns after winning a medal will be given a government job. In the past nine years, every athlete who won a medal has received a government job as well as a cash prize." The prize money has also been increased twofold to threefold. Athletes are being given direct recruitment opportunities. So far, 17 athletes have been given direct government jobs. Seven athletes have been appointed as deputy superintendents of police. Jobs have also been given to athletes in posts including district panchayati raj officer. The minister said, "Earlier, athletes were unable to develop their talent because of a lack of funds. The Eklavya Sports Fund has been established for them. More than 500 athletes have so far received assistance from this fund." Girish Yadav said mini-stadiums were also being built at the development-block level. Uttar Pradesh has established a sports university for the first time. Prime Minister Narendra Modi will soon inaugurate it. Sports colleges will also be opened at the divisional level. Yogi writes: New sports culture is a picture of change Chief Minister Yogi posted on X, saying, "A new sports culture in Uttar Pradesh means recognising merit on the field, honouring achievement and giving talent an opportunity to serve the nation." Taking this culture forward, appointment letters were given to 470 players selected under the skilled players quota in the police department. The Chief Minister said, "These doors to government service opening for players are a picture of the change that the state has witnessed after 2017." Before this, the sports quota was neglected. In recruitment, there was more talk of recommendations and connections than talent.

stories.title: BJP MP posts Pakistani aircraft image on Air Force Day:Bhola Singh says it was 'poster-maker’s mistake’ amid row
stories.summary: Bulandshahr BJP MP and party national secretary Bhola Singh landed in controversy on Thursday after his Air Force Day greeting on social media featured a picture of a Pakistani F-16 fighter jet. The post showed Bhola Singh's greeting message alongside a fighter jet, with an image of the Pakistani flag visible on its rear section. The post soon went viral, prompting criticism and questions on social media. Congress spokesperson Pawan Khera also criticised the post on X, saying that a BJP MP had used a Pakistani fighter jet while extending greetings on Indian Air Force Day. Post deleted after controversy The post was later removed from social media after the controversy escalated. Speaking to Dainik Bhaskar over the phone, Bhola Singh dismissed the controversy as a technical error. He said opposition parties had no real political issues left and were therefore trying to turn a technical mistake into a political issue. F-16 developed by General Dynamics, now manufactured by Lockheed Martin The F-16 Fighting Falcon is a fourth-generation, single-engine, multirole fighter aircraft developed in the United States. General Dynamics developed and produced the aircraft in the 1970s. It is now manufactured by US defence company Lockheed Martin. The F-16 is operated by more than 25 countries, including Pakistan. Pakistan operates F-16s; Indian Air Force does not The F-16 has been one of the Pakistan Air Force's key fighter aircraft, with Pakistan operating multiple variants of the jet. The Indian Air Force does not operate the F-16. MP calls it a human error, says post was deleted immediately After the controversy grew, Bulandshahr MP Dr Bhola Singh issued a clarification, saying the use of the wrong fighter jet image was not deliberate. Speaking to a Bhaskar reporter over the phone, Singh said the mistake was made by the person who designed and edited the poster and described it as a human error. He said the post was deleted immediately after the error came to light.

stories.title: Varanasi-Vadnagar Seva Yatra concludes:Bhupendra Patel, Shivraj Singh Chouhan attend; began to mark PM’s 25 years in public service
stories.summary: The 'Varanasi to Vadnagar Seva Yatra' concluded in Vadnagar on Wednesday (7 Oct) as Prime Minister Narendra Modi completed 25 years of public service and governance. The concluding ceremony was organised under the 'Seva Sankalp Abhiyan' and was attended by several senior leaders, including Gujarat Chief Minister Bhupendra Patel, Union Agriculture Minister Shivraj Singh Chouhan and West Bengal Chief Minister Suvendu Adhikari. The leaders also felicitated bikers who participated in the yatra. Bhupendra Patel said, ‘Power was treated as a means of service’ Chief Minister Bhupendra Patel said, “Narendra Modi took charge as Gujarat Chief Minister on October 7, 2001. He treated power not as a position but as a means to serve people.” Patel claimed that policies of the Modi government had helped 25 crore people move out of poverty and that India had become one of the world's top five economies. Shivraj Singh Chouhan called it a historic achievement Union Agriculture Minister Shivraj Singh Chouhan said, “Working continuously for the poor and the country for 25 years without taking a single day's break was a historic achievement.” Praising the youth who participated in the yatra, he said, “A true youth is one who has patriotism in the heart and speed in the feet.” Shubhendu Adhikari says service yatra strengthened India's unity West Bengal Chief Minister Shubhendu Adhikari said, “The sacred land of Vadnagar had given the country a strong mass leader. The Seva Yatra connected the eastern and western parts of the country, as well as the north and south, and strengthened social harmony and national unity.” Yatra covered 10 states Around 500 bikers and service volunteers travelled through hundreds of villages and cities across 10 states, carrying out social initiatives including cleanliness drives, plantation activities and anti-drug campaigns. As part of the yatra, water from Vadnagar's Sharmishtha Lake was taken to Kashi Vishwanath. In return, the holy water brought from Varanasi was used for the abhishek of Vadnagar's historic Hatkeshwar Mahadev temple.

stories.title: Women chase down man hit him with 'chappals':Woman says his son misbehaved with a girl in Jhansi; ‘7 cases filed, 8th is fine too’
stories.summary: In Jhansi, three women severely beat the father of a man accused of molesting a girl. They chased him and hit him with their fists, feet and slippers. They struck him with slippers around 17 times in 20 seconds. A constable kept trying to protect him during the assault. When the constable said, "A counter-case will be filed," one of the women replied, "Seven have been filed; the eighth is fine too." The incident took place in the Kotwali police station area on Tuesday. A video of it emerged today. In it, the women can be heard saying, "His son molested and misbehaved with the girl. We complained to the police seven days ago. Whenever the police come to the house, they find it locked." The woman alleged that when she reached the accused's house, his father misbehaved with her. Angered by this, the women began assaulting him. The commotion continued for around half an hour. Police who reached the spot somehow brought the situation under control. Watch the video... Video showed: Constable kept trying to save him while women continued beating him Several videos showing the father of a molestation accused being beaten have emerged. In a 37-second video, women can be seen beginning to beat the accused's father after an argument escalates during a conversation. A constable tries to take him away to protect him. Meanwhile, the women chase him and hit him with slippers. A little further on, the women knock the father to the ground and beat him with kicks, punches and slippers. When he gets up once, a woman pushes him and knocks him down again. The women leave when people arrive. During this, they say, "His son molested the girl. There is a recording of it too." Student attended coaching classes, called on the pretext of an extra class According to social worker Shweta Parashar, the student attended coaching classes with the accused. He would call her on the pretext of extra classes. He would tell the student not to call her mother and threaten to fail her if she did. The accused is married and has children. He is accused of telling the student that he loved her. The student went home and told her mother everything that had happened. Accused of beating her with a belt and sticks According to Shweta, after hearing what her daughter had told her, the mother assaulted the accused. The student was then beaten with a belt, sticks and an iron rod. The student subsequently called me and sought help. I took the student to the police station. We lodged a complaint with the police and sought action in the case. We initially said that the accused should be called in front of us so that his side could be heard. They gave the police seven days to arrest the accused. The police also went to the accused's house, but found it locked. The accused had fled from home. Accused of offering to settle the matter for ₹50 lakh Shweta said that some people had suggested settling the matter for ₹50 lakh. We opposed this. A case involving the alleged exploitation of a girl cannot be settled in exchange for money. We want a fair investigation into the matter. If the investigation establishes their fault, they are ready to face action. At the same time, if the accused is found guilty, strict action should be taken against him. The accused is the student's maternal uncle by relation. They have demanded that the police investigate the entire matter and ensure justice for the student. ------------------------- - Two Pet Elephants Accompanied Woman's Final Journey: 1,500 People Arrived from 12 Villages in Sambhal, Son Said-Both Are Grief-Stricken A unique funeral procession was held in Sambhal on Wednesday evening for a 74-year-old woman. stories.title: Clash erupts between Agra police and SP workers:MP put under house arrest; protesters wear prisoner uniforms in Lucknow; burn Gyanesh Kumar’s effigy in Prayagraj
stories.summary: Samajwadi Party workers are out on the streets in Uttar Pradesh, demanding the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar. In Lucknow, SP workers are staging a protest dressed as prisoners. They are wearing handcuffs and masks depicting the Chief Election Commissioner. In Agra, SP workers had a heated exchange and jostled with the police. The police have placed SP MP Ramjilal Suman under house arrest. He said, This is not the Election Commission; it is the Modi Commission. Police personnel have come and are sitting at our house too. This is a very serious matter. It is a mockery of democracy. Security at Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar's residence has been increased in view of the protest. Gyanesh Kumar has Z-category security. In Prayagraj, SP workers tore up posters of Gyanesh Kumar and also burnt his effigy. They raised slogans of ‘Vote choron, gaddhi chhodo’.

stories.summary: BJP national president Nitin Nabin spoke to Gen-Z students in Kashi on Thursday. He said, Why are we dividing young people? There were teenagers in the past too. No one should divide them into Alpha, Beta and Gamma. Our country was, and remains, a country of young people. We will not give the rights of India's youth to infiltrators who have come from abroad. Twelve students questioned Nitin Nabin at Kashi Vidyapeeth. Responding to questions about careers, the BJP president said India would soon become a hub for AI. Uttar Pradesh has changed. Earlier, whenever Uttar Pradesh was mentioned, people spoke of mafias and murders. Now, expressways and defence corridors are being built. Earlier in the morning, he offered prayers at the Baba Vishwanath Temple. He said, ‘Rahul Gandhi and the people in the Opposition have an anarchist mindset and know only how to spread poison in society. The people of the country are watching the kind of game they are playing. The Leader of the Opposition is working to protect infiltrators.’

stories.title: Fire breaks out in 2-storey house in Baghpat, mother-daughter die:Husband injured saving them; 2 cylinders explode
stories.summary: A two-storey house caught fire in Uttar Pradesh’s Baghpat on Thursday, killing a mother and her daughter. The businessman husband suffered burn injuries while trying to rescue them. The house has a grocery shop on the ground floor. The fire reportedly started there due to a short circuit, after which two gas cylinders kept inside caught fire. Both cylinders exploded one after another, causing the fire and smoke to spread rapidly through the building. A fire brigade team reached the spot and brought the blaze under control in around 30-40 minutes. Employees entered the house using a ladder and brought out businessman Ankur Jain (40), his wife Swati (37) and their daughter Ananya (7). Police took all three to a nearby hospital in an ambulance, where Swati and Ananya succumbed to their injuries. Ankur has been referred to Delhi for treatment. The incident took place on Mubarikpur Road in Khekra town, around 17 km from the district headquarters. Pictures of the incident Full case, explained step by step Fire spread throughout the house after cylinder blasts Chief Fire Officer Amarendra Pratap Singh said two fire tenders were sent from Khekra, two from Baghpat and one from Baraut after the fire was reported at the shop. Preliminary investigation suggests a short circuit caused the fire. The fire spread throughout the house after two cylinders kept inside the shop exploded. DM orders probe into incident Baghpat DM Divyanshu Kumar said electricity department officials were called to the spot and the power supply to the area was cut off. The area has been secured and relief work is underway. An investigation into the entire incident has been ordered.

stories.title: Premanand visits Keli Kunj for first time after disciple’s death:Devotees run behind him chanting ‘Radhe-Radhe’; he stays for 10 minutes
stories.summary: Spiritual leader Premanand Maharaj visited the Keli Kunj Ashram in Vrindavan for the first time since the death of his disciple on Thursday at around 5am. As soon as devotees saw him, they began following him while chanting ‘Shri Harivansh’ and ‘Radhe-Radhe’. Premanand Maharaj stayed at the ashram for around 10 minutes. He then went to meet his guru, Shri Hit Govind Sharan Maharaj, at an ashram around 150 metres away. After the meeting, he returned to his new Yamuna Bihar Kunj Ashram. Disciple died after jumping from fourth floor Disciple Rasik Dulari Sharan died by suicide on the morning of September 25 after jumping from the fourth floor of the Keli Kunj Trust building. Four videos related to the incident have emerged so far. Police have questioned more than 50 people as part of their investigation. After the incident, Keli Kunj Ashram issued a statement saying Maharajji and all the disciples were deeply hurt. The ashram said it was cooperating with the investigation and urged people not to pay attention to rumours aimed at damaging Maharajji’s image. See 2 pictures- Now, learn about the four VIDEOS... First video: The first video of Rasik Dulari Sharan’s death emerged on September 27. It shows him apparently falling from a height of around 40 feet and landing on his feet on the road. His head then hits the ground and he begins to suffer severe injuries. Blood can be seen spreading on the road. Two cyclists pass by at the time, one of whom was a disciple wearing yellow clothes. Both appear shocked after seeing what happened. A vehicle supplying water also reaches the spot around the same time. Second video: The second video, which emerged on October 3, shows Rasik Dulari Sharan sitting on the boundary wall of the terrace. Around six seconds later, he lies down on the floor. He suddenly gets up and jumps from the boundary wall. After hearing the noise, another disciple runs to the spot and looks down from the terrace. Third video: The third video, which emerged on October 4 and is 33 seconds long, shows Rasik Dulari Sharan climbing the stairs towards the terrace. Blood stains can be seen on his dhoti. He also appears to have some difficulty walking while climbing the stairs. Fourth video: A 12-second video emerged on October 5. It shows Rasik Dulari Sharan leaving a room. He is wearing a white half-kurta and yellow dhoti, with white sandalwood paste on his forehead. He is not wearing footwear or wooden sandals. He appears to be walking slowly and unsteadily while adjusting his clothes. He then turns towards the other side of the gallery to take the stairs. Had been living in the Kripa Kunj building for three months Rasik Dulari Sharan had been living for around three months in the four-storey Guru Kripa Kunj building in Vrindavan’s Varah Ghat area. He died after jumping from the building’s terrace. According to police, he was taken to Sarvodaya Hospital in a critical condition, where he died. Eyewitnesses had claimed that he was bleeding from his private parts. A grinder with blood stains was also found in the room. A two-doctor panel conducted the post-mortem on September 26. According to the preliminary report, injuries were found on his head, legs and waist. Cuts were also found on his private parts. Took initiation from Premanand Maharaj two years ago Rasik Dulari Sharan was originally from Jabalpur in Madhya Pradesh. He moved to Vrindavan around two years ago and took initiation from Premanand Maharaj. He subsequently changed his name from Deepak Lodhi to Rasik Dulari Sharan. He was skilled in electrical work and was assigned related duties at the ashram. Deepak was the second of three siblings. He had an elder sister and a younger brother named Manish.

stories.title: AI-video showing SSB camp being blown up made, creator arrested:Pleads with Maharajganj police, says 'Did it for likes-followers'
stories.summary: A young man in Maharajganj created an AI-generated video depicting the camp of the 22nd Battalion of the Sashastra Seema Bal (SSB) on the India-Nepal border being blown up. He then posted it on Instagram. As soon as this came to light, the police and security agencies swung into action. They traced his location through digital surveillance and arrested him within 24 hours. At the police station, the accused pleaded for forgiveness. He said, "I did this to increase my likes and followers on Instagram. I will not make such a mistake again." The accused has been identified as Faiyaz Ahmed (22). He has completed a BPharma degree but is unemployed. The case is from the Parsamalik police station area, 70 km from the district headquarters. See three pictures- Understand the entire case step by step- Video removed from the account immediately During the action, the police immediately had the objectionable video removed from the accused's Instagram account. In view of the sensitivity of the case, officials have stepped up monitoring of social media activity. Action has been taken against the accused under the necessary legal provisions, and his challan has been sent to the court. Avoid misleading posts about security establishments The police have warned that creating misleading and objectionable content related to security forces, camps or sensitive locations to increase likes, views and followers on social media is a serious offence. stories.title: Thai woman pleads with husband:'No money even for food; return ₹60 lakh', Kanpur’s Irfan remarried by lying
stories.summary: An audio recording has emerged of a woman from Thailand who accused a Kanpur businessman of marrying her for a second time by lying to her. In the recording, she can be heard pleading with the businessman, Irfan. She says, ‘My financial situation is very bad. I do not even have money for food. You have a family, but I have no one here. Return my ₹60 lakh.’ Irfan then begins arguing with her. He says, ‘I am also very troubled. I am not lying. I will return the money as soon as I receive payment from the customer.’ In the recording, Irfan can also be heard evading the conversation by citing that his bank account is frozen and saying that he is at the police station. In fact, the Thai woman, Apsorn, suddenly arrived in Kanpur on Tuesday and complained to the ADCP that she had been defrauded. She said the accused had married her by lying to her and then defrauded her of ₹60 lakh. He was now distancing himself from her. The woman also accused the man of pressuring her to convert to Islam forcibly. The police subsequently arrested the accused and sent him to jail. WhatsApp call recordings and chats handed over to police Read the WhatsApp chat between Irfan and Apsorn Irfan: Everything is about the same thing again... You only think about money in every matter. You do not think about anything else. Apsorn: My life is in a very difficult situation. I have to make payments every day. I do not even have money to buy food. You have a family, but I have no one here. Irfan: I have a lot of problems too. You do not listen to me either because you are angry. Apsorn: When I message you, you do not reply. But you have time to message your friends and view their stories. Irfan: I am not lying. Improve the way you speak first. Talk calmly and I will listen to you. Apsorn: You have created problems for me. If you do not give me the money, I will come to you. I have to pay my room rent and my daughter's bike payments. If you do not return the money, I will have to pay even more. Irfan: The matter concerning KK is from a month or two ago. I did not message her; I only viewed her story. Apsorn: You are lying. If you do not give me anything, I will come. Irfan: Fine, come. Come, then we will see. Apsorn: You have created trouble for me, so I will create trouble for you too. Irfan's WhatsApp chat with the Thai woman's sister Apsorn also handed the police a recording of Irfan's WhatsApp conversation with her sister. In it, her sister is asking for her money back, while Irfan assures her that he will make the payment soon. Apsorn's sister: Am I supposed to keep waiting for my money? Irfan: As far as I can tell, your balance is 2 lakh 66 thousand in Thai currency. I know this is your money. Apsorn's sister: I deposited the money into her account. She will have to return all my money. Irfan: Don't worry, sister. My customer has confirmed the payment. You will receive the money today or tomorrow. Apsorn's sister: When will you give me the money? Irfan: As soon as the payment reaches me, I will give it to you. I understand your problem. I will try to return your money as soon as possible this month. Later, Irfan said that his account had been frozen and that he had been making repeated visits to the police station. Irfan: My wife is in hospital, so please don't message her. My money has been frozen. Give me some time and I will return your money. I have been going to the police station for the past 5-6 days because my money is stuck somewhere. After this, Irfan also sent a photograph of a sub-inspector and a picture of police personnel working on computers. Claimed he would receive ₹10 lakh, used server outage as an excuse In another conversation, Irfan referred to an ₹18 lakh deal. He said he was supposed to receive ₹10 lakh, but the other person was offering only ₹5 lakh. Irfan: I had an ₹18 lakh deal in progress. I was supposed to receive ₹10 lakh, but he was offering only ₹5 lakh. I refused. Otherwise, I would have given you ₹10 lakh today. Just give me a little more time. Apsorn's sister: You could have given ₹5 lakh. You could have paid the remaining amount two or three days later. You have put me in a very difficult situation. Irfan: I am at the bank. An amount has been debited from my account and the money has been frozen. It is stuck on the internal server. Please give me some time; I am getting it fixed. Read what Apsorn alleged in the FIR

stories.title: Missed by 1 mark, was sure of uniform this time:Ran 9 laps, collapsed and died; father weeps over body in Shamli
stories.summary: 23-year-old Vivek Kumar from Shamli suddenly developed chest pain during a PAC recruitment race in Ghaziabad. He stood on the ground for a while, holding a pole and pressing his chest, before collapsing. He was rushed to hospital, but died on the way. The incident took place at 1 p.m. on Tuesday (6 October). On the morning of 7 October, Vivek's body reached Purmafi village, around 20 km from Shamli district headquarters. The eyes of everyone who took part in the funeral procession were filled with tears. His father broke down while clinging to the body. The village elders kept repeating only one thing: Vivek used to say that he had missed selection by one mark last time and that this time he would return only after wearing the uniform. The Dainik Bhaskar team visited Vivek's village in Un tehsil. Read the full report... Father burst into tears before he could speak An eerie silence hung over the village. The elders sat on wooden platforms and charpais, talking only about Vivek. Meanwhile, seeing our team, an elderly man gestured for us to sit in an empty space nearby. In the sombre atmosphere, we somehow gathered the courage to ask about Vivek. Vivek's father, Balendra Singh, burst into tears before he could say anything. The villagers somehow managed to calm him down. A young man sitting nearby offered him water. After taking two sips, he stared silently for a while at the people coming and going along the distant road. Once he had composed himself, he began speaking. "Papa, I will definitely get the marks this time..." Farmer Balendra said, "Vivek was my only son. He would always say, 'I will definitely wear the uniform. Last time, I missed it by just one mark. This time, I will come back wearing khaki.'" The farmer father had nurtured his only son's dreams by toiling in the fields. Every day, his mother prayed that stars would shine on her son's shoulders. Incident at Govindpuri ground in Ghaziabad No one had imagined that the racing track of the 47th Battalion PAC, Govindpuram (Ghaziabad), would become the final ground of Vivek's life on 6 October. The race began, and his legs were moving swiftly towards the finish. But suddenly, his pace faltered and Vivek collapsed unconscious. Coach recognised his talent and secured his admission Vivek's story was not just that of a candidate, but also of a talented sportsperson's struggle. While studying at the village primary school, Vivek's talent blossomed as he played volleyball at a nearby ground. Coach Bharat Veer (Babla) recognised his talent and secured his admission to Veer Bahadur Sports Academy in Gorakhpur. As the family's only son, he became aware of his responsibilities. He left the sport midway and returned to the village. He then began preparing for the police recruitment exam alongside his BA studies. Villagers say that Vivek's father was also a good sportsperson. He played cricket. Coach says - Vivek was the best among 35 players Vivek's coach Bharat Veer says, "Around 35 players play volleyball in the village. Vivek was the best and most hardworking among them. He had to give up the sport because of his family, but he never lost courage. Joining the police became his sole passion. Vivek had also appeared in two other recruitment drives before the one in Ghaziabad. The previous recruitment drive was held in Pilibhit. He missed out by one mark. Friend said: Met him at the station on 4 October; he was very happy Vivek's close friend, Vivek Tomar, said that he had met Vivek at Hind Railway Station on 4 October. He was extremely excited about the recruitment. He kept saying that his preparation was complete this time and that the khaki uniform would be his. When news of Vivek's death reached the village on the night of 6 October, his family could not believe it either. His anxious father repeatedly called his son's number, but there was only ringing on the other end. When Jhinjhana (Shamli) police officially confirmed the news, the house erupted in cries of grief. Funeral held in a sombre atmosphere When Vivek's mortal remains reached Purmafi village on 7 October, the atmosphere became so sombre that even the eyes of those who had come to offer comfort filled with tears. His grieving mother and elder sister Savita were inconsolable. His last rites were performed that afternoon. Thanabhawan MLA Ashraf Ali and former MLA Rao Waris visited Vivek's home, met his family and expressed their grief. The son whom his farmer father had hoped to see in a khaki uniform was left behind forever in the race of life. Now, only stories of Vivek's games and his unfulfilled dream remain in the lanes of Purmafi village.

stories.title: Case filed against woman SI, cop in Varanasi:Victim says they entered home at night, picked up son; showed arrest next day and sent him to jail
stories.summary: A case has been registered against woman Sub-Inspector (SI) Sandhya Jaiswal and an unidentified police officer at Cholapur police station in Varanasi. The action was taken on the court's orders. The woman had alleged that the police officers entered her home on the night of 22 July and took her son away without any offence having been committed. The next day, his arrest was shown and he was sent to jail in a case. The woman has also claimed that she filed a complaint about the matter on the IGRS portal. Based on the application submitted to the court and the evidence presented, the court had directed Cholapur police to register a case. Here is what the case is about Sushila Devi, a resident of Dasnipur in the Cholapur police station area, identified herself as a Scheduled Caste woman in the application submitted to the court. She alleged that at around 3 a.m. on the night of 22 July 2026, her family members were sleeping at home. During this time, Sandhya Jaiswal, the then in-charge of Murdaha outpost, arrived at her house with two constables. It is alleged that the police officers entered the house and began abusing her, taking her son's name. They then woke her son and detained him before taking him to the police station. The woman alleges that she was also treated indecently during the incident and that casteist slurs were used against her. Put on a phone call with lawyer and told to come to the police station to discuss the matter According to Sushila Devi, she called her lawyer and had him speak to the police officers. It is alleged that the police told her during the conversation that a case had been registered against her son and that she should come to the police station to discuss the matter. The woman said that when she reached the police station, she was not immediately given any information about her son. The woman told the court that a case was registered after around 1 p.m., after her son had been taken from the house at night. He was then sent to jail on 23 July. Sushila Devi alleges that her son had committed no crime and that the police first took him from his home and later sent him to jail after showing him as arrested. Allegations linked to case involving photo editing on social media In her application, the woman also mentioned another case. According to her, she had submitted an application in court on 29 January. She alleged that Anjana Kumari, a resident of the Bhelupur police station area, was editing photographs of her and her family members and posting them on social media, thereby defaming her. Based on the complaint, a case was registered on the court's directions. Sushila Devi alleged that her son was falsely implicated in a case to benefit Anjana Kumari in this matter and to put pressure on her. Sushila Devi challenged the police action by filing an application in court. She accused the police of entering her house and taking her son away, showing his arrest later and using casteist slurs, among other allegations. Based on the evidence presented, the court directed Cholapur police to register a case against the police personnel concerned. Police registered the case under these sections Cholapur police station in-charge inspector Sadhuban Ram Gautam said that, on the court's directions, a case had been registered against sub-inspector Sandhya Jaiswal and unidentified police personnel. According to the police, the case was registered under Sections 127(2), 115(2) and 333 of the BNS and Section 3(1)(d) of the SC/ST Act, and further action is under way.

stories.title: Rain amid floods in Lucknow, Palassio Mall turns island:IIIT campus submerged, Gomti reaches disaster management office; alert in 42 cities
stories.summary: The weather has worsened again in Uttar Pradesh amid the floods. Intermittent rain has been lashing five cities, including Lucknow, Barabanki, Sitapur and Sultanpur, since morning. The Gomti river in Lucknow continues to remain in spate. The water level has been rising for the 10th consecutive day. Plasio Mall has turned into an island, while knee-deep water has accumulated on the roads around it. Water has reached Ekana Stadium and the disaster management office. The IIIT campus is also inundated. As a result, the institute has been closed until further orders and examinations have been postponed. In the Faizullaganj area, around 40,000 homes have been inundated with 5-6 feet of water for the past eight days. A rain alert has been issued for 42 districts today. Atul Singh, a scientist in Lucknow, said a western disturbance has become active over Uttar Pradesh, leading to the change in weather.

stories.title: Kanpur siblings arrested for Rs 45,000 PM housing fraud:Duped several people with fake allotment letters
stories.summary: A brother and sister accused of cheating people on the pretext of securing them houses under the Pradhan Mantri Awas Yojana have been arrested by Jajmau police in Noida. The accused took money from people by guaranteeing them housing and handed them fake allotment and possession letters. Jajmau residents Asif Mansoori and Amit Gautam had lodged a case against the accused. The investigation revealed that several people had been cheated in the same manner, following which a reward of ₹10,000 each was announced for the two accused. Non-bailable warrants had also been issued against the accused by the court. With the help of the surveillance team, police arrested Satyam Tiwari and his sister Ojस्वी Tiwari in Noida and sent them to jail. ₹45,000 taken by issuing fake allotment letters ACP Ashutosh Singh said the complainants had alleged that Rajesh Tiwari had got forms filled for the Pradhan Mantri Awas Yojana through his son Satyam Tiwari, daughter Ojasvi Tiwari and associate Naushad Ali. The accused took ₹45,000 from them, guaranteeing that they would be provided housing. They were then handed a fake allotment letter and possession letter for the housing scheme. When they learnt about this some time later, they lodged a complaint with the police. The investigation revealed that the accused had similarly taken money from other people as well, promising to arrange housing for them. ₹10,000 reward announced for each of the two The investigation confirmed the allegations, while the allotment and possession letters provided by the accused were also found to be fake. The police then announced a reward of ₹10,000 each for information leading to the arrest of Satyam Tiwari and Ojasvi Tiwari. The court also issued non-bailable warrants against both of them. With the help of the surveillance team, Jajmau police arrested both men in Noida. After presenting them in court, the police sent them to jail. Police raids are underway to find the other accused named in the case.

stories.title: 4 blackbucks die at Kanpur Zoo in 15 days:Doctor says infection spreads through tabanid flies; deaths also reported in 2015
stories.summary: The deaths of blackbucks at Kanpur Zoo show no sign of stopping. Four blackbucks have died in the past 15 days. Following the deaths, a team of wildlife experts from the Indian Veterinary Research Institute (IVRI), Izatnagar-Bareilly, reached Kanpur Zoo on Tuesday. The team inspected the blackbuck enclosure and conducted a post-mortem examination on one of the dead animals. The viscera and other samples have been taken to Bareilly for testing. In its preliminary examination, the team suspected a haemoprotozoan infection, but the actual cause of death will be clear only after the report is received. Infection spreads through fly bites Dr Mohammed Nasir of Kanpur Zoo said the infection can spread from one deer to another through a Tabanid fly. After biting an infected deer, the same fly can transmit the infection to another deer when it bites it. He said that once the infection enters the bloodstream, deer begin showing symptoms such as eating less, reduced movement and weakness. As their condition worsens, they may suddenly collapse while walking and die. Similar symptoms were also seen in Raipur in 2015 According to Dr Nasir, similar symptoms were seen among blackbucks at Nandan Van in Raipur in 2015. The deer also died around October at that time. The disease was correctly identified several months later, in February. Scientists who came to Kanpur Zoo for an investigation also said that the symptoms seen in the deer were similar to those in the incidents reported in Raipur. In view of this, the zoo administration has begun taking precautionary measures. 26 of the 87 deer vaccinated Dr Nasir said that the zoo has a total of 87 blackbucks. In view of the infection, 26 blackbucks were vaccinated on Wednesday. The remaining blackbucks are also being monitored. In addition, the blackbuck enclosure has been cleaned. Lime and medicines have also been sprayed to prevent the infection and flies. Letter sent to IVRI after deaths Dr Nasir said that in recent days, the blackbucks had been suddenly collapsing while walking and dying within a short time. Zoo doctors Nasir and Katiyar were treating the blackbucks, but after the continuous deaths, the zoo administration, considering the seriousness of the matter, decided to have the case investigated by experts from IVRI Bareilly. The zoo director sent a letter to IVRI. Following this, a team of experts reached Kanpur Zoo on Tuesday. The team included senior scientist Dr M. Karikalan, senior scientist Dr Akhilesh Kumar and technician Adarsh Kumar. The team first inspected the blackbuck enclosure. A post-mortem examination was then conducted on one of the dead blackbucks, and its viscera along with other samples were taken to Bareilly for testing. No permanent veterinary officer for one and a half years Kanpur Zoo has not had a permanent veterinary officer for around one and a half years. At present, the wildlife are being cared for by contract doctors. This has raised questions about regular health check-ups, timely treatment, vaccination and the cleanliness of the enclosures. However, the actual cause of the blackbucks' deaths will become clear only after the IVRI investigation report is received.

Gorakhpur’s Anshika wins wrestling gold in Hong Kong:Started in Class 5, now wants to train women wrestlers for India
stories.summary: International wrestler Anshika Yadav, who hails from Gorakhpur, has brought honour to the country at the international level through her hard work and dedication. She won gold after putting in an outstanding performance at the International Championship held in Hong Kong. She has also been honoured by the governor for this achievement. Anshika is the first girl from her village to take up wrestling. Seeing her ability, other girls were inspired as well. They are now undergoing wrestling training and want to represent the country like her. Anshika is currently living in Bengaluru under JSW and pursuing further training. Anshika says that she wants to help girls from villages progress in wrestling so that they can establish their identity and learn self-defence as well. Started wrestling in the fifth grade Anshika, 17, who lives in the small village of Jamouli Bazar in Chauri Chaura, said she was studying at a school in the village. When she was in the fifth grade, a kabaddi competition was organised at her school, in which she took part. During the same event, a small wrestling competition was also held. At that time, Anshika knew nothing about wrestling. Even so, she put in an outstanding performance. The teachers were very pleased to see the way she played. They felt that the girl could progress in this field. Wrestled at the village akhara Then the teachers spoke to Anshika's father. At the time, he was not willing to accept that a girl should take up wrestling. He was then persuaded. One day, he sent her to an akhara located around 3 kilometres from their home. When he saw his daughter's performance himself, he decided to support her further. Anshika practised at the same wrestling arena for a long time. Seeing her growing interest in wrestling, her father enrolled her in a sports college, where she received excellent training in wrestling alongside her studies. Guided by her coach's discipline and driven by her own dedication, Anshika first competed at the local level. Despite limited resources, she continued to progress. Gradually, she made a name for herself by competing at the state level. She then established herself at the national level as well. Anshika also represented India at an international championship held in Hong Kong and brought glory to the country by winning gold. Honoured by the Governor She has also been honoured for this by Governor Anandiben Patel. Anshika has competed at national level eight times and at international level once so far. She is currently living and training in Bengaluru under JSW's sponsorship. Inspired 15 to 20 girls to take up wrestling Anshika said she was the first girl from her village to take up wrestling. Now, inspired by her, 15 to 20 girls have also entered the field and are training in an effort to progress further. Anshika's father, Murlidhar Yadav, works for the Railways. Her mother, Malti Devi, is a homemaker. Anshika is the youngest of four siblings. Her elder sister Preeti is married, while her other sister, Pooja, is engaged to be married. Her brother, Jitendra Yadav, is a CRPF personnel. Anshika Yadav is pursuing a Bachelor of Physical Education and Sports. She will take part in the Senior State Championship on 23 October, which will be held in Gorakhpur.

Carpet with 45 lakh knots, 50 animals hidden in design:Jaipur rug made from saree waste, claimed to last 200 years; buyers from 56 countries at Bhadohi Expo
stories.summary: The 50th India Carpet Expo at Bhadohi’s Carpet Expo Mart brought together some of the most unique examples of Indian handmade carpets. A Kashmiri ‘Happy Tree of Life’ carpet made with 45 lakh knots and Jaipur carpets made from sari waste were among the biggest attractions at the expo. The expo ended on October 7. More than 400 buyers from 56 countries, including the US and Europe, visited Bhadohi to see Indian carpets. Stalls of 300 exporters and weavers from four states were set up at the expo. Weavers from Andhra Pradesh took part for the first time. ‘Happy Tree of Life’ carpet gets most attention The ‘Happy Tree of Life’ carpet made by weavers from Jammu and Kashmir was one of the biggest highlights of the expo. Made from mulberry silk, the carpet stood out for its design and fine work of 45 lakh hand-tied knots. More than 50 animals and birds, including peacocks, parrots, deer and nightingales, have been shown among the branches and leaves of the tree. From a distance, the design looks like a canvas painting, but its fine details become clear when seen up close. The shine of mulberry silk makes the design stand out even more. Kashmiri exporter Mehraj Jan said the price of a carpet depends on the fine work that goes into making it. Three weavers took 14 months to make this carpet, which measures 6x9 feet and weighs around 12 kg. The carpet uses 25 to 30 colours, making it even more special. It is part of the premium carpet range and is priced at ₹9,200 per square foot. Mehraj, who has been taking part in the India Carpet Expo for 16 years, said three generations of his family have been making carpets. He said business was good this time because of the presence of 10 BRICS countries. New buyers were also seen at the stall, with the ‘Happy Tree of Life’ carpet getting the most attention. Jaipur carpets made from sari waste Carpets at Jaipur-based Omkar Vijay’s stall were also selling quickly. What made them different was the material used to make them. These carpets are made from waste fabric left over during sari production. The material that was once treated as waste is now being sold in the market for around ₹1,000 per kg. The carpets were being presented to foreign buyers as products that can last for at least 200 years. Omkar said making these carpets is a time-consuming process. A sketch is first made on the fabric, after which sari fabric is selected according to the colour and pattern. One carpet can use up to 56 different colours, with different shades mixed to create the design. The weaving takes around four months, followed by another month of finishing. Overall, three workers take around five months to complete one carpet. Around 100 knots are woven into every square foot of the carpet. The designs are based on antique patterns that are 100 to 200 years old. Omkar, whose family has been making carpets for four generations, said around 90% of the carpets at the expo had been sold. The carpets are priced at ₹2,760 per square foot and can last around 200 years. Similar old-style antique carpets have also been used at Jaipur’s City Palace. New buyers from Russia and Türkiye also showed interest. Andhra Pradesh weaver joins expo for first time Imtiaz Ahmed from Andhra Pradesh took part in the expo for the first time. His family has been making carpets for six generations. Imtiaz said around 22 to 25 companies in Andhra Pradesh are involved in the carpet business, with around 100 to 200 people working in the trade. He said expos like this give weavers direct access to foreign buyers. “We do not have to look for new markets ourselves,” he said. Bhadohi’s tiger carpet also attracts buyers A special ‘Tiger Carpet’ at Bhadohi-based Bismillah’s stall also attracted buyers. The 6x9-foot carpet is made of pure silk and takes three to four months to complete. Bismillah said the carpet goes through 25 to 30 steps, from making the design to weaving and finishing. Different workers are involved at different stages. The carpet is priced at around ₹736 per square foot. Buyers from Belgium, France and Germany have already purchased similar carpets. The tiger design is considered a special product in the floor-covering category. US buyers look for neutral shades Aman Anand, who came to the expo from the US, said Indian carpets have good demand in the American market. He said buyers in the US prefer carpets in neutral shades. The size of homes there is also one reason for this preference. Weaver makes PM Modi’s picture on carpet Varanasi-based weaver Gyan Devi has made a carpet featuring Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s picture. She said she had met Modi in Kashi, where he spoke to her with a smile. After that meeting, she thought of making his picture on a carpet. She said the carpet took several months of hard work to complete. Gyan Devi is from Kamalgaon and does hand weaving. She earns around ₹400 a day from weaving. During the inauguration of the expo, Uttar Pradesh Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath also visited Gyan Devi’s stall and saw her work. He asked her about her earnings. The Carpet Export Promotion Council (CEPC) had invited Gyan Devi to the expo so that foreign buyers and other visitors could see how weavers make carpets by hand. Her husband, Jokhan Bind, works in colour dyeing for carpets. Gyan Devi’s story is not just about one family’s livelihood, but also shows the work of the large number of artisans whose hands have given Indian carpets their identity. Around 10 years ago, Gyan Devi was also honoured by Prime Minister Narendra Modi in Gujarat. Carpets worth up to ₹46 crore sold at expo An estimated ₹36.8 crore to ₹46 crore worth of carpets were sold at the 50th India Carpet Expo in Bhadohi. Exporters are hopeful that the presence of foreign buyers will bring more orders in the coming months. More than 212 foreign buyers and 231 buying representatives from 56 countries attended the expo, taking the total number of foreign visitors to more than 400. Artisans who deal with foreign buyers said good weaving alone is not enough for the overseas market. Buyers’ preferences for colours, designs and carpet sizes also have a major impact on business.
