Sharadiya Navratri to last 10 days; know auspicious timings:Kashi priests say Goddess arrives on elephant, departs on rooster, signalling political change
stories.summary: The grand festival of Sharadiya Navratri, dedicated to the worship of Shakti, will begin tomorrow, October 11. This year, due to a special alignment of dates, Navratri will last for 10 days. On the first day, worship of the nine forms of Goddess Durga will begin in homes and temples with the installation of the sacred kalash. According to astrologers in Kashi, the Abhijit Muhurat has special significance for the kalash installation because Chitra Nakshatra and Vaidhriti Yoga coincide with the Pratipada tithi. The kalash can be installed on Sunday between 11.20 am and 12.07 pm. As the Navami tithi will continue until the morning of October 20, havan, worship and the concluding rituals can be performed that day. Astrologers said that this time, the Goddess will arrive riding an elephant and depart riding a rooster. Her arrival on an elephant is considered a sign of prosperity, happiness and peace. Meanwhile, her departure on a rooster is believed to indicate political changes. Chant these mantras during kalash installation “Kalashasya mukhe Vishnuh kanthe Rudrah samashritah. Mule tvasya sthito Brahma madhye matriganah smritah.” Meaning: Lord Vishnu resides at the mouth of the kalash, Rudra at its neck, Brahma at its base, and all the Mother Goddesses reside in its middle. During the worship, devotees can recite the Durga Chalisa, Durga Saptashati or mantras dedicated to the Goddess. If time is limited, they can also chant Goddess Durga’s mantras and meditate on her. Perform Sandhi Puja on October 19, with a 48-minute auspicious period Astrologer Pt Rishi Dwivedi said that the transitional period between Maha Ashtami and Maha Navami holds special significance during Navratri. The final 24 minutes of the Ashtami tithi and the first 24 minutes of the Navami tithi are known as the Sandhi Kaal. Sandhi Puja is performed during this period. This year, the ritual will take place on October 19, from 10.27 am to 11.15 am. According to religious beliefs, it was during this transitional period that Goddess Durga assumed the form of Chamunda and killed the demons Chanda and Munda. Therefore, worship performed at this time is considered especially auspicious. Devotees should worship Maa Bhagwati during this period and pray for happiness, peace and the well-being of their families. Fasts can be concluded on October 20 or 21 Both Navami and Vijayadashami fall on October 20. Havan, worship and the concluding rituals can be performed on the morning of October 20, during the Navami tithi. However, devotees should follow their traditional beliefs and scriptural practices when deciding when to conclude their fasts. Religious scholar Vinay Pandey said that Navratri begins with Pratipada in the Shukla Paksha of the month of Ashwin, and the nine forms of Goddess Durga are worshipped until Navami. Because of changes in the duration of lunar dates, Navratri sometimes lasts for 8 days, 9 days or even 10 days. He said that different traditions are followed for concluding the fast. Some devotees break their fast during the Dashami tithi after havan and the concluding rituals, while others consider it appropriate to do so during the pure Dashami tithi. Therefore, devotees will have to decide whether to conclude their fast on October 20 or October 21, according to their family traditions and beliefs. Arrival on an elephant signifies prosperity, while departure on a rooster indicates political changes Dr Subhash Pandey of the Department of Astrology at Banaras Hindu University said that since Navratri begins on Sunday, Goddess Durga will arrive riding an elephant this year. In religious beliefs, an elephant is considered a symbol of good rainfall, agricultural prosperity and happiness. It is also believed to purify the environment and help devotees overcome illnesses and afflictions. Meanwhile, as Navratri concludes on Tuesday, the Goddess will depart riding a rooster, also known as a kukuta. Here are three other possible implications: 1. Stability in India and the world: The Goddess arriving on an elephant is believed to bring peace and stability to India and the world. An atmosphere of global unrest may ease, and dialogue could become possible between rival countries, potentially strengthening friendly relations. A sense of brotherhood may also spread through society. 2. Strengthening of the economy: The Goddess arriving on an elephant is also considered a symbol of wealth, prosperity and abundance. Therefore, people may experience greater financial stability after Sharadiya Navratri. Markets such as the stock market and real estate may see an upswing, while new employment opportunities may emerge. 3. Political changes: According to astrological beliefs, the Goddess departing on a rooster may bring political changes in India and across the world. These changes are considered positive. The confrontation between the ruling party and the opposition may ease, while greater stability may also emerge in global politics.

stories.title: Falahari Baba, who switched from SP to BJP, courts controversy:Questions Kohli and Premanand, apologises, spreads rumour of donation theft at Janmabhoomi
stories.summary: Dinesh Sharma, also known as Falahari Baba and president of the Shri Krishna Janmabhoomi Sangharsh Nyas, has had to apologise after claiming that ₹5 crore was paid to bring cricketer Virat Kohli and his wife, actor Anushka Sharma, to Premanand Maharaj’s ashram. Not the first time he has withdrawn a claim This is not the first time Falahari Baba has faced criticism over his statements. Earlier, he had alleged that offerings made at the Shri Krishna Janmasthan were being stolen. After office-bearers associated with the shrine responded to his allegations, he withdrew his claims, admitting that he had no evidence to substantiate them. From Samajwadi Party to BJP Around 45 years old, Falahari Baba lives in Mahmadpur village in Govardhan, Mathura. He was associated with the Samajwadi Party until 2014, after which he joined the BJP. Why did he come to be known as Falahari Baba, and which of his earlier statements have sparked controversy? Read the full report. Major controversies and statements by Falahari Baba 1. Alleged theft of temple offerings: Writes to CM Yogi in blood On June 16, 2026, Falahari Baba wrote a letter in blood to Uttar Pradesh Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath, demanding a CBI investigation into offerings received at Shri Krishna Janmasthan. He alleged that silver had been stolen from the temple over several years. According to him, CCTV cameras were switched off when donation boxes were opened, allowing money, gold, silver, diamonds and jewellery to be misappropriated. He also claimed that the wealth of people associated with the temple had increased as a result. Baba warned that he would file a petition in the Allahabad High Court if no action was taken. Baba withdraws allegations, admits lack of evidence Following the allegations, members of the temple trust came out against Baba. He later withdrew his claims, admitting that he did not have sufficient evidence to prove the alleged theft of offerings. He said a priest had informed him about the alleged theft. 2. ‘Builder lobby has infiltrated Premanand Maharaj’s ashram’ In October 2026, Falahari Baba made serious allegations about Shrihit Radha Kelikunj, the ashram of Premanand Maharaj. He claimed that a builder lobby had infiltrated the ashram and that people associated with a public relations company from Rajasthan were living there disguised as saints. Addressing Premanand Maharaj, he urged him to leave the ashram and move to Govardhan Giriraj. He also demanded a CBI investigation into the recent incidents in Vrindavan, saying only investigating agencies could establish what was happening inside the ashram. He claimed that neither he nor lower-ranking officials were allowed to enter the premises and that a high-level investigation was needed to uncover the facts. 3. ‘Mafia elements have entered your team disguised as saints’ On October 5, Falahari Baba wrote a letter to Premanand Maharaj, alleging that land mafia members had joined the saint’s team disguised as sadhus. He claimed they were selling land in the Yamuna floodplain and were involved in crimes such as the alleged theft of children’s kidneys. He urged the saint to seek a CBI investigation into the matter and said the government should provide him with Z-plus security. 4. Claims ₹5 crore was paid to bring Virat Kohli to the ashram In the letter dated October 5, Falahari Baba also claimed that a group of sadhus associated with Premanand Maharaj’s team had paid ₹5 crore to bring cricketer Virat Kohli to the saint’s ashram for a meeting. He alleged that the aim was to turn Premanand Maharaj into a celebrity. 5. Falahari Baba apologises after saints plan to boycott him On October 7, Virat Kohli denied allegations that he had been paid ₹5 crore to visit Premanand Maharaj’s ashram. In a statement, Kohli’s spokesperson described the allegations as false, baseless and factually incorrect. The spokesperson said Kohli visits the ashram to seek Premanand Maharaj’s blessings out of deep faith and respect. Following the denial, saints in Mathura held a meeting and planned to boycott Falahari Baba. On October 8, he apologised, saying, “I have never said a single word against Premanand Maharaj. I apologise to the revered Maharaj.” 6. ‘Raj Kundra’s kidney is impure; Premanand Maharaj should not accept it’ On August 14, 2025, Bollywood actress Shilpa Shetty visited Premanand Maharaj with her husband, Raj Kundra, to seek his blessings. During the visit, Kundra reportedly told the saint, “Maharaj ji, I wish you would take one of my kidneys. I want to donate it to you.” Falahari Baba later wrote a letter advising Premanand Maharaj against accepting Kundra’s kidney. He claimed that because Kundra had consumed meat and alcohol, his kidney had become “tamasic” and “impure”. 7. ‘Aniruddhacharya has no right to live in Braj’ In August 2025, religious preacher Aniruddhacharya sparked controversy over his remarks about women. During the row, Falahari Baba spoke out against him, saying he had no right to live in Braj. He alleged that Aniruddhacharya’s comments went against the traditions of Braj and the dignity of the Vyaspeeth (the seat from which religious discourses are delivered). Find out who Falahari Baba is Dinesh Sharma, also known as Falahari Baba, is around 45 years old and hails from Mahmadpur village, about 2 km from Govardhan. He comes from a farming family. His family includes his mother, wife, a daughter and a son. Sharma was associated with the Samajwadi Party until 2014. After the change of government at the Centre, he switched sides and joined the BJP in the same year. He claims that he also served as the national secretary of the BJP Kisan Morcha’s Panchayat Committee for six months in 2017. Says heart attack gave him a second chance at life, which he dedicated to God Speaking to Dainik Bhaskar, Falahari Baba said he suffered a heart attack in 2017. At the time, he prayed to God to give him another chance at life, promising to dedicate that life to the service of God. He said he recovered and subsequently devoted himself to religious work. In 2021, he filed a case in a Mathura court seeking the release of land associated with Shri Krishna Janmasthan. The matter is currently pending before the Allahabad High Court and the Supreme Court. Baba said he speaks out on public-interest issues, but some people misinterpret his statements. Vowed to give up grains, earning him the name Falahari Baba Dinesh Sharma is known as Falahari Baba because of a vow he took in 2020. He pledged not to eat grain until Shri Krishna Janmabhoomi was freed and not to wear shoes, slippers or wooden sandals. Baba claims that he has abstained from eating grain ever since and continues to walk barefoot. His vow is the reason he came to be known as Falahari Baba.

stories.title: 7 deaths in 20 days during home guard fitness test:Cardiac arrest or heat stroke? What will recruitment board do next?
stories.summary: Seven candidates have died so far during running tests for UP Police and Home Guard recruitment. Reports of deaths following the runs began emerging on September 15, when 11 candidates fell ill after a Home Guard recruitment run at Kailash Prakash Sports Stadium in Meerut. By September 20, three candidates had died. Between then and October 6, four more candidates died in Lucknow, Moradabad and Ghaziabad. The deaths were attributed to heart attacks triggered by running in extreme heat. But how can heat and humidity increase the risk of a cardiac emergency? What do professional athletes and doctors say about the possible causes? Read this UP Explainer. Question 1: Why can someone suddenly collapse and die while running? Answer: Young people who appear completely fit sometimes collapse during a run and fail to get back up. Such incidents are often described as a “heart attack” in everyday conversation, but the medical term for a sudden loss of heart function is sudden cardiac arrest. Several factors can trigger such an event during strenuous exercise. A. When the heart’s electrical system malfunctions The heart relies on electrical signals to maintain a regular rhythm. During prolonged, intense running, an abnormal heart rhythm can develop, preventing the heart from pumping blood effectively. This is known as arrhythmia. If the heart stops pumping, oxygen-rich blood no longer reaches the brain, and the person can lose consciousness within seconds. B. Sudden physical overload without adequate training Gaurav Tyagi, coach of the Meerut District Athletics Association, says many candidates begin running without sufficient preparation because they are eager to clear the recruitment test. A body accustomed only to routine walking and everyday activity may suddenly be subjected to the strain of running 4–5 km at high intensity. As the muscles work harder, they demand more oxygen and blood, forcing the heart to increase its workload. An abrupt increase in exertion can trigger a serious cardiac event, particularly in someone with an underlying health condition. C. Undiagnosed heart conditions Some young people may have an underlying heart condition without knowing it. One such condition is hypertrophic cardiomyopathy (HCM), in which the heart muscle becomes abnormally thick. It may cause few or no noticeable symptoms during everyday activities but can increase the risk of dangerous heart rhythms during intense physical exertion. D. Risks associated with stimulants and performance-enhancing substances Empty wrappers of a product called Polybion were reportedly found in large numbers near the running ground in Meerut. The product is a vitamin supplement, and concerns were raised over its possible use by candidates. However, the presence of wrappers alone does not establish that the product contributed to the deaths. Some young people also turn to energy drinks, caffeine tablets, pre-workout supplements or injectable substances in an attempt to improve stamina quickly. Depending on the substance and dose, these products may increase heart rate and blood pressure or trigger abnormal heart rhythms. Combining stimulants with strenuous exercise and heat exposure can pose additional risks. E. Dehydration and electrolyte imbalance Running in hot and humid conditions can cause heavy sweating, leading to a loss of water and essential electrolytes. Significant dehydration reduces the volume of circulating blood and can place additional strain on the cardiovascular system. As the body struggles to regulate its temperature and maintain blood circulation, the heart must work harder. Severe dehydration and electrolyte disturbances can contribute to dangerous heart rhythms and other medical emergencies, especially during intense exercise in extreme heat. Question 2: Did mismanagement by the recruitment board also contribute to the candidates’ deaths? Answer: The Uttar Pradesh Police Recruitment and Promotion Board (UPPRPB) conducts recruitment examinations for the state police, Home Guards and Provincial Armed Constabulary (PAC). After three candidates died during the recruitment test in Meerut on September 15, the board faced allegations of poor arrangements. Candidates allege lack of water, medical facilities Candidates said the running test was conducted amid heat and humidity, without adequate arrangements for drinking water or glucose. They also alleged that doctors and ambulances were unavailable to handle emergencies. According to them, the run began at around 9.40 am. Candidates’ reporting time is 5–5.30 am Under the recruitment board’s rules, candidates are required to report at the ground between 5 am and 5.30 am. After entering the venue early in the morning, they undergo biometric verification and document checks, and digital RFID chips are attached to their feet. The first batch of candidates is then sent for the running test. Board denies allegations, seeks report The recruitment board has denied the allegations. Avnish Kumar, SP (Crime) and the nodal officer for the examination in Meerut, said a report had been sought on the causes of the candidates’ deaths and the arrangements made during the physical test. Question 3: What changes did the recruitment board make to physical test rules after these deaths? Answer: The physical tests for Home Guard and police recruitment have separate running requirements for men and women. Unlike Bihar and Madhya Pradesh, Uttar Pradesh does not include activities such as the long jump, high jump or shot put in these recruitment tests. Different running requirements for Home Guards and police constables For Home Guard recruitment, male candidates must complete a 4.8-km run in 28 minutes, while female candidates must cover 2.4 km in 16 minutes. For police constable recruitment, men must complete 4.8 km in 25 minutes and women must cover 2.4 km in 14 minutes. Afternoon running tests discontinued The recruitment board has not changed the running distance or qualifying time. However, the schedule was adjusted for subsequent tests, and afternoon runs were discontinued. Candidates were asked to report an hour and a half before the time mentioned on their admit cards, with an effort to complete the runs before noon. These timing changes were made locally in Meerut. The recruitment board did not issue any such guideline. Despite the revised schedule, two candidates fell ill on September 20. Question 4: What precautions should candidates take during physical tests? Answer: Senior cardiologist Dr Rajendra Gupta recommends undergoing basic medical checks, including an ECG, blood pressure measurement and haemoglobin test, before the physical test. Candidates should also ensure adequate hydration in the 24–48 hours before the run. Along with plain water, they can have coconut water, lemon water or glucose drinks. Avoid running on an empty stomach Dr Gupta advises candidates not to run on an empty stomach. Light carbohydrate-rich foods, such as a banana or porridge, can be consumed around 90 minutes to two hours before the run. Getting sufficient sleep before the test is also important, as fatigue can increase the risk of injury and muscle strain. Question 5: Which candidates died during recruitment runs? Answer:

stories.title: BJP MLA accused of assaulting holding domestic workers hostage:Family alleges they were hung upside down, beaten with belts and sticks, and given electric shocks
stories.summary: In Moradabad, BJP MLA from Barhapur Kunwar Sushant Singh has been accused of brutally beating three young men, including two of his servants. According to one of the injured men, they were tied up with ropes and hung upside down at the MLA's palace on suspicion of theft. They were then beaten with belts and sticks. Salt was rubbed into their wounds and they were also given electric shocks. The MLA was reportedly angry over the theft of his son's gold bracelets. However, the bracelets were not recovered despite the beatings. The three young men's condition deteriorated after they were assaulted. The MLA then admitted them to his private hospital. Their families allege that they pleaded with the MLA for four days to release their sons, but were not even allowed to meet the young men. At around 10 a.m. on Friday, the families created a commotion outside the MLA's residence. They then learnt that the injured men had been admitted to hospital. See 2 pictures... Now, know the full details The MLA's son had his gold bracelets stolen Omwati Kashyap, who lives in Dilar, has six children. All of them are married. Her youngest son, Ramu, lives in the village. He sometimes works as a cook at weddings and sometimes catches fish and sells them in the market. Omwati said that her neighbours, Atul and Ravish, work at Barhapur MLA Sushant Singh's mansion, making rotis and sweeping. Four days ago, the gold bangles belonging to the MLA's son went missing. Suspecting them of theft, the MLA beat Atul and Ravish. It is alleged that the two said they had stolen the bangles and given them to Ramu. After this, the MLA's men caught Ramu and took him to the MLA's mansion in Ratoopura. Salt rubbed into wounds and electric shocks administered Omwati alleges that MLA Sushant Singh had her son Ramu hung upside down after tying him up with ropes, along with their neighbours Atul and Ravish. He then beat the three of them with sticks and belts. The MLA's guards also assaulted them. Salt was rubbed into Ramu's wounds, and he was also given electric shocks. According to Omwati, Ramu lost consciousness after the assault. He was then admitted to the MLA's private hospital. After regaining consciousness, he was beaten again. During this period, the families kept visiting the MLA's palace every day, but they were not allowed to meet the three youths. The MLA threatened them, saying, "Leave this place, or things will not end well." Omwati Arrived With a Crowd, and Her Son Was Freed Omwati said a relative who worked at the palace had told her that if she wanted to save her son, she had to somehow get him out of there, otherwise he would not survive. She then arrived at the palace on Friday with relatives and villagers. The crowd created a disturbance outside the palace. A written complaint was submitted to the police against the MLA. Ramu was then allowed to meet them. Seeing his condition, we admitted Ramu to a private hospital in Kashipur. The other two youths are being treated at a private hospital in Ratupura. According to the family, Ramu has serious injury marks all over his body. Omwati says-CO pressuring her to remove MLA's name Omwati Kashyap has alleged that the Circle Officer of Thakurdwara is pressuring her to remove the MLA's name from the complaint in exchange for ₹20 lakh. She claims that the CO is a close relative of the MLA. Despite the complaint being submitted and evidence being available, an FIR has not been registered yet. SP Rural Kunwar Akash Singh said- We received a complaint about someone being questioned over the theft. Both sides have reached a settlement.

stories.title: Bank manager kicks assistant manager, threatens to shoot him:Says he will transfer him from Bijnor to Chennai
stories.summary: An Indian Bank manager in Bijnor kicked the assistant branch manager. The incident took place on 6 October. CCTV footage of the incident emerged on Friday. The video shows a crowd inside the bank. Meanwhile, the bank manager approaches the assistant branch manager. The two exchange heated words. The manager then kicks the assistant branch manager. A guard present at the scene intervenes and tries to move the manager away. The incident took place at an Indian Bank branch in the Najibabad police station area. Police have registered a case against the bank manager and begun an investigation. See the pictures... Read the full story... According to Assistant Branch Manager Gaurav Singh, Bank Manager Sudhir Kumar had called him to the bank in connection with an investigation. He was standing inside the bank when Sudhir Kumar approached him and began arguing with him. The argument escalated. The bank manager got into a physical altercation with him and suddenly kicked him from behind, causing him to fall to the ground. The manager is accused of threatening him, saying, "I will shoot you dead. You cannot equal us." Several customers were present in the bank during the incident. The guard intervened and separated the two. The bank manager then went into his office. 'They threatened to transfer me to Chennai' Gaurav Singh alleges that he had previously been threatened with a transfer to Chennai. He also has an audio recording of this. He says that he is constantly harassed when he refuses to work against the bank's rules. False complaints were also being filed against him. CO Sunil Kumar said, “A dispute had occurred between two employees at the Indian Bank branch over a banking-related matter. The police have registered a case. The matter is being investigated.”

stories.title: Man strips naked in front of MBBS student:Follows her to class at Jhansi Medical College; security guard thrashes him
stories.summary: A man stripped in front of an MBBS student at Maharani Laxmibai Medical College in Jhansi and began making obscene gestures. The incident took place on Thursday morning. The student was going from the hostel to her class when the man followed her on a scooter and reached the classroom. He stopped her and behaved indecently. When she protested, he took off his clothes. The student panicked and began shouting loudly. Hearing her cries, a security guard and some students reached the spot. When he saw people approaching, the accused tried to flee, but the security guard caught him. The students present there beat him. On Friday, police arrested the accused following the student's complaint. The case falls under the jurisdiction of Nawabad police station. When the student did not stop, he chased her on a scooter The student, who is from Hardoi, is pursuing an MBBS degree at Jhansi Medical College. She told the police that on the morning of 8 October, she was going to class from the girls' hostel. A young man was standing on the way with a scooter. When the student approached him, he called her over with ill intentions. The student did not stop and continued ahead. The young man then followed her on his scooter and reached near her class. A little ahead of the post-mortem house, he stopped the student by positioning his scooter in her way. He then began making obscene gestures. He had also behaved indecently with other female students The student was badly frightened and began screaming loudly. Hearing her cries, other students and security guard Amit reached the spot. On seeing them, the accused tried to flee on his scooter. However, they all managed to catch him. The accused identified himself as Roshan Prajapati, son of Surendra Prajapati. He is a resident of Kochabhanwar. According to the student, the accused, Roshan, had previously behaved in a similar manner with other female students near the hostel. An oral complaint about this had also been made to the principal. The crowd beat the accused after he was caught. The security guards then took him to CMS Dr Sachin Mahour. He was later handed over to the police. The police registered a case and arrested the accused. CMS Dr Sachin Mahour said: “Whenever the hostel students came and went, a young man would often come over and behave inappropriately. He would then run away. On Thursday, he came over for the third time and made obscene gestures at the students. The students then informed the security guard, who caught him. He was subsequently handed over to the police.”

stories.title: ‘It’s just love, it won’t last forever’:Man posts status on Instagram in Mainpuri, shoots himself in chest, and dies
stories.summary: A young man shot himself dead after posting a status featuring a dialogue from the film Mirzapur in Mainpuri. He posted "Love hi toh hai, lifetime thodi rahega" as his Instagram status. He was alone at home at the time of the incident. After lying down on the bed, he placed a country-made pistol on the right side of his chest and shot himself. Hearing the gunshot, neighbours rushed to his house. They found him lying in a pool of blood on the bed inside the room. When the neighbours took him to hospital, doctors referred him to Saifai. However, he died on the way. The neighbours informed the police and the young man's family about the incident. The police then sent the body to Mainpuri District Hospital for a post-mortem examination. The incident took place in the Qazi Tola locality of the Bewar area, 30 km from the district headquarters. Two pictures related to the incident... Now read the entire incident in chronological order... Mohammad Azam, alias Shahenshah (32), a resident of Bewar, worked for a finance company in Delhi. He had gone to Jaipur for a few days for some work and returned home from there on Thursday. He had built a separate house at his maternal relatives' place and lived there with his family. According to Azam's maternal uncle, Shamshad Ali, Azam was alone at home on Friday. His mother, Mahjama, and two sisters had gone to Gursahaiganj to visit relatives, while his father and brother were in Jaipur. At around 12 p.m., the loud sound of a gunshot suddenly came from his room. Hearing the sound, neighbours ran towards the room. Azam was found lying there covered in blood. The neighbours first took him to the CHC in Bewar. He was referred from there to Saifai, but died on the way while being taken there. After receiving information about the incident, the police and family members reached the spot. The police sent the body to Mainpuri District Hospital for a post-mortem examination. 10-year-old love affair comes to light According to the family, Azam had an affair with Rubina, a resident of the Chaman Ganj neighbourhood, around 10 years ago. Around three years ago, Rubina married Ahmad, a resident of Bilhaur in Kanpur. Despite this, the two continued speaking over the phone. The family alleged that Rubina was pressuring Azam over the phone to return ₹70,000. Country-made pistol, four cartridges and mobile phone recovered from room Bewar police went to the scene and searched the room. They found a country-made pistol, a spent cartridge casing lodged in its barrel, four live cartridges, and Azam's mobile phone. The forensic team collected fingerprints and other evidence from the scene.

stories.title: Rahul admits calling Amit Shah a murderer:Says he did not intend to defame him; submits written statement in Sultanpur court
stories.summary: A hearing in the defamation case involving Home Minister Amit Shah was held at the MP/MLA court in Sultanpur on Friday. Congress MP Rahul Gandhi acknowledged that he had made a statement against Amit Shah in 2018 in good faith. Rahul said that his intention was not to defame anyone. Advocate Kashi Prasad Shukla has submitted written arguments, with paragraphs 17 and 18 referring to the incident and Rahul Gandhi's statements. Santosh Pandey, the lawyer for complainant and BJP leader Vijay Mishra, has completed his arguments. On 12 October, Rahul's lawyer Kashi Prasad Shukla will present his case. The court may then fix a date for the verdict. Vijay Mishra's lawyer Santosh Pandey said that he had argued that Rahul Gandhi had admitted to the incident and the speech. He said he had asked the court to convict Rahul Gandhi. Rahul Gandhi is out on bail in the case. Case against Rahul was filed in 2018 Vijay Mishra, a BJP leader from Sultanpur, filed a defamation case against Rahul Gandhi in the MP/MLA Court in August 2018. Mishra said, "On 8 May 2018, Rahul held a press conference in Bengaluru, Karnataka. The Congress leader had said, 'Amit Shah is an accused in a murder case. The Supreme Court mentioned this in the Judge Loya case. Therefore, I do not think Amit Shah has any credibility. The president of a party that talks about honesty and integrity is an accused in a murder case.'" During the 2018 Karnataka Assembly elections, Rahul Gandhi allegedly commented on Amit Shah, who was the BJP president at the time, at a rally in Bengaluru. Rahul Gandhi is accused of having said that the BJP talked about honest politics, but its president was an accused in a murder case. Amit Shah's name was linked to the 2005 alleged fake encounter case involving Sohrabuddin Sheikh. However, in 2014, a special CBI court in Mumbai discharged him from the case. Summoned in 2023, granted bail in 2024; statement recorded in 2026 Sultanpur's MP/MLA Court summoned Rahul Gandhi in the case on 27 November 2023. Rahul Gandhi subsequently appeared before the court on 20 February 2024 and secured bail. Two sureties of ₹25,000 each were furnished for this purpose. Rahul Gandhi's statement in the case was recorded in court on 26 July 2024. During the proceedings, he presented his defence regarding the allegations against him. Demand to match voice sample rejected Complainant Vijay Mishra had submitted a CD to the court. He had sought to have the voice recorded on it matched with Rahul Gandhi's voice sample through the Forensic Science Laboratory (FSL). The trial court rejected the application on 2 May 2026. Following this, the complainant's side filed an application in the Sessions Court. The Sessions Court also rejected it on 15 July 2026. The decision was then challenged in the High Court. In September 2026, it came to light that a petition related to matching the voice sample had been filed. Following this, proceedings on the final arguments in the case moved forward. Petitioner says he was defamed in society Petitioner Vijay Mishra said Rahul's statement had hurt him because he himself was associated with the BJP. He too had been defamed in society. Therefore, he had filed a case in court in connection with the matter. Vijay Mishra had presented two witnesses in court. As evidence, he had submitted Rahul's statement, which had been carried on YouTube and other websites. Two sections invoked against Rahul Rahul Gandhi has been booked under Sections 499 and 500 in this case. Section 499 deals with spreading false rumours about someone, making comments about them, and defaming them. Section 500 provides for punishment for defamation. Rahul could face up to two years in prison in this case. Rahul lost his Parliament membership in a defamation case Rahul Gandhi's membership of Parliament was revoked on 24 March 2023. The Surat court had sentenced him to two years in prison in a defamation case. Rahul was then the MP from Wayanad. However, his membership was later restored after the sentence was suspended. Read at the end what the Justice Loya case was about.. Justice Loya's son had described his father's death as natural. The Supreme Court had also dismissed a petition seeking an SIT investigation into the case, saying that it was a natural death. Justice Brijmohan Harikishan Loya died in Nagpur in December 2014. At the time, he had gone to the wedding of his colleague's daughter. Judge Loya was hearing the high-profile Sohrabuddin Sheikh encounter case in Gujarat. Amit Shah was an accused in the case.

stories.title: UP Politics: बृजेश पाठक का विपक्ष पर तीखा प्रहार, बोले-हारते ही कांग्रेस और इंडी गठबंधन को याद आती हैं संस्थाएं
stories.summary: Brijesh Pathak Statement: उत्तर प्रदेश के उपमुख्यमंत्री बृजेश पाठक ने कांग्रेस और इंडी गठबंधन पर निशाना साधते हुए कहा कि अब इनकी दाल नहीं गल रही है। उन्होंने आरोप लगाया कि संवैधानिक संस्थाओं पर सवाल उठाना कांग्रेस और इंडी गठबंधन की शैली बन चुकी है। पाठक के मुताबिक, जब विपक्षी दल किसी प्रदेश में चुनाव जीतते हैं तो उन्हें सब कुछ ठीक नजर आता है, लेकिन चुनाव में हार मिलने पर वही दल संवैधानिक संस्थाओं पर गड़बड़ी के आरोप लगाने लगते हैं। उन्होंने विपक्ष की इस राजनीतिक रणनीति पर सवाल उठाते हुए कहा कि चुनावी नतीजों को स्वीकार करने के बजाय संस्थाओं की कार्यप्रणाली पर सवाल उठाना उचित नहीं है।

stories.title: Lawyers hold symbolic funeral procession for Gyanesh Kumar in Varanasi:Say ‘murderer of democracy is dead’, will perform last rites after his resignation
stories.summary: Advocates held a symbolic funeral procession against Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar at the Varanasi court on Friday. They lit incense sticks and carried the body around the entire court complex. Slogans such as "Gyanesh Kumar, the killer of democracy, is dead" were raised during the procession. The advocates said that Gyanesh Kumar had been missing since the day the vote theft case came to light. They said that his funeral procession had therefore been taken out and he had been declared dead. They said that they would also hold his thirteenth-day death ceremony on the day Gyanesh Kumar resigns. Strong slogans raised; body carried around court after incense sticks were lit Varanasi's lawyers protested against Gyanesh Kumar on Friday. During the protest, the advocates carried a funeral procession through the court complex and raised slogans vigorously. Advocate Rahul Raj said, "We have declared Gyanesh Kumar dead. The people of the country have been out on the streets with their demands for so many days, while Gyanesh Kumar has remained silent to this day. In such a situation, we have declared him dead." We will consider him alive only when he addresses the nation Rahul Raj said, "If Gyanesh Kumar is alive, he should come forward, address the people of the country and explain the misuse of SIR that he carried out, as well as what he did with the votes of lakhs of people. He should say at whose behest he did this and at whose behest he murdered democracy. Only then will the people of the country consider forgiving him and decide on their future strategy. Otherwise, from today, he is dead to us." Hold elections by ballot Advocate Rahul Raj said, "We have three demands with this funeral procession: Gyanesh Kumar should resign, elections in the country should be held using ballot papers, and the SIR should be cancelled immediately. We have taken out this funeral procession with these three demands. We will hold Gyanesh Kumar's terahvin ceremony after his resignation."

stories.title: Akhilesh says CM changed airport name, public will replace him:Named it after living person, fearing nobody would remember him
stories.summary: Akhilesh Yadav said that the people would change the chief minister who keeps changing names this time in Ballia. The SP chief also took a jibe at the proposal to name the Noida airport after PM Modi. He said, "Names are given in memory of someone. It seems they do not trust that anyone will remember them in the future." Akhilesh arrived on Friday afternoon to pay tribute to late SP leader Ramgovind Chaudhary at his terahvin ceremony. Chaudhary died in Lucknow on 25 September. Akhilesh said, "Ramgovind ji's name contained the names of both Ram and Govind, the two avatars." No member of the Opposition in the Legislative Assembly had been able to respond to his sharp arguments. Asked why he had not visited the Ram temple despite going to Ayodhya, Akhilesh said, "I have told Pawan Pandey to ask a scholar for the day and date; once the Kedareswar Temple is built, we will definitely visit the Ram temple." Akhilesh had gone to Ayodhya on Thursday to attend a religious recital at the residence of Pawan Pandey, a former SP minister. Now read Akhilesh Yadav's eight key points 1. Only those in power are hypocrites Akhilesh Yadav said, "Only those in power are hypocrites. Donations were stolen in Ayodhya. The Chief Minister used to say that he would separate milk from water within 15 days. If he is so confident about Ayodhya, he should contest the election from there. If he has such confidence in the people of Ayodhya, he should take this decision and contest the next election among them." "Work in Ayodhya has not progressed at the speed expected of a double-engine government. The people of Ayodhya should not be treated with discrimination. Their shops were taken away, their houses were taken away, and their land was acquired, but they were not paid the market rate. That is why I said that if the Chief Minister is so confident about Ayodhya, he should take this decision. This is not a challenge; it is advice." 2. Sanatan teaches people to serve Sanatan Dharma is the path of truth. Sanatan is the path of service. It is the socialist path. Sanatan is the path of non-discrimination and brotherhood. Sanatan shows only one path-"Vasudhaiva Kutumbakam": that we are all living across the earth as one family; we are all one family. And those who create divisions, foster discrimination, and spread hatred in the name of religion may call themselves, on their own, by themselves, self-attested Sanatanis. Think about it: during their time, Ramdhan was stolen, and offerings were stolen. 3. Sanjay Nishad should not interfere in other matters Akhilesh Yadav went on to say that the Samajwadi Party would win more seats than ever before in the 2027 Assembly elections. Public support would be seen to be with the SP. Taking a dig at Sanjay Nishad without naming him, Akhilesh said that he should run his own bus, sort out the tickets, and not interfere in other matters. He also spoke of saving the entire state from the RTO. 4. BJP reduced its allies' bargaining power Akhilesh Yadav accused the BJP of eliminating its allies' political strength and their ability to bargain over seats. He said the allies were unable to understand the BJP's strategy. The BJP's people work more behind the scenes than the party's leaders do publicly. The BJP has reduced its allies' bargaining power to zero, and it will now have to be content with just two seats. 5. Government cornered over farmers and fertiliser problems Responding to a question about the upcoming Assembly elections and the Samajwadi Party's preparations, Akhilesh Yadav asked, "When will you ask about the BJP?" He alleged that the people of the state want to remove the government. Farmers had been assured that they would receive a fair price for their produce, but the availability of fertiliser, pesticides and DAP is not satisfactory. He also questioned the government over compensation for the damage caused by rain and floods. 6. Talk of generating atomic energy from cow dung Akhilesh said, "The government has failed to make any concrete arrangements for stray cattle. The government talks about purchasing cow urine. We had 200 litres of cow urine collected in a single day, but found no one willing to buy it. These people talk about generating nuclear energy from cow dung. Look at the BJP's thinking: they are talking about generating atomic energy from cow dung." 7. Inflation, employment and economy also come under attack Akhilesh Yadav also targeted the BJP government over inflation and the economy. Referring to the mixing of ethanol with petrol and the Narhi police station in Ballia, he raised questions. He alleged that the country's economy was under pressure from all sides, while the US and China were increasing their influence over the Indian market. Look at the condition of companies such as Wipro, HCL, and Tata. Indian companies' employees are losing their jobs in the US. No one is telling us what is happening to 'Make in India' and 'Digital India'. 8. 200 schools closed in Ballia, boats operating in Gorakhpur Akhilesh Yadav questioned the education system, claiming that primary schools had been closed in Ballia. He said, “Around 200 schools may have been closed in Ballia. The 100-number police system introduced earlier has been weakened. Tell me, there was waterlogging in the capital, Lucknow, and flooding occurred. The situation reached a point where boats had to be operated in Gorakhpur. It had been said that the Chief Minister would make the state look like Spain.”

stories.title: 8 BJP, 2 SP Rajya Sabha candidates win in UP:Nathwani skips certificate collection, Ram Gopal and Radhakant send representatives
stories.summary: The results for 10 Rajya Sabha seats in Uttar Pradesh have been announced. The BJP has won eight seats and the Samajwadi Party two. Elections for all these seats were scheduled to be held on 16 October, but no polling was conducted as there were exactly 10 candidates for the 10 seats. BJP candidates and Cabinet Minister Dharampal Singh, BJP OBC Morcha state president Prakash Pal, Shruti Gangwar, BJP state vice-president Priyanka Rawat, Vidyasagar Sonkar, Gopi Krishna Pandey, Radha Kant Ojha and state general secretary Ram Pratap Singh Chauhan have been elected unopposed. Meanwhile, Samajwadi Party national general secretary Ramgopal Yadav and industrialist Dhanraj Parimal Nathwani have also been elected unopposed. The Samajwadi Party's strength in the Rajya Sabha has increased. Until now, the party had four MPs in the Upper House: Ramgopal Yadav, Javed Ali, Ramji Lal Suman and Jaya Bachchan. Following the election of Ramgopal Yadav and Dhanraj Nathwani, the number of Samajwadi Party MPs has risen to five. Radha Kant Ojha and Ram Gopal sent representatives to collect certificates At 3 p.m. on Friday, Election Officer Ajit Kumar Verma distributed certificates in the Legislative Assembly. BJP candidates Dharampal Singh, Prakash Pal, Shruti Gangwar, Vidya Sagar Sonkar, Priyanka Rawat, Gopi Krishna Pandey and Ram Pratap Singh Chauhan collected their certificates in person. A representative collected the certificate on behalf of Radhakant Ojha. Meanwhile, former MLC Rakesh Yadav arrived to collect the certificate on behalf of Samajwadi Party MP Ram Gopal Yadav. However, he did not have an authority letter. For this reason, Returning Officer Ajit Kumar Verma initially refused to hand over the certificate to him. He arranged for the authority letter to be sent over the phone. Ram Gopal Yadav's certificate was handed over later. Industrialist Dhanraj Nathwani did not come to collect the certificate. He will arrive on 12 October. What did the Rajya Sabha MP say after his victory? Prakash Pal said, "I have been shouldering various responsibilities in the party for the past 36 years. I will now work to raise the problems of the people of the state and the country in the House. Today, the BJP has won eight of the 10 seats, and this trend will continue until the Assembly elections. The BJP will win 80% of the seats and the INDI alliance 20%." Priyanka Singh Rawat said, "An ordinary worker like me has been given a major responsibility. I have risen to a position as significant as that of a Member of Parliament. This is seen only in the BJP. The BJP is a worker-based party in which any worker can rise to any position. There is no doubt that a BJP government with a full majority will be formed in 2027." Dhanraj Nathwani wrote on X, "I am grateful to SP chief Akhilesh Yadav, who expressed unwavering faith in me. I will be fully dedicated to advancing Akhilesh's progressive vision for Uttar Pradesh's all-round development, modern infrastructure, and the bright future of its youth on the floor of Parliament. During the holy festival of Sharadiya Navratri, I will receive my certificate of victory on 12 October." Know the BJP and SP candidates... First, the BJP... 1. Dharampal Singh Dharampal Singh is a BJP MLA from the Aonla Assembly seat in Bareilly and the Animal Husbandry Minister in the Yogi Cabinet. 2. Radhakant Ojha Radhakant Ojha is a senior advocate from Prayagraj. His name also prominently emerged among the BJP's potential contenders during the Phulpur Assembly by-election in 2024. 3. Prakash Pal Prakash Pal is the state president of the BJP Backward Classes Morcha. He was given this responsibility in June 2026. He has also served as the BJP's regional president for the Kanpur-Bundelkhand region. 4. Vidyasagar Sonkar Vidyasagar Sonkar is a senior BJP leader from Jaunpur. He has previously served as a Lok Sabha MP and has also held the post of state general secretary in the BJP organisation. 5. Gopi Krishna Pandey The BJP has fielded Gopi Krishna Pandey as a Rajya Sabha candidate at this level for the first time. 6. Priyanka Singh Rawat Priyanka Singh Rawat was elected to the Lok Sabha from the Barabanki seat on a BJP ticket in 2014. She became Barabanki's first woman MP. In 2019, the BJP gave the ticket to Upendra Singh Rawat instead of her. 7. Ram Pratap Singh Chauhan In June, he was appointed the BJP's state general secretary. He was also made in-charge of western Uttar Pradesh. He served as the BJP Yuva Morcha's mandal president from 1991 to 1994. 8. Shruti Gangwar Shruti Gangwar is the daughter of Jharkhand Governor Santosh Gangwar. On 24 September, Santosh Gangwar met BJP state president Pankaj Chaudhary in Delhi. It is believed that after this meeting, his daughter Shruti Gangwar's entry into the Rajya Sabha was finalised. Now, about the SP candidates... SP candidate Dhanraj Parimal Nathwani is the Group President of Reliance Industries. He is considered close to renowned businessman Mukesh Ambani. He is also the president of the Gujarat Cricket Association. His father, Parimal Nathwani, is an Independent Rajya Sabha MP from Jharkhand. He entered the Rajya Sabha three months ago with the support of the NDA. The SP's other candidate, Prof. Ramgopal Yadav, is Akhilesh Yadav's uncle. He has been representing the SP in the Rajya Sabha continuously since the 1990s. He has also served once as a Lok Sabha MP. Ram Gopal Yadav is currently the party's principal general secretary as well.

Umashanker. Andhra Pradesh recorded a decline in cases in 2025, but Chittoor saw a rise while Anantapur and Kurnool recorded falls. stories.title: Noida airport to be renamed as Narendra Modi International Airport:Agniveers to get 20% quota and direct recruitment without exams
stories.summary: The Jewar airport in Noida will be named Narendra Modi International Airport. Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath announced this on Friday. He said the UP Cabinet had approved the proposal to rename the airport. Finance Minister Suresh Khanna said the proposal would now be sent to the central government. The name will be changed after its approval. This will be the second public establishment to be named after Modi. Earlier, on February 24, 2021, the cricket stadium in Ahmedabad, Gujarat, was renamed Narendra Modi Stadium. PM Modi inaugurated Phase 1 of Noida International Airport on March 28, 2026. The first phase includes a terminal and runway spread across 3,300 acres. The airport will handle around 12 million passengers annually. The project cost ₹11,000 crore. The Cabinet meeting, chaired by CM Yogi, was held at 11 am on Friday. It also took a major decision regarding the Agniveer scheme. Transport Minister Dayashankar Singh said: Agniveers will get 20% reservation in the police, transport, prisons and forest departments. They will also get a three-year relaxation in the age limit. They will receive joining letters directly, without having to take written or physical tests. Agniveers will get 20% reservation in the police, transport, prisons and forest departments. They will also get a three-year age relaxation and direct appointment without written or physical tests. Yogi says PM Modi and UP share a deep bond Yogi held a press conference after the Cabinet meeting. It was the first time in three years that the CM had addressed the media after a Cabinet meeting. He said a resolution congratulating PM Modi on completing 25 years of public service had been passed. Yogi said PM Modi shares a close bond with Uttar Pradesh, which has grown stronger over time. He has prioritised the state's development, helping it progress rapidly. Modi has made nation-building his goal and given India a new identity on the global stage. Read the major decisions taken by the Yogi Cabinet Free LPG cylinder before Diwali Beneficiaries of the Pradhan Mantri Ujjwala Yojana will receive a free LPG cylinder before Diwali. The Cabinet approved the continuation of the scheme to provide one free LPG cylinder each on Diwali and Holi. The government will spend ₹2,142.78 crore on the scheme. Minister Manoj Pandey said the first free cylinder would be provided between October and December 2026, and the second between January and March 2027. 1,725 AC electric buses to run in 18 cities The Yogi government will introduce 1,725 new AC electric buses in 18 cities, including Agra, Aligarh, Ayodhya, Bareilly, Firozabad, Ghaziabad, Gorakhpur, Jhansi, Kanpur, Lucknow, Mathura-Vrindavan, Meerut, Moradabad, Prayagraj, Shahjahanpur, Saharanpur, Varanasi and Noida. Private operators will run the buses, while the government will decide the fares. Currently, 743 electric buses are operating across 15 municipal corporations in the state. UP to become a global manpower hub The Cabinet approved the Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel Skill Training and Employment Zone (SVPSTPZ) Development Scheme. It aims to develop Uttar Pradesh into an ‘ultimate sourcing hub of skilled manpower’ and a ‘global manpower hub’. All 75 districts will be divided into nine zones to develop integrated skill training and employment hubs. The initiative will help connect young people with job opportunities in India and abroad. Paddy procurement target set at 6.5 million tonnes The government has set a target of procuring 6.5 million tonnes of paddy during the 2026–27 Kharif Marketing Year. Procurement in western UP will take place from October 15 to February 15, 2027, while in eastern UP it will run from November 1 to February 28, 2027. Last year, 6.2 million tonnes of paddy were procured. The procurement price of maize has been increased by ₹10 to ₹2,410 per quintal. CM Yogi approved 39 proposals at the Cabinet meeting. Integrated bus terminal to be built in Lucknow An integrated bus terminal will be developed under the public-private partnership (PPP) model in the Vrindavan Vihar Yojana area of Lucknow. The project will cost around ₹265 crore. The commercial area will be leased for 90 years, while the bus terminal will be leased for 30 years. UP AI Mission approved Artificial intelligence (AI) centres will be established in all 75 districts of the state. Three committees will oversee the mission. An apex committee will be chaired by the Chief Minister, while other committees will be formed at the chief secretary and principal secretary levels. Additional saree for Anganwadi workers The Cabinet approved a proposal to provide one additional saree to around 3.90 lakh Anganwadi workers and helpers across the state. Monthly allowance for AYUSH interns doubled The monthly stipend for interns at Ayurveda, Unani and Homoeopathy medical colleges has been increased from ₹7,500 to ₹15,000. GST interest waiver scheme approved The Cabinet also approved the state tax department's GST interest waiver scheme. New scheme for youth skill development The Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel Skill Training and Employment Zone Development Scheme was approved to establish an integrated training and employment system across all 75 districts, divided into nine zones. In the first phase, skill training and employment centres will be established in Lucknow, Kanpur, Gorakhpur, Gautam Buddh Nagar and Jhansi. The centres will provide industry-oriented training and help young people access employment opportunities in India and abroad. Bhadohi to be renamed Sant Ravidas Nagar Bhadohi The Cabinet approved a proposal to rename the district Sant Ravidas Nagar Bhadohi.

stories.title: Headmaster taps child’s head like a tabla:Mocks him in class for shaving his head; BSA suspends him
stories.summary: At a government school in Etawah, the headmaster drummed on the shaved head of a Class 4 student like a tabla. He continued laughing loudly while mocking the boy in front of the children in the classroom. The other children also laughed during the incident. After the video surfaced on Thursday, the Basic Education Officer suspended the headmaster accused in the incident. The inquiry has been handed over to the Block Education Officer. The incident took place at the primary school in Birauli, Saifai, around 25 kilometres from the district headquarters. However, it is not clear when the incident occurred. See the pictures... Read the full story... Two teachers, one education volunteer and headmaster Dinesh Kumar are posted at Primary School Birauli. The school has 76 children studying up to Class 5. Headmaster Dinesh Kumar, a resident of Unwa village, has been posted at the school since 2018-19. A child from Birauli village studies in Class 4 at the same school. For some reason, he had shaved his head. When he arrived at school after shaving his head, the headmaster called him over, began tapping his head like a tabla and made fun of him. What is shown in the 27-second video? The video shows headmaster Dinesh Kumar sitting on a chair, while the child is seated on the floor near his feet. The headmaster plays tabla music on his mobile phone and begins tapping the child's shaved head with both hands. He taps the head as though a tabla player is performing. During this, the headmaster keeps laughing loudly. His gestures also appear as though he is playing the tabla. Seeing his behaviour, the other children sitting nearby also begin laughing. The video claims that the headmaster himself had it made. Uproar after video emerges Education department officials were thrown into a commotion after the video emerged on Thursday afternoon. People on social media expressed outrage, calling the headmaster's behaviour shameful. The education department deemed it conduct unbecoming and against the student's dignity. Based on the video, District Basic Education Officer Rajesh Kumar suspended Dinesh Kumar, headteacher of Primary School Birauli, with immediate effect. During the suspension period, he has been attached to the Saifai BRC. Orders to submit inquiry report within 15 days Uday Singh Raj, Block Education Officer of Basrehar, has been appointed as the investigating officer to look into the matter. He has been directed to issue a charge sheet and submit the investigation report within 15 days. Further action will be taken on the basis of the investigation report. Headmaster says, "I am ashamed" Headmaster Dinesh Kumar said: "I am ashamed of my actions. I did not do this to hurt any child's feelings. I will apologise in writing for this." BSA Rajesh Kumar said: "Such conduct by a headmaster at a school is inappropriate. An investigation is being conducted to determine when the video was recorded. What is seen in the video appears to be correct at first sight. Action has been taken on this basis."

stories.title: Gangster shot dead by men he confronted 3 days ago:Rampur murder linked to rivalry; wife says they had a love marriage, asks what happens now
stories.summary: I left everyone for them, and now they too have left me. I had a love marriage with Sandeep. My family had already turned their backs on me. Now my husband is no longer in this world either. Where will I go with my two innocent children? This is the pain of a woman from Rampur whose husband was shot dead. On Thursday (8 October), the gangster was shot dead three times. CCTV footage of the murder has also emerged, showing the attackers opening indiscriminate fire as soon as they got out of their car. Dainik Bhaskar spoke to the deceased's wife and the friend who was with him in his final moments. Read the report... Pictures of the murder Understand the case Sandeep Chauhan, alias Sunny (30), a resident of the Sanga Farm area in Dibdiba village, worked at a rice mill. Sunny's family consists of his wife, Shivani, their nine-month-old son, Aditya, and their three-year-old daughter, Aaradhya. Sandeep's parents and the rest of the family, including his four brothers, live in Mohammadganj village in Bareilly. On Thursday morning (8 October), Sandeep took his son to get medicine after he fell ill. On the way back, he met his friend Brijesh. Sandeep parked his bike by the side of the road and got into Brijesh's car to talk. His wife went home with the child. As soon as he got out of the car, three assailants arrived on a bike and opened rapid fire. Sandeep collapsed on the spot, while the attackers fled, firing as they went. More than 16 cases, including those related to gang activity and robbery, had been registered against Sandeep. The process of opening a history sheet against him was also under way. He had been released from jail just 10 days earlier. Police said Sandeep had cornered a boy named Rummy three days earlier. He had escaped that day. Police said Rummy had carried out the murder with his accomplices. Read what the wife said Shivani said, "Four years ago, I chose Sandeep as my life partner of my own free will. I left my parental home for him. My family did not approve of my marriage and turned their backs on me. I thought Sandeep was the only person I had left. I would spend my life with him. But Sandeep's murder has destroyed my entire world." "Today, I have neither the support of my parental family nor my husband. I have a nine-month-old son in my arms and a three-year-old daughter in front of me. When I look at them, only one question comes to my mind: where will I go with them now? There were frequent quarrels and animosities at my in-laws' home as well. That is why I lived with Sandeep in a rented house in Dibdiba." She said - Fights used to break out while helping friends The cases filed against Sandeep are only related to his helping friends. He himself had never fought with anyone. He even went to jail while trying to help. I used to work earlier, but now I look after the children at home. There has been an ongoing enmity with some people for a long time. Shots had been fired from both sides in the past. I learnt over the phone that Sandeep had been under surveillance for the past three or four days. Men had been brought in from outside to kill him. I was frightened. I feared that something could happen to him. Shot in the head after he fell We were returning to our colony after getting medicine from the doctor. On the way, his friends met him near a liquor shop. He stopped to talk to them, and I came home. Meanwhile, three or four attackers arrived on a motorcycle and opened indiscriminate fire at Sandeep. He was hit by three bullets. Even after Sandeep fell, the attackers shot him in the head. The incident was carried out as part of a well-planned conspiracy. Now, my two children are all I have in my life. I do not know how we will manage to get by in the future. My only appeal to the police and administration is that all those involved in this conspiracy be arrested as soon as possible. I should be provided justice and security. Brijesh said, I had been friends with Sandeep for four years. He arrived and sat in the car. He parked his bike nearby. He was worried because the children were ill. He said he had just returned after getting medicine for his son. He had sent his wife home, and she was likely to arrive shortly. After talking for five minutes, he began getting out of the car. He had barely managed to get down when a Splendor motorcycle approached from behind. There were three people riding on it. They opened fire in rapid succession. I know one of them, Rummy. Threatening me, he said, "Get out of the car, or we will shoot you too." I stayed inside the car out of fear. As soon as they left, I called the police. I took him to the hospital with the police, but he had died. Brother said-There was no time to recover Sandeep's brother Rajiv said, "As soon as my brother got out of the car, they immediately started firing. Brijesh, who was in the car, says, 'I was suddenly in such shock that I could not understand anything or do anything. One of the attackers pointed a country-made pistol at me; otherwise, I could have driven the car over all three of them.' Brijesh first called his sister-in-law Shivani, but the call did not connect." ASP Anurag Singh said... Three days ago, Sandeep had cornered Rummy and tried to kill him. Rummy survived. Rummy killed Sandeep with the help of his associates because of this enmity. Based on a complaint filed by Sandeep's brother Rajeev, a case has been registered against Rummy, Vishal Tablet, Munna, Fauji and one unidentified person.

stories.title: 'Don't worry about criticism, if not done wrong':Premanandji says treat it as 'bitter prasad' amidst disciple's death, Kohli row
stories.summary: Amid the criticism over a disciple's death at Keli Kunj Ashram and claims that Virat Kohli was invited there after being paid ₹5 crore, Saint Premanand Maharaj said that people should not become restless if they are innocent but face criticism from society. “If you are innocent yet society begins to condemn and despise you, you should not become restless. You should regard it as God's bitter prasad. It helps destroy the ego within us,” he said. He also said that people who remain patient and control themselves during difficult times move forward on the path of devotion. They should neither lose hope nor allow their faith in God to weaken. Premanand Maharaj made these remarks on Thursday. The video emerged the same day and was uploaded to his YouTube channel, ‘Bhajan Marg’. Last month, Premanand Maharaj’s disciple Rasik Dulari Sharan died after jumping from the building of the Keli Kunj Trust. After the incident, Falahari Maharaj Dinesh Sharma claimed that money had been paid to invite Kohli to Keli Kunj Ashram. Read the key points from Saint Premanand Maharaj's satsang: Why has Premanandji's ashram been in the news in recent days? 1. Disciple jumped to his death from the fourth floor On 25 September, Rasik Dulari Sharan jumped from the fourth floor and took his own life. His last rites were performed on the banks of the Yamuna on 26 September. During this, his mother had alleged that her son was not allowed to meet her. Rasik Dulari Sharan was originally from Jabalpur in Madhya Pradesh. He had come to Vrindavan two years earlier and been initiated by Premanandji. After this, he changed his name from Deepak Lodhi to Rasik Dulari Sharan. 2. Family staged a sit-in outside the ashram after their son went missing On 2 October, a family from Hathras staged a seven-hour sit-in outside the Keli Kunj Ashram. The family alleged that their son, Anuj Chaudhary, had taken initiation from Sant Premanand Maharaj at the Keli Kunj Ashram three months earlier. He had not returned home since then. Officials assured the family that they would search for Anuj. The family then returned to Baramai Kheda village in Hathras. The next day, on 3 October, police found Anuj at an ashram in Barsana. The police then took him to Hathras and handed him over to his family. 3. Falahari Maharaj claimed: Kohli was invited to the ashram after being paid ₹5 crore On 5 October, Falahari Maharaj Dinesh Sharma, president of the Shri Krishna Janmabhoomi Sangharsh Nyas, wrote a letter to Premanandji claiming that a group of sadhus from the saint's team had invited Virat Kohli to Premanandji's court for a darshan after paying him ₹5 crore, so that Maharaj could be made a celebrity. However, Kohli had denied the allegations. On 7 October, Kohli's spokesperson said that all the allegations were false, baseless and without foundation. Kohli visits the ashram to seek Premanand Maharaj's blessings solely out of deep devotion and respect.

stories.title: Akash seen with Mayawati for the first time after returning:Placed flowers on Kanshi Ram's photograph; Aunt called him to Delhi
stories.summary: BSP supremo Mayawati paid tribute to the party's founder, Kanshi Ram, on his death anniversary on Friday. Her nephew Akash Anand was also seen with her. This was the first time Akash was seen with his aunt Mayawati after she forgave him and he returned to the party. At 9 a.m., Mayawati laid flowers at Kanshi Ram's photograph at the BSP state office. She then gestured to Akash to pay tribute. Akash stepped forward, laid flowers at the photograph, bowed and paid his respects to Kanshi Ram. According to sources, Mayawati had specifically summoned her nephew Akash from Delhi to Lucknow on Thursday night, while her brother Anand Kumar and younger nephew Ishan Anand were attending the tribute meeting in Delhi. In Lucknow, BSP state president Vishwanath Pal and national general secretary Satish Chandra Mishra were also present with Mayawati. More than one lakh BSP workers have gathered at Ambedkar Park on Kanshi Ram's death anniversary. Other programmes, including a tribute ceremony, will be held here under Vishwanath Pal's leadership. See 2 photos- Mayawati said, "He gave the oppressed the master key to power and turned them into rulers." Mayawati wrote on X: "It was Kanshi Ram who awakened the sleeping Bahujan Samaj. Through the power of the vote, he gave the master key to power to crores of Dalits, Adivasis and weaker sections who had been pushed backwards for centuries on the basis of caste. He transformed them from the oppressed into rulers." "The formation of a BSP government four times in a large state like Uttar Pradesh was the result of his mission-driven resolve. We brought to the ground the struggle for equality and parity waged by Jyotiba Phule, Narayana Guru, Chhatrapati Shahuji Maharaj and Babasaheb." Aakash also retweeted Mayawati's post. When did Mayawati assign responsibilities to Akash Anand, and when did she remove him? Here is the timeline December 10, 2023: Mayawati called a meeting of leaders from Uttar Pradesh and Uttarakhand and declared Akash, the son of her youngest brother Anand Kumar, as her successor. On May 7, 2024, Mayawati stripped him of all responsibilities over his controversial remarks. She removed him as both her successor and the national coordinator, saying Akash was still immature. June 23, 2024: After 47 days, Mayawati reversed her decision and reinstated Akash as her successor, assigning him the role of national coordinator again. However, on March 2, 2025, she once again stripped him of all responsibilities. March 3, 2025: Mayawati expelled Akash from the party. She said he should have shown maturity through remorse but had become selfish and arrogant under the influence of his father-in-law. April 13, 2026: Mayawati forgave Akash but said she would not make him her successor. Three months later, on May 18, she reappointed him as chief national coordinator, saying he was being given a second chance. On August 29, the party created a new post of national coordinator and assigned the responsibility to Akash. September 3: Mayawati removed Akash from the post of national coordinator, saying he needed to become more mature. September 9: Mayawati set a condition for restoring Akash's responsibilities: his father-in-law would have to retire from political life. September 10: Mayawati expelled Akash from the party. A few hours later, his father-in-law, Ashok Siddharth, announced his retirement from politics. Akash entered politics in 2017 In 2017, Akash was seen alongside Mayawati at a public meeting in Saharanpur. After that, he continued working for the party. In 2019, he was appointed national coordinator. Later, the BSP-SP alliance broke down. At the time, reports emerged that Mayawati had ended the alliance at Akash's suggestion. Akash's name appeared on the list of star campaigners for the 2022 Himachal Pradesh Assembly elections for the first time. He holds an MBA degree from London.

stories.title: Govt should consider relocating industrial areas away from rivers:SC orders probe into illegal industries’ financial transactions and entire network
stories.summary: In a case concerning the pollution and conservation of the Jojari-Bandi-Luni river system in Rajasthan, the Supreme Court has issued strict directions to the state government and the concerned authorities. A bench comprising Supreme Court Justices Vikram Nath and Sandeep Mehta said that the problems affecting the river system were not limited to violations by individual industrial units, but stemmed from broader issues such as inadequate treatment capacity, illegal industrial activities, irregularities in land use and a lack of effective monitoring. The Supreme Court also directed that an assessment be carried out to consider relocating the industrial area situated near the river to another location. It further directed an investigation into the entire network of illegal industrial units operating on residential and agricultural land. The Supreme Court directed that all illegal or unauthorised discharge points, bypass arrangements, manholes, chambers, pipelines and drains that have been identified and for which permission for removal has already been granted be sealed, intercepted or removed without delay. The completion of a comprehensive survey will not be awaited for this. The officials concerned will have to physically verify the action taken on the ground and submit an action-taken report to the committee every 15 days. Comprehensive action to be taken against illegal industrial units The court has directed comprehensive action against industrial units operating illegally on agricultural and residential land. If any such unit is found, action will not be limited to the unit itself; the network of financial transactions, job work, raw materials, transportation and beneficiaries linked to it will also be investigated. The directions include taking revenue and land-use-related action concerning the land, removing or seizing machinery, restoring the affected land and initiating prosecution in accordance with the law. Permanent monitoring system in every district The Supreme Court has directed the Rajasthan government to establish permanent and district-level coordinated mechanisms to prevent illegal industrial activities that cause pollution. These mechanisms will include the Rajasthan State Pollution Control Board, district administration, police, revenue, transport, local bodies and other concerned departments. The court has directed that arrangements be made for regular monitoring, designated nodal officers and time-bound action. Advocate Rishabh Sancheti represented the Jodhpur Pollution Control and Research Foundation. Directions to recover environmental compensation The Rajasthan State Pollution Control Board has been directed to begin the process of assessing and actually recovering environmental compensation from the concerned industrial units and responsible persons for the entire period of the violations. The board will also have to state how much compensation was assessed, how much was recovered and how much remains outstanding. The court has directed that decisions on proposals concerning the expansion of the existing Common Effluent Treatment Plant (CETP), the establishment of a new CETP, and the upgrading of Effluent Treatment Plants (ETPs) at industrial units to a Zero Liquid Discharge (JLD) system be taken within the stipulated timeframe. It has also directed that the approved seven-MLD CETP (JLD) in Pali's RIICO Industrial Area be commissioned immediately and in phases. The processes of tendering, issuing the work order, construction, commissioning and stabilisation must be completed without unnecessary administrative delays. Crackdown on illegal gravel mining too The Supreme Court has directed immediate action against illegal and unauthorised gravel and sand mining affecting riverbeds, riverbanks and natural water flow. The committee has been asked to be provided with complete information on mining areas, leases, permitted quantities, mining depths, replenishment and restoration obligations. This information must be submitted by 15 October 2026. Bridges over the Joji, Bandi and Luni rivers to undergo technical inspection The court has also directed a comprehensive technical inspection of bridges and road crossings built over the Luni, Joji and Bandi river systems and their tributaries. Structures that obstruct or could obstruct the rivers' natural flow will be identified. Artificial obstructions will be removed as necessary, and measures will be taken to protect the rivers' natural flow during construction in the future. Possibility of relocating industrial areas to also be examined The Supreme Court has asked the state government to conduct a comprehensive assessment of the feasibility of relocating polluting industrial areas located in close proximity to the Luni, Joji and Bandi river systems to suitable locations. The assessment will take into account the rivers' environmental sensitivity, carrying capacity, the availability of treatment facilities, the possibility of ZLD and the long-term interests of affected communities. State to present a comprehensive solution plan The court directed the Rajasthan government to consider the committee's observations and concerns, finalise a comprehensive solution plan, and include clear timelines, responsible departments and defined targets to measure progress. The next hearing in the case will be held on 26 October.

stories.title: Large motorboats resume in Kashi today:Tourists can view 84 ghats from Ganga; life jackets mandatory
stories.summary: There is relief for tourists and devotees visiting Kashi. After the Ganga's water level fell and conditions improved, the operation of large motor boats in Varanasi was permitted from Friday. Tourists and devotees will now be able to board motor boats on the Ganga and see Kashi's 84 ghats. However, the ban on operating hand-rowed boats will remain in place for now for safety reasons. ACP Dashashwamedh Dr Atul Anjaan Tripathi said that motor boats would be allowed to operate only from 6 a.m. to 5 p.m. Action will be taken against those operating boats outside the prescribed hours or violating safety rules. Two boatmen trained in swimming on every boat The administration has set strict rules to ensure the safety of passengers on motorboats. Each boat must have at least two boatmen trained in swimming. All passengers and pilgrims on board must wear life jackets. No one will be allowed to travel without a life jacket. Instructions have also been issued regarding the number of passengers on motorboats. Boats will be allowed to carry only half their prescribed capacity. The aim is to prevent overloading and ensure passengers' safety in an emergency. Keeping ropes, life buoys and other safety equipment is mandatory Every motorboat must have ropes, a life buoy and other essential safety equipment. Boatmen have been instructed to prioritise passenger safety and comply with all standards set by the administration. Operations may be suspended again if the water level rises Boat operations had been halted in recent days because the Ganga's water level was rising and weather conditions were unfavourable. Now, after conditions improved, permission has been granted to operate large motorboats. However, the administration has made it clear that if the Ganga's water level rises again or the weather deteriorates, the situation may be reviewed and a decision taken to halt operations again.
