stories.title: ₹50,000 fine on doctors who beat attendants:Clash breaks out at Gorakhpur’s BRD Medical College
stories.summary: BRD Medical College administration in Gorakhpur has taken strict action over a dispute between patients' attendants and junior doctors at Nehru Hospital. The altercation took place on Tuesday night after the death of a patient injured in a road accident, when the attendants demanded that a post-mortem examination be conducted. Fines ranging from ₹25,000 to ₹50,000 have been imposed on the six junior doctors involved in the incident. All six junior doctors have also been suspended for one week. To prevent a recurrence, the college administration has decided that the accused junior doctors will undergo psychiatric counselling every week for one month. They have also been made to submit written affidavits stating that such incidents will not happen again. CCTV footage became the basis of the investigation All six accused junior doctors were summoned before the committee formed to investigate the dispute that took place late on Tuesday night. CCTV footage was also examined during the investigation. Based on the footage, none of the accused was able to deny their role in the incident. A fine of ₹50,000 each has been imposed on the three main accused junior doctors, while the three other junior doctors who supported them have each been fined ₹25,000. All of them have given a written assurance that such an incident will not recur in the future. Accused doctors to undergo counselling The college administration has not limited the matter to punitive action alone. Along with arranging regular counselling for the accused junior doctors, it has also decided to send new students for soft-skills training and counselling sessions. The aim is to prepare doctors to communicate with patients and their attendants and to handle stressful situations more effectively. The junior doctors had also lodged a complaint against the patients' attendants. They alleged that a large number of attendants had gathered in the corridor of the medicine ward and that one attendant had tried to grab and pull a female junior doctor by the hand. They said this was what led to the situation worsening. The college administration has also taken this aspect seriously. Questions have also been raised over the role of the security guard deployed at the time of the incident. The administration has written to the Sainik Welfare Corporation seeking the removal of the guard deployed at the scene. The administration says 15 guards were deployed there. The guard posted at the Medicine Ward gate was responsible for preventing attendants from entering the gallery and calling another guard for help. Victim files complaint against doctors The investigation into the assault on an attendant at BRD Medical College is now proceeding on the basis of a viral video and the complaint filed by the victim. Injured Ajay Singh has filed a complaint with Gulhariya police, making several serious allegations, including assault, against junior doctors and other staff members. He has also provided the police with a video related to the incident. The police are investigating the authenticity of the video and the sequence of events shown in it. According to injured Ajay Singh, a resident of Semra in the Gulhariya area, a dispute broke out over a demand for a post-mortem examination after the death of his relative, Umakant Chaudhary. During the incident, the doctors and staff members closed the channel gate of the gallery in Ward No. 11 and assaulted him. Full details of the case Umakant Chaudhary, a resident of Tenuhारी Soyam village in the Kotwali police station area of Sant Kabir Nagar, was injured in a road accident on 3 October. He was referred to BRD Medical College after receiving primary treatment at the district hospital. At the medical college, he was admitted to Ward 11 of the Medicine Emergency department because of a head injury. He died during treatment at around 12 midnight on Tuesday. According to the attendants, the junior doctors on duty issued a death certificate and told them to take the body home. The attendants demanded a post-mortem because the death had occurred in a road accident. This led to a heated argument between the two sides. Attendants alleged that as the dispute escalated, the channel gate of the gallery in Ward No. 11 was closed and they were assaulted. A video of the incident is going viral on social media. Police brought the situation under control The dispute continued until around 2 a.m. on Tuesday night. On receiving the information, police reached the spot and brought the matter under control after speaking to both sides. A memo was then prepared for the post-mortem and sent to Gulriha police. The medical college administration had formed a three-member committee to investigate the entire matter. Action was taken against the doctors after its report was submitted. In this connection, BRD Medical College Principal Dr Dharmendra Kumar said that the incident was reviewed before the inquiry committee on the basis of CCTV footage. Action has been taken against six junior doctors.

stories.title: Hailstorm in western UP, floods in Lucknow:8 Gonda villages submerged, 13 houses swept away in Lakhimpur
stories.summary: The weather suddenly changed across western Uttar Pradesh on Friday morning. Meerut witnessed heavy rain accompanied by hail. In Muzaffarnagar, hailstones the size of peas fell without any rain. The weather department has issued a thunderstorm and rain alert for eight districts today. Meanwhile, floods continue to cause trouble across the state. In Lucknow, the water level of the Gomti river has been rising for the 11th consecutive day. Roads in VIP areas have been submerged. Water has entered several temples, including Lete Hanuman and Hanumant Dham. The Riverfront has been closed until further orders. Water has reached neck level in the lanes of Faizullaganj. More than 40,000 houses are over half submerged, affecting a population of over 3 lakh. The Ghaghara river is in spate in Gonda, with floodwater entering eight villages. More than 7,000 people are stranded in the flood. In Lakhimpur Kheri, the Sharda river is causing severe erosion. So far, 13 houses and four temples have been washed away into the river.

stories.title: 6.45 lakh voters removed in Gorakhpur to be verified:BLOs to visit every voter’s home to check current status
stories.summary: After the completion of the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of the electoral roll, voters who were left out of the final voter list published on 10 April 2026 or whose names were deleted will be verified again. The list published on 7 January 2025, before the SIR, will be compared with it. The names included in the earlier list but missing from the post-SIR list will be verified. Their number is approximately 6,45,000. A booth-level list of all such voters will be given to Booth Level Officers (BLOs), who will visit their homes and verify them. During the verification, the current status of those whose names are missing from the later list will be checked. Those found to be eligible will be asked to fill out Form 6. Verification must be completed within a month The verification campaign will continue for a month. During this period, young people who have turned 18 will also be registered as voters. Within a month, all voters will be verified and a list will be prepared, recording their current status. The names of those who have been made to fill out Form 6 will also be included in this list. It will be shared with representatives of political parties. Camps to be held in homeless and workers' settlements too The campaign will not be limited to door-to-door verification. Camps will be set up at the booth level to add names to the electoral roll. Special camps will be organised for people staying in night shelters, workers' settlements, those who are homeless and those living outside the mainstream of society. Information about the process of getting names added will also be provided through educational institutions, public outreach, SVEEP activities and press briefings. The District Election Officer and Electoral Registration Officer will regularly review and monitor the campaign. How many voters were there before and after SIR? Gorakhpur had more than 36.66 lakh voters before the SIR. The campaign removed more than 6.45 lakh names. A large number of them were people who were voters but could not provide the necessary information or records linked to their own names or those of their parents or grandparents in the 2003 electoral roll. Figures released at the district level after the SIR showed that 6,45,634 names had been removed and that the number of voters had fallen to 30,20,908. During the SIR, providing details of the 2003 records through a declaration form along with Form 6 had become important. The removal of this additional requirement may now provide relief to people who had been getting stuck in the application process because they did not have information about old family records. Chillupar saw the highest number of deletions Constituency-wise, Chillupar saw the highest number of deletions, with 87,732 names removed. It was followed by Bansgaon, where 83,062 names were removed, and Khajni, where 83,014 names were removed. The number of names removed was 70,763 in Gorakhpur Rural, 68,242 in Campierganj, 67,355 in Chauri Chaura, 62,175 in Pipraich, 62,152 in Gorakhpur City and 61,130 in Sahjanwa.

stories.title: 'You’re beautiful, my wife can’t make me happy':Home guard commander accused of rape; woman threatens suicide
stories.summary: A woman in Uttar Pradesh's Jaunpur has accused a Home Guard platoon commander of sexually assaulting her over eight years and threatening to kill her husband and children if she refused to comply. She has alleged that he exploited her financial difficulties and forced her to continue the relationship against her will. “If I do not get justice, I will set myself on fire outside the Chief Minister's residence in Lucknow,” the woman said. She also alleged that the accused was pressuring her to change her statement after she approached the police. The case relates to the Badlapur police station area, around 38 km from the Jaunpur district headquarters. The woman approached the police on October 7, according to the report. Dainik Bhaskar spoke to her over the phone. Woman says accused took advantage of her financial difficulties The accused, Dharmendra Sharma, alias Makrand, 44, lives in Sarokhanpur and works as a Home Guard platoon commander in Badlapur. He lives with his wife, two daughters and a son. The woman lives nearby with her husband and children. The woman said she married in 2017 and was struggling financially after moving to her marital home. Her family owed around ₹3,000 for milk supplied by the accused's household. She said the accused offered her work at his house, promising to pay her ₹12,000 a month. She began looking after livestock and also worked at his house and fields. “I thought that if I found some work, I could help with the household expenses. Dharmendra told me to work at his house and promised to pay me ₹12,000 a month,” she said. She alleged that she worked at his house and fields for three years but was never paid the full amount. 'You look very beautiful': Woman alleges sexual abuse The woman alleged that the accused began making inappropriate remarks and pressuring her to enter into a sexual relationship. “He used to tell me, ‘You look very beautiful. Get into a relationship with me. I will help you,’” she said. She alleged that he exploited her financial circumstances and sexually assaulted her against her will. She said she became pregnant in 2019 as a result of the alleged relationship. The woman said she told her husband that the accused was harassing her. According to her, the accused continued to trouble her, including by entering her house at night. She alleged that when her husband objected, the accused became aggressive and threatened those who intervened. 'He threatened to kill my husband and children' The woman said she eventually asked the accused to leave her alone, but he threatened her family. “When I told him that enough was enough and asked him to leave me alone, he said that if I did not have physical relations with him, he would kill my husband and me,” she alleged. She said she continued to comply because she feared for her husband and children's lives. She also alleged that when she went to her parental home to escape the harassment, the accused threatened to kill her husband if she did not return. “He used to say, ‘I feel satisfied with you. My wife cannot keep me happy. I will stay with you,’” she said. The woman said the accused was married and had two daughters, aged 17 and 18, and a 16-year-old son. Woman alleges accused smashed her phone The woman said she suffered a miscarriage in February this year. Despite her poor health, she alleged, the accused continued to pressure her for sex. She said she had recorded videos to support her account and establish her innocence. When she warned the accused that she had evidence against him and would take it to the police, he allegedly assaulted her and smashed her phone, destroying the recordings. “I had complained against him three times. Every time, he would say that the police station was in his pocket and that I could do nothing against him,” she alleged. The woman said the accused assaulted her again on the night of October 5, prompting her to approach the police. Woman claims she is being pressured to change statement The woman alleged that after she filed the complaint, the accused called village residents and pressured her to change her statement. She also claimed that he took ₹2.85 lakh from a self-help group and had not returned the money. “My husband is also no longer willing to keep me with him after learning everything. If he goes to jail, his family is capable of getting him released immediately. But my children's future and mine have been ruined,” she said. The woman said she had attempted suicide three times in the past and threatened to set herself on fire outside the Chief Minister's residence in Lucknow if she did not get justice. Police say dispute was over money, both parties reached settlement Badlapur police station in-charge Phoolchand Pandey said the dispute was related to a financial transaction. “There was a dispute over a monetary transaction. The woman had lodged a complaint earlier, and a case was registered under those sections. Both parties have now reached a settlement. A final report (FR) will be filed in the FIR case,” Pandey said. The police statement differs from the woman's allegations of prolonged sexual abuse, threats and pressure to withdraw her complaint. The status of the FIR and the proposed final report should be verified before publication.

Bundelkhand gets heavy rain instead of Purvanchal:2-day rain equals monthly quota; drought-hit areas now flooded; 8-year analysis
stories.summary: The pattern of monsoon rainfall in Uttar Pradesh is changing. Until 8 years ago, eastern UP received more rainfall, while western UP and Bundelkhand often received less. But the picture has now changed. Areas that traditionally received less rainfall, such as Mahoba, Jalaun and Banda, are now recording “very heavy rainfall”. Here, the monthly rainfall quota is being met within just 2-4 days. The pattern of rainfall across the state has also changed. This is creating flood-like conditions in some areas and drought-like conditions in others. Dainik Bhaskar analysed 8 years of monsoon rainfall data in UP from 2019 to 2026. The analysis revealed 4 major changes in the rainfall pattern. The biggest change is visible in the difference in rainfall between eastern and western UP. Read the report… First change: Rainfall pattern changed rapidly after 2022 The past 50 years of monsoon rainfall data (LPA) show that eastern UP has received more rainfall than the western part. Eastern UP has received an average of 799.2 mm of rainfall, while Western UP has received 672 mm. However, this pattern appears to have changed over the past 8 years. According to the IMD, eastern UP received 7% more than average rainfall in 2019, at 852.4 mm. In comparison, western UP received only 523.8 mm, which was 20% below average. In 2020, when eastern UP received 2% less rainfall, the rainfall deficit in western UP was 32%. However, in 2022, the two regions were almost at par. After that, the situation gradually reversed. In 2023, western UP came close to normal rainfall with 696.2 mm, while eastern UP remained at 567.3 mm, or 29% below average. In 2024, rainfall in both regions was almost equal. In 2025, western UP received 12% more rainfall than average, while eastern UP received 17% less. In 2026, western UP received 16% more rainfall, while eastern UP received only 2% more. If we look at the figures district-wise, the picture becomes even clearer. Of the 33 districts in western UP, 12 received below-average rainfall, while 25 of the 42 districts in eastern UP faced a rainfall deficit. Second change: Heavy rainfall in traditionally water-deficient Bundelkhand The biggest change is visible in Bundelkhand. Mahoba is the clearest example. The region receives an average of 597.9 mm of rainfall during the monsoon season. In 2019, it received 518.2 mm. However, in 2026, it received 1,127 mm of rainfall, which was 88% above average. Banda has an average rainfall of 767.1 mm. This year, it received 1,348.4 mm, which was 76% above normal. It also received 41% more rainfall in 2025. Chitrakoot received 1,358.1 mm of rainfall, which was 73% above normal. Hamirpur is another example of this change. It receives an average of 708 mm of rainfall. In 2026, it received 1,307.7 mm, which was 85% above normal. Overall, Bundelkhand, which is traditionally associated with low rainfall and drought, is now receiving much more rainfall than average. This trend has been clearly visible since 2022. However, it would be premature to say that the weather in Bundelkhand has permanently changed. Eight years of data is not conclusive evidence of climate change. But it does show that even areas traditionally affected by rainfall deficits are now experiencing very heavy rainfall in some years. Third change: Rainfall decreased in June-July, August-September made up the deficit The timing of the monsoon in UP, meaning how much rainfall the state receives in each month, also appears to be changing. According to an IMD study covering 20 years from 2001-2020, the normal pattern in UP was for July to receive the highest rainfall. On average, around 34% of monsoon rainfall occurred in July and 31% in August. However, the data from 2019 to 2026 shows that the share of August and September is increasing. In 2019, only 40.2 mm of rain was recorded in June. This was followed by 296.9 mm in July, 169.1 mm in August and 213.8 mm in September. This means a large share of the year’s rainfall came after July. The change became more evident from 2022. That year, only 193 mm of rainfall was recorded in June-July, while August-September received 340.5 mm. This means around 64% of the rainfall came in the final two months. In 2023, 52% of the monsoon quota was received in August-September. In 2024, this figure reached 60%. The trend became even stronger in 2026. By July 31, rainfall was 27% below average, and August-September made up the deficit. By the end of the season, UP had recorded 8% more rainfall than average. Over these 8 years, only 2020 and 2025 saw consistent and good rainfall from June to September. The overall indication is that the monsoon appears to be shifting from June-July towards August-September. However, years such as 2020 and 2025 also show a different pattern. Therefore, it would be premature to call this a permanent change in the monsoon pattern. Fourth change: Monthly rainfall quota being met within 2-4 days The way monsoon rainfall occurs in UP is also changing. The number of rainy days is decreasing, while dry spells are increasing. On the other hand, when it does rain, a large amount of water often falls within a short period. This means the number of days on which rainfall is spread across the monsoon season has decreased. But within a few hours or 1-2 days, rainfall equivalent to an entire month can occur. For example: In 2020 and 2021, several districts experienced such intense rainfall an average of 3-5 times, fulfilling 30-50% of their monthly rainfall quota. In 2022, more than 60% of September’s rainfall was received through heavy rain over 2-3 days. In September 2023, there were 3-4 days when western UP and the Terai areas recorded up to 180 mm of heavy rainfall in 24 hours. In 2024 and 2026, several such days were recorded in eastern and western UP when 30-40% of the monthly quota was met in a single day. In September 2026, there were 4-5 such days when up to 245 mm of rainfall was recorded within 24-48 hours. Historically, eastern UP was known for heavy rainfall. However, over the past 8 years, the number of days with heavy rainfall has increased in parts of western UP and Bundelkhand. Due to the changing pattern, the total rainfall figures on paper may appear normal or even above normal, with rainfall crossing 800 mm in 2026. However, this is leading to waterlogging, inadequate groundwater recharge and severe damage to crops.

‘Killed my husband, I should be hanged’:Beautician wife in Meerut confesses; says, ‘I miss him, regret it’
stories.summary: I killed my husband with the help of my lover and his friend. I request the law to give me the death penalty along with both of them. My husband used to fight with me every day. That day too, he strangled me and threatened to kill me. I then called my lover and asked him to come. I mixed a sedative into my husband’s food and gave it to him. My lover came with his friend. I held my husband’s legs, his friend held his hands, and my lover strangled him with a dupatta. I am missing my husband a lot. I regret what I did. I have done wrong. Meerut beautician Ilma made this confession while speaking to Dainik Bhaskar. The incident took place on September 28 in Zakir Nagar Colony under Lohia Nagar police station. After the murder, the family was informed that Talib had died of a heart attack, and they buried his body. However, after the deceased’s mobile phone was found on October 5, the family began suspecting his wife. When they questioned her strictly, she confessed to the murder. On Thursday, the grave was dug up and the body was exhumed and sent for post-mortem. Couple married 4 years ago; they have a 3-year-old daughter Talib (30), son of Zulfiqar from Rasulpur-Dabhedi village in Muzaffarnagar, married Ilma (27), daughter of Momin from Anjum Palace in Meerut’s Brahmapuri area, four years ago. They have a three-year-old daughter. Talib worked as a mason. After their marriage, he lived with his wife in a rented house in Zakir Nagar Colony, Meerut. Ilma worked at the nearby Signature Style Beauty Studio. Now read the accused wife’s full confession They had a fight in the afternoon; husband beat me badly Ilma said, “At around 3:30 pm on September 28, my husband Talib returned home from work. At that time, I had gone to give a facial to the landlord’s son’s wife. Talib called me, and I returned home shortly afterwards. When I reached home, Talib and his nephew Sharik were lying down. Talib asked me to knead the flour and make rotis. After I made the rotis, we had an argument over work. Talib beat me badly, after which I went and sat in another room. After some time, Talib came to call me and we had another argument.” Husband strangled me, so I called my lover Ilma said, “After the argument, I called my lover Aman and told him that Talib was beating me and threatening to kill me. He had also strangled me several times. Aman said over the phone that he was coming and would ‘deal with’ Talib after he arrived. “I then gave Talib food mixed with a sedative. After some time, Aman arrived. He was accompanied by another young man, his friend.” Wife held his legs, friend held his hands, Aman strangled him Ilma said, “Talib was unconscious. Aman’s friend held his hands while I held his legs. Aman then strangled Talib with a dupatta. I had met Aman around 13–14 months ago at 60-Futa crossing. He gave me his number and said he would help me get a job at a parlour. “Talib found out about Aman around 6–7 months ago. After that, they had several arguments and fights over the phone. However, Talib had never met Aman in person. He had only seen him in photographs.” Ilma said, ‘I don’t know what suddenly happened to me’ When Dainik Bhaskar asked Ilma why she broke the trust of her husband and her four-year-old marriage for a relationship that began around 14 months ago, and why she killed him, she said, “I don’t know myself what happened to me. I had no intention of killing my husband beforehand, but suddenly all this happened.” Daughter witnessed the murder Ilma said, “My husband beat me during the argument. He also threatened to hit our daughter. After that, I became even more angry with him. When we were killing my husband, our daughter was using a mobile phone. After the murder, when the dupatta was removed from my husband’s neck, the girl saw all of us. However, she did not say anything. “When asked about her daughter’s future, Ilma said that Talib’s family would look after her. “Nothing is going through my mind about what will happen next. I will accept whatever punishment the law gives me.” Mother said, ‘They got my son-in-law, who was like my own child, killed’ CO said, ‘Further action will be based on the post-mortem report’ Kotwali CO Sangram Singh said, “Talib’s grave was dug up and his body was exhumed in the presence of the administration. SDM Bhupendra Singh and CO Gajendra Singh, along with a large police force, were present during the process. The body has been sent for post-mortem. Further action will be taken based on the post-mortem report.”

stories.title: 11 UP athletes at Asian Games:One learnt javelin with stick, another drove cabs at night; one won ₹3 crore without playing
stories.summary: A total of 85 medals came to India at the Asian Games held in Aichi-Nagoya, Japan. Of these, 16 medals were won by athletes from UP — 5 gold, 3 silver and 8 bronze. These are not just medals, but the result of the struggles of 11 athletes who achieved success despite difficult circumstances. One athlete could not get a javelin for practice, so he peeled bamboo and made a spear-like javelin himself. Another lost his father, drove a cab in Delhi, supported his family and still brought glory to the country despite difficult circumstances. Let’s take a look at the stories of such athletes… The first story is of Rohit Yadav from Jaunpur. Rohit, who won a bronze medal in javelin throw, began practising not at a sports academy but in the fields of his village. He would help his father with farm work and often throw sticks to measure the distance. Rohit’s father, Sabhajeet Yadav, was himself an athlete. He recognised his son’s talent, but the family’s financial condition was so poor that he could not afford to buy a real javelin for him. Seeing Rohit’s growing passion, his father cut and peeled bamboo growing near their house in 2013 and made javelins for him. What happened next was that 14-year-old Rohit started practising his throws with the bamboo stick itself. Later, after saving money, he bought a javelin. He then began practising javelin throw every day. After 13 years of hard work, he finally reached the Asian Games. In the javelin throw final, he won the bronze medal with a throw of 84.35 metres. The government will now give him ₹75 lakh and a government job. Salman Khan from Amethi won a bronze medal in rowing. Salman is the eldest of four brothers and two sisters. He wanted to join the Indian Army and had started preparing for it at the age of 15. But when he turned 18, he lost his father. The responsibility of supporting the family fell on his shoulders. Salman was forced to go to Delhi to earn a living. He initially did small jobs and later started driving a cab. At night, when he would lie down in bed, he would remember his dream of joining the Indian Army. Salman was not someone who gave up easily. He began waking up at 5 am and practising 1,600-metre runs in a park. Sometimes, he would also run 4–5 kilometres. After persistent efforts, Salman finally joined the Army through the sports quota in 2018. It was here that he got an opportunity to train in rowing. Salman pushed himself so hard that today he has won a bronze medal for the country. Jay Kumar Nagar from Noida won a bronze medal in the 4x400-metre relay. Until 2019, he played kabaddi at the district level. Jay’s father runs a small grocery shop in Dadri. Seeing his son’s interest in sports, he got him enrolled at a sports stadium. With his father’s support, Jay left kabaddi and started running on the athletics track. He continued preparing for the 400-metre race every day. On the strength of seven years of rigorous training, he won a medal at the Asian Games. Jay will now receive ₹75 lakh from the UP government. Meeraj Ahmed Khan from Bulandshahr won a bronze medal in shooting at the age of 50. In the 1990s, Meeraj used to play cricket alongside Virender Sehwag. Both were part of the cricket team of Delhi’s Jamia Millia Islamia University. By the age of 28, Meeraj had captained the Under-19 team. Meeraj dreamed that whenever he played, his jersey would have the name ‘INDIA’ written on it. But he was unable to make it to the Ranji or national team. Meeraj comes from a landlord family. His father Ilyas Ahmed Khan, brother and uncle were all state-level trap shooters. Around 2003, when his cricket career reached a standstill, he went to Delhi’s Karni Singh Shooting Range with his cousin. There, he saw legendary shooters such as Raja Randhir Singh and Mansher Singh, whose jerseys carried the Indian Tricolour. This was when he found a way to fulfil his dream. He then said goodbye to his first love, cricket, and made shooting his career. Rajkumar from Ghazipur played an important role in helping the Indian team win the gold medal at the Asian Games. However, during the match against Bangladesh, he suffered a fracture in the thumb of his left hand. He could not play in the semi-final and final. However, his team registered a शानदार victory in the final to win gold. It also secured a ticket to the 2028 Los Angeles Olympics. Rajkumar Pal is the youngest of three brothers. His elder brothers Jokhan Pal and Rahul Pal were national-level hockey players. Watching them inspired Rajkumar to take up hockey as well. As a child, Rajkumar would play hockey with a bamboo stick and learn the art of scoring goals from his elder brother. When he was 10, his father, Kalika Pal, suddenly passed away. His elder brother Jokhan wanted to play at the international level, but the responsibility of the family now fell on his shoulders. Therefore, Jokhan handed his hockey stick to Rajkumar. He first took him to Karampur Stadium in Ghazipur and then to Meghbaran Singh Hockey Stadium, where Rajkumar learned the finer aspects of hockey. In 2012, Rajkumar was selected for the SAI Sports Hostel in Lucknow. Then, in 2018, another tragedy struck Rajkumar. His elder brother Jokhan Pal died after an illness. However, Rajkumar’s second brother Rahul and their mother Manraji Devi did not let his morale break. His mother and brother worked as labourers and arranged money for him, allowing Rajkumar to continue working hard. He eventually moved ahead and earned his place in the Indian hockey team. Vipraj will get ₹3 crore without playing, Gulveer to receive the highest reward Barabanki’s Vipraj Nigam is an all-rounder in the Indian cricket team. He was part of the 15-member squad selected for the Asian Games. However, he did not get an opportunity to play in any match during the tournament. Team India defeated Bangladesh in the semi-final. India were scheduled to face Afghanistan in the final, but the match could not be played due to rain. India were subsequently declared winners on the basis of their better ranking. Thus, Team India won the gold medal. As per the rules, every member of the squad is considered part of the victory. Therefore, even without bowling or batting a single ball, Vipraj Nigam will receive ₹3 crore from the UP government. He will also be offered a Class-I officer’s job. Gulveer Singh, a resident of Sirsa village in Aligarh, was UP’s most successful athlete this time. He won 2 silver and 1 bronze medal at the Asian Games. Earlier, Gulveer had also won 1 silver and 1 bronze at the Glasgow Commonwealth Games. If the five medals from the two major tournaments are considered together, Gulveer will receive the highest prize money from the UP government ₹5 crore. There was a time when it was difficult for him to arrange money to buy athletics kits and shoes. Today, Gulveer is among the athletes from UP receiving the highest prize money.

Amit Shah vows to eliminate every trace of Naxalism after five decades of tribal suffering
stories.summary: Amit Shah highlighted the importance of eradicating Naxalism to restore growth in Bastar, Chhattisgarh. He noted that significant efforts had been made in this regard by local tribal leadership. Shah mentioned a distribution program of assistive devices benefiting over 3,600 disabled individuals, particularly Naxal violence victims. He emphasized the need to heal the wounds from years of suffering while maintaining that Naxalism's end does not restore dignity immediately.

stories.title: US not to livestream execution of Fort Hood gunman Nidal Hasan
stories.summary: Former US Army Major Nidal Hasan is scheduled for execution by firing squad on December 3, for the 2009 shooting at the US Army's Fort Hood base in Texas. Donald Trump stated that the execution will not be livestreamed, despite previous announcements from the Pentagon. Howevr, immediate family members of the victims may attend in person, if they choose.

stories.title: Supreme Court seeks Centre’s response on plea to hold protest organisers liable for damage
stories.summary: The Supreme Court has requested responses regarding a plea to hold protest organizers accountable for damages. This includes potential liabilities for loss of life, injuries, and property damage incurred during protests. Additionally, the plea advocates for designated protest locations to minimize disturbances in densely populated areas. It proposes that protest organizers disclose their funding sources to ensure transparency.

stories.title: France begins implementing agreement to protect Saudi oil facilities; what it means
stories.summary: France has started deploying military resources to Saudi Arabia to protect its oil facilities from regional attacks. This decision follows an agreement aimed at enhancing defense cooperation, especially amid increased drone and missile threats. President Emmanuel Macron confirmed the deployment, which includes soldiers and defense systems to bolster security. Recent attacks by Houthi militants have escalated tensions in the area, raising concerns for energy stability.

stories.title: Donald Trump is looking for a replacement of Susie Wiles; 'She's burned a lot of people': Report
J&K HC restricts motorboat operations on Dal Lake
stories.summary: The high court of Jammu and Kashmir and Ladakh has ordered a ban on fuel-powered motorboats and jet skis on Dal Lake. Authorities are directed to enforce this prohibition strictly to protect the lake from pollution. The court suggested exploring solar-powered boats as an alternative for tourism-related activities. Emergency services and safety operations are exempt from this ban. A comprehensive policy on motorised boat operations is expected for further review.

stories.title: Bought in 2014, Magnolia’s Waco site grew from to 5.3 acres, adding shops, a ball field and church
stories.summary: In a remarkable transformation, Chip and Joanna Gaines have converted a historic cottonseed mill site in Waco into a buzzing tourist hub. Spanning 5.3 acres, the revitalized Magnolia property now features an array of shops, dining venues, and lush green spaces. Guests can experience restored historic buildings like the Old Church, while the newly built Katy Ballpark commemorates the original Katy Park.

stories.title: 'Stunned': Rahul urges President Murmu to put Dushyant Gautam’s appointment as Sikkim Governor on hold
Dhanush Narpani Iyakkam: Telugu star's fan club rebrands as welfare movement with new logo and flag
Zelenskyy claims jets hit: Ukraine says Su-34s struck with Neptune; vows long-range attacks continue
‘Please pretend I’m running’: Trump urges voters to back Republicans in US midterm elections
Meet Gabriella Rothberg, 17, who turned a sandwich idea into a patent for meat-flavoured tomatoes
stories.summary: A sandwich idea at 15 led Miami student Gabriella Rothberg to develop genetically engineered tomatoes designed to produce heme, an iron-containing molecule associated with meat flavour. Now 17, she is listed alongside her father on a US patent issued in June 2026. The project remains experimental, with taste and nutritional benefits yet to be established.

stories.title: Police shooting, water shortages, rising costs: Mauritius extends curfew amid unrest
stories.summary: Mauritius has extended a curfew for two additional nights after protests erupted over police violence. The unrest followed the shooting of a woman by a police officer in Camp Levieux, prompting increased tensions. Authorities reported over 100 arrests related to the disturbances and canceled school classes for security reasons. Anger over rising living costs and worsening water shortages has fueled public discontent across the island.

stories.title: IMD announces onset of winter monsoon in south Peninsular India, summer monsoon withdrawal completes on normal date
stories.summary: The southwest monsoon in India withdrew on schedule. Simultaneously, the northeast monsoon commenced, bringing rainfall to parts of south Peninsular India. Regions including Tamil Nadu, Puducherry, and coastal Andhra Pradesh experienced the initial winter rainfall. Predictions indicate a normal winter monsoon may provide relief after a significant summer rainfall deficit.

stories.title: Ex-IAS Divya Mittal launches own party: 10 civil servants who quit service to enter politics
stories.summary: Divya Mittal, an ex-IAS officer, has established the Jan Neeti Bharat party in preparation for the forthcoming elections. With a focus on enhancing citizen participation in policymaking rather than adhering to conventional governance methods, she aims to make a significant impact. Her decision to retire after 13 years in civil service aligns with a trend of bureaucrats entering politics.

stories.title: 13-year-old Indian-American wins $25,000 for ocean acidification solution
EC announces Special Summary Revision of voters' list in 17 states amid SIR row
stories.summary: While a Summary Revision focuses on new eligibles and routine corrections, SIR goes far deeper, involving statewide house-to-house verification, detailed scrutiny of entries, and large-scale data audits. For instance, under a Summary Revision, a voter who has shifted homes must file a form to update their address. Under SIR, the Booth Level Officer visits that address, confirms whether the voter still lives there, checks if anyone new has become eligible, and updates the roll based on physical verification rather than waiting for the voter to initiate the change.

stories.title: President Murmu accepts L Murugan’s resignation amid buzz over Union Cabinet reshuffle
Evening news wrap: India seeks US probe into Illinois Hindu temple attack plot; BJP calls Rahul 'anarchic' & more
stories.summary: Men cheered outside a bathroom where a woman was reportedly being sexually assaulted at a Chicago party. India has called for a US investigation into a potential mass shooting plot against a Hindu temple. The BJP criticized Rahul Gandhi for undermining institutions during protests against the chief election commissioner. Congress questioned the government’s silence on Marco Rubio's planned visit to India.

stories.title: Pakistan ranks lowest in South Asia on hunger index amid rising food prices
stories.summary: Pakistan's 2026 Global Hunger Index standings reveal an alarming crisis, showcasing the worst performance in South Asia amid ongoing economic challenges. Soaring food prices and the increasing frequency of climate-related disasters have sharply intensified food insecurity. With around 218 million individuals in South Asia experiencing undernourishment from 2023 to 2025, urgent strategies are required to bolster access to healthy food and enhance agricultural resilience against severe weather patterns.

stories.title: Akhilesh’s anti-BJP formula for UP: PDA, Muslim-Yadav votes and Gen Z
Lula or Bolsonaro: Why Brazil's presidential election matters for Brics and India
stories.summary: Brics began with five members and grew to eleven after the 2024 expansion, with Indonesia the newest, joining in 2025. Brazil opposed the enlargement, particularly because of the one nation. Iran. It feared that adding the avowedly anti-West Islamic Republic would cost the group its cohesion. Like India, Brazil wants Brics to be reformist and not revolutionary, thereby limiting it to a body that argues for change inside the existing order rather than one that tries to replace it.

stories.title: 'We all want regime change, anything wrong?' Bhushan attacks government; BJP hits back
Opened in 2005, Lucas’ 850,000-sq-ft San Francisco campus spans 23 acres, with 4 buildings
stories.summary: In the heart of San Francisco, the former military hospital site has been ingeniously repurposed into the Letterman Digital Arts Center. This vibrant digital arts hub, established by George Lucas in 2005 post-demolition, now serves as a creative haven for Lucasfilm and other innovative firms. Careful attention to open spaces fosters community interaction and leisure, showcasing a successful model for urban redevelopment and creative collaborations.

stories.title: California cement worker turned discarded bottles into 200 desert art trees along Route 66
stories.summary: California cement worker Elmer Long transformed discarded glass bottles and scrap metal into an unusual art forest along Route 66. His two-acre Bottle Tree Ranch, featuring around 200 trees and over 1,000 bottles, became a popular tourist attraction. As Route 66 celebrates its 100th anniversary in 2026, Long's family continues to preserve his creations.

stories.title: Isaiah Zagar's 3,000-sq-ft Philadelphia maze of bottles and bike wheels was saved in 2004
stories.summary: Philadelphia's Magic Gardens, a vibrant masterpiece by Isaiah Zagar, comprises stunning mosaics made from found objects that capture his personal journey and artistic influences. In 2004, when demolition loomed, local advocates banded together to form a nonprofit, securing the beloved site. Over the years, Zagar enriched the gardens with imaginative tunnels and diverse mosaics, right up to his death in 2026.

stories.title: Former FBI building in Washington handed to receiver over $221.6 million debt
‘Anything possible in politics’: Sachin Pilot on speculation over Amarinder Singh’s return to Congress
stories.summary: Sachin Pilot remarked on the potential for Captain Amarinder Singh's return to Congress, emphasizing that politics is unpredictable. While Singh expressed dissatisfaction with the BJP, he has not discussed his future political plans with Pilot. Singh previously led the Congress in Punjab and left over internal conflicts within the party. He later formed the Punjab Lok Congress which did not succeed in recent elections.

stories.title: Govt issues clarification on 'unconditional apology' in SC over internet shutdown
stories.summary: In a statement, the government reacted to the media reports that the Union home secretary Govind Mohan had tendered an unconditional apology to the Supreme Court in response to a contempt notice. It said whenever the Supreme Court issues a contempt notice, the party responding to it is required to begin its affidavit with an unconditional apology, followed by the presentation of other facts and arguments.

Florida woman lets couple charge phone; they steal her car and crash during police chase
Ontario homeowner property listed for sheriff’s sale after $520,000 court order
Kumaraswamy slams Karnataka government over questioning of JD(S) workers
stories.summary: H D Kumaraswamy has voiced strong concerns about the Karnataka government allegedly targeting JD(S) members after a supposed sting operation. He reported that a party worker was detained at an undisclosed place without legal notice. Kumaraswamy staged a protest outside the police commissioner's office and expressed his willingness to be investigated, raising issues of biased investigations against opposition figures and social media actions.

'Planned terrorist acts on behalf of Ukraine': Swedish national arrested in Russia
stories.summary: Russia’s FSB has detained a Swedish national accused of planning terrorist acts and sabotage for Ukraine. The agency claims he illegally crossed the border to execute these attacks on military facilities. Identified as Freddy Lindholm, he allegedly trained in drone operations after signing a contract with Ukraine’s army. His detention highlights Russian measures against foreign espionage amid ongoing tensions. The situation remains sensitive with varying international responses to the allegations.

stories.title: Erika Kirk pens emotional tribute to late husband Charlie Kirk on his birthday - video
Supreme Court issues notice on SIR petition, seeks records of EC decision-making
Oregon woman sold home to son-in-law, says he promised she could stay for life; court rejects claim
stories.summary: An Oregon woman who sold her home worth approximately $398,000 to her son-in-law for $270,000 in 2006 claimed she was promised the right to live there for life. After a dispute over her occupancy, a trial court ruled in her favour. However, the Oregon Court of Appeals overturned the decision, finding that the written sale documents transferred her entire ownership interest without reserving a life estate.

stories.title: CJP's Dipke questions Imran Khan's 'Leave India' notice, cites Mary Millben's support for BJP
'Growing concern over anti-India hate in US': MEA demands probe into Hindu temple attack plot
stories.summary: The ministry of external affairs (MEA) has raised concerns about an alleged conspiracy aimed at a Hindu temple in the US. It called for a comprehensive investigation came following the arrest of Alexandros Paporakis in Illinois, accused of plotting a mass shooting driven at a Hindu temple in Aurora, Illinois. Authorities uncovered alarming evidence tied to extremist views at his residence, leading the MEA to demand justice and advocate for community safety measures.

stories.title: 'Where anti-Indian hatred can lead': US lawmaker Raja Krishnamoorthi's warning after plot targeting Aurora Hindu temple
Duty-free billionaire Chuck Feeney gave Cornell $350 million in 2011; six years later, its New York tech campus opened
stories.summary: In 2011, Chuck Feeney, a notable billionaire, pledged an impressive $350 million to create Cornell Tech in New York City. This generous gesture was pivotal in clinching a contest for a new technology campus. Launched in phases starting in 2017, this initiative integrates academic research with industry collaboration. Feeney believed in living philanthropy, contributing nearly $1 billion to Cornell and global causes throughout his life.

stories.title: London’s oldest restaurant, where Edward VII met his mistress and showbiz stars gathered, is now protected by the National Trust
stories.summary: A historic restaurant in London, renowned for its royal visitors and celebrity clientele over the past 228 years, has been gifted to a conservation organization to ensure its legacy. The donation encompasses the building alongside valuable memorabilia to support conservation initiatives. Operations of the restaurant will persist, securing jobs for its staff while marking a paramount effort in safeguarding this cultural icon for future generations.

stories.title: Jenny McCarthy co-hosted a pet contest; raised $8 million for 25-acre centre
Pennsylvania man’s home sold for $28,000 over unpaid taxes; court overturns sale after 4 years
stories.summary: A Pennsylvania man who owned a Chester home for 10 years saw it sold for $28,000 at a tax sale over unpaid property taxes, with an upset price of $5,741. On October 13, 2026, the Commonwealth Court of Pennsylvania overturned the sale, ruling that officials had failed to make reasonable efforts to notify him after a notice was returned unclaimed.

Nando’s billionaire buys North Bondi beach house for $17.4M
stories.summary: A beach house located on the Ben Buckler headland has been sold for A$17.4 million. Richard Enthoven, the owner of Nando's, and his wife bought the property recently. This four-bedroom home is designed for comfortable coastal living and features luxurious amenities throughout. The sale was completed on June 20, highlighting the property's appeal and the buyers' interests.

stories.title: Over 150 more 'Aam Aadmi Clinics' opened in Punjab: CM Bhagwant Mann
stories.summary: Chief Minister Bhagwant Mann dedicated 154 new Aam Aadmi Clinics to support healthcare initiatives across Punjab. He emphasized the significance of quality healthcare, education, and employment for all. Mann warned that changing the government could jeopardize public welfare programs like free bus travel for women. The new clinics are part of a larger commitment to accessible and affordable healthcare for families in need.

stories.title: Arizona homebuilder spent years and thousands of dollars building a 4,000-foot backyard railway
stories.summary: Arizona businessman Dennis Sirrine spent years and hundreds of thousands of dollars transforming his backyard into one of America's largest private garden railways. Started in 2004, the Palo Verde & Southwestern Railroad featured nearly 4,000 feet of track, hundreds of model train cars, artificial mountains and lakes. The project involved extensive construction, repeated rebuilding and a specially designed operating system.

stories.title: Demi Moore owns 2,000 art dolls and once planned to turn them into a museum
Obama’s Chicago presidential center went from a $500 million plan to $850 million
Shakira’s $3.68 million contribution helps Cartagena school educate 1,000+ children yearly
stories.summary: In 2014, Colombian superstar Shakira embarked on a noble mission by establishing the Lomas del Peyé school in Cartagena, aimed at supporting at-risk children. Each year, this invaluable institution serves over 1,000 students, with a capacity to educate 1,700. Shakira's foundation has generously funded approximately $3.68 million of the total $8 million needed for construction.

stories.title: 'Nobody can browbeat judiciary': SC issues notice to Rahul Gandhi, Akhilesh Yadav and others over October 12 march
Paul Bocuse’s culinary school now trains 1,200 students from 75 nationalities across two French castles
stories.summary: Institut Lyfe, formerly known as Institut Paul Bocuse, is a premier institution dedicated to culinary arts and hospitality education. Founded in 1990, it now serves a diverse international student community of 1,200. With modern facilities in two castles, students enjoy enriched experiences. Notably, it conducts advanced research and boasts a Michelin-starred restaurant, Saisons, highlighting its dedication to quality in hospitality education.

stories.title: ACP Vivek Bhagat case: HC refuses urgent hearing on woman journalist’s arrest protection plea
'Open admission of regime change': BJP targets Rahul over Neha Bora's 'Bangladesh showed us the way' remark
Naples Pier Reef Deployment: Hurricane Ian debris becomes artificial reef; rebuilding project continues
stories.summary: In an inspiring move, pieces from the historical Naples Pier, damaged by Hurricane Ian, are being transformed into vital marine habitats. This initiative involves placing 59 concrete pilings at Wasmer Reef, providing support for diverse marine life. Not only does this project recycle construction debris, but it also fosters new ecosystems. Future reconstruction efforts for Naples Pier will emphasize improved safety and resilience to withstand upcoming storms.

stories.title: Could the dodo return? US firm maps 95% of its genome and identifies gene-editing targets
stories.summary: Colossal Biosciences aims to resurrect the extinct dodo bird using cutting-edge gene-editing technologies. By leveraging their sophisticated AI platform, GenoMorph, the company has pinpointed essential genetic traits. With 95% of the dodo genome analysis complete, their ambitious project is on track, though a specific timeline for the living dodo remains undisclosed. This groundbreaking venture is part of a larger initiative to counteract the effects of human-induced species extinction.

'They silence voices of victims': Rahul, Kharge slam detention of Ankita Bhandari's parents
Actor Imran Khan told to leave India by October 28 for protesting in Mumbai
'Go to jail or be shot’: Trump warns US military secret leakers
stories.summary: Trump issued a warning to those leaking military secrets, suggesting jail or execution as consequences. He also discussed the bombing of Iran's nuclear facilities and threats against leakers. The Pentagon is planning a live-stream execution of Nidal Malik Hasan for his 2009 attack at Fort Hood. Trump confirmed support for this execution, emphasizing that he is indifferent to the method used.

stories.title: 'Can Hindus Eat Beef? BJP IT Cell Part 2': Dhruv Rathee faces two defamation cases in 24 hours
Oct 10 Jantar Mantar protest permission denied due to violence during CJP protest on Jul 20: Delhi Police
How opposition to data centres is bringing Democrats and Republicans together
‘Timely action’: India welcomes US response after Illinois teen held over Hindu temple attack plot
Con Edison’s $300M Bronx substation mimics a row of homes as $47.3M upgrade gets approval
stories.summary: Con Edison is set to invest $47.3 million in enhancing the East 179th Street substation in the Bronx. This vital upgrade will include the installation of a fifth transformer and a new feeder line. The initiative aims to bolster the local electric capacity, facilitating support for electrification and electric vehicles.

stories.title: NYC subway hides ventilation shaft and emergency exit behind 1847 Brooklyn townhouse façade
stories.summary: Nestled at 58 Joralemon Street in Brooklyn Heights lies a historic brownstone that harbors a subway ventilation shaft beneath its surface. Established in 1847, it transformed into a vital transit hub in 1908 under the Brooklyn Rapid Transit Company. The building's unchanged facade allows it to integrate seamlessly into the neighborhood while fulfilling crucial safety roles.

stories.title: Lake Ringgold Reservoir Permit: Judge overturns state approval; Wichita Falls weighs appeal
stories.summary: In a significant legal development, a Texas judge has scrapped the permit for the Lake Ringgold reservoir, amidst ongoing opposition from local ranchers concerned about environmental issues and property rights. Wichita Falls aims to appeal this ruling as they push for their water supply plans. This situation underscores the complex relationship between infrastructure advancements and conservation, with the city's next moves remaining unclear.

Australian court orders bamboo removal after roots block neighbour’s sewer, awards A$6,253 in damages
stories.summary: In a landmark decision, an Australian court addressed a bamboo dispute affecting two neighboring properties in New South Wales. The court determined that the bamboo created a blockage and posed a risk for future damage to the sewer line. As a result, Homes NSW was ordered to compensate A$6,253.50 for previous treatment costs. The ruling highlights the importance of communication and diligent records for homeowners facing similar issues.

stories.title: ED seizes assets worth over Rs 2,000 crore of Reliance Power
Meet Aryash Shyam, 14-year-old Indian-American who won $1,000 for a story set in 1776
stories.summary: Indian-American student Aryash Shyam, 14, has won a $1,000 national writing prize for his historical-fiction story set in a Philadelphia print shop on July 4, 1776. The Pennsylvania ninth-grader was among four middle-school winners of the 2026 John Estey Student Writing Competition. He has also earned recognition for projects involving space research, artificial intelligence and robotics.

stories.title: West Bengal BJP must get rid of its 'garbage': RSS magazine
Many Indians willingly joining Russian forces, government informs SC
Walsh Warns On AI Chatbots: US commentator fears ‘friend-like’ bonds; questions big tech power
stories.summary: Matt Walsh criticized the growing use of AI chatbots among young people in an October 14 post on X. He warned that people could begin treating AI systems as friends and spending much of their day talking to them. Walsh has also raised concerns about AI's effects on jobs, films, music, and advertising, arguing that technology could change human relationships and creative work.

stories.title: SC: Order to clear Form 6 anomaly will come October 28
Scottish church turned into five-bedroom home and bistro
stories.summary: The Old Kirk, a former church, has undergone extensive renovations to become a family home. The property features five bedrooms and spacious living areas, combining original charm with modern elements. It currently operates as a bistro while being on the market for offers over £550,000. The home retains beautiful architectural details, including arched windows and high ceilings. Surrounding gardens provide a peaceful setting and enhance the property’s appeal.

stories.title: 'Faced a lot of racism': Indian woman working as a nurse in Australia asks if not liking life abroad a good reason to return. Redditors say...
Woman buys £15,000 diamond ring for just £5 at car boot sale
stories.summary: A woman found a ring at a car boot sale that cost her £5 and initially seemed ordinary. She later took the ring to a valuation event at WeBuyVintage for a professional opinion. The gemologist examined the ring, discovering it was a genuine diamond set in 18-carat gold. The estimated value of the ring was approximately £15,000, shocking the woman who bought it.

stories.title: In 1930, a Pittsburgh plumber built an aluminium observatory that helped him meet Einstein
stories.summary: Established in 1930 by Leo Scanlon, the Valley View Observatory in Pittsburgh quickly gained traction among amateur astronomers, primarily due to its cost-effective construction and unique aluminium dome. Scanlon's fresh approach drew attention from enthusiasts nationwide, leading to a memorable encounter with Albert Einstein in 1934, who appreciated the spirit of amateur science. To honor its significant role in astronomy, asteroid 8131 was named 'Scanlon', recognizing the observatory's legacy.

stories.title: Parts of Ontario move to permanent daylight saving time to avoid disruption for businesses and families. What will happen on November 1?
Georgia farmer turned scrap metal into folk art, filling his yard with figures that reached museums
stories.summary: After stepping away from farming and preaching, Reuben Aaron Miller channeled his creativity into art. He crafted enchanting, wind-powered whirligigs and striking metal figures that captured the attention of collectors near and far. His partnership with R.E.M. propelled his art to new heights, significantly boosting its market value. Now featured in numerous museum exhibitions, Miller's work continues to resonate within the American folk-art community.

New Zealand couple turns old school into a home with a twist
stories.summary: After acquiring a rundown school in Tokanui, Ian and Sue Rogers dedicated years and around NZ$250,000 to revitalize the property, successfully turning it into a beloved family residence. They maintained many of the school’s original features, which highlight its rich history. They even converted a damaged swimming pool into a delightful chalet. Eager for their next venture, the couple has decided against tackling another school renovation.

stories.title: London man bought painting for £45 in 1968; it turned out to be a Van Gogh worth up to €15 million
stories.summary: A painting bought for just £45 from a London junk shop in 1968 was later authenticated as an original Vincent van Gogh. The artwork, which had previously sold for only £4 at a farm sale in 1967, changed hands several times before being sold to a private collector for approximately €12 million to €15 million in 2020.

In 1956, Tressa Prisbrey turned discarded bottles into a 15-building folk-art village in California
stories.summary: Tressa Prisbrey, at age 60, began building Bottle Village using glass bottles from a local landfill. Over 25 years, she constructed 15 unique structures dedicated to her lost children and their memories. The site eventually became a cultural landmark and received various recognitions for its artistic significance. Visitors paid small admission fees to see her creative work and hear her story.

stories.title: Alice Waters’ school garden project grew into a global network of 5,800 programmes across 75 countries
stories.summary: Launched back in 1995 in California, the Edible Schoolyard Project has blossomed into a global initiative founded by chef Alice Waters. The project imparts essential lessons on gardening and environmental stewardship, seamlessly integrating with subjects like science and math. With a mission to foster healthy eating habits, it has inspired educational platforms across more than 75 countries, aiming to weave food education into everyday school curricula for enhanced student wellbeing.

stories.title: 'Shocked': Odisha governor's 'will work for BJP' remark sparks political row

Uttarakhand bans sale of gutkha, paan masala, tobacco products for one year: CM Dhami
stories.summary: Uttarakhand Chief Minister Pushkar Singh Dhami on Wednesday said the state government has imposed a one-year ban on the sale of gutkha, paan masala and tobacco products, stressing the need to curb addiction and protect the younger generation.

stories.title: Shania Twain turns childhood hunger into school support for vulnerable children through her charity
stories.summary: Founded in 2010, Shania Twain's Shania Kids Can initiative seeks to empower children facing poverty and food insecurity. The program provides academic help and emotional support in a nurturing school atmosphere, aiming to enhance children's self-esteem, food security, and mental health, all vital for effective learning. With dedicated Clubhouses, the foundation directly engages with children in their everyday setting, steadily reaching out to underserved communities throughout North America.

stories.title: TVK to join INDIA bloc's anti-CEC protest in Chennai as Congress-DMK rift deepens
A judge voided Rhode Island’s seizure of 31 acres planned for 252 affordable homes
stories.summary: A federal judge ruled against the Town of Johnston, asserting the town lacked authority to seize a property. The judge's decision allows the Santoro family to proceed with a 252-unit affordable housing project. The town had attempted to use eminent domain to halt the development, claiming the land was needed for a municipal complex. Legal challenges arose regarding the town’s adherence to proper procedures and public notification.

stories.title: Indian-origin man in Australia denied bail for 'stalking' woman he met on dating app; judge says risk to her safety 'too great'
Scientists mapped a locked zone behind Kamchatka’s 2025 magnitude-8.8 quake
Child among 6 killed in small plane crash in Wisconsin; FAA, NTSB probe underway
stories.summary: Six individuals lost their lives, including a child, after a plane crash in Wisconsin Dells. The small Piper PA-46 was travelling from Kenosha to Menomonie when it went down. Weather conditions at the time are being investigated to determine their impact on the crash. Authorities received reports of the aircraft down just before 10 pm, with rescue teams finding no survivors.

stories.title: Pleas filed in SC, Delhi HC against de-notification of Jantar Mantar as protest site
stories.summary: The application was filed on Wednesday by IYC president Uday Bhanu Chib in a pending petition over the denial of permission to hold the demonstration at Jantar Mantar in central Delhi. The organisation has challenged a standing order issued on October 11. The order removed Jantar Mantar from the list of designated protest sites and named Ramlila Ground, Burari Ground and CBD Ground in east Delhi as alternative venues.

Cleveland must consider compensation after rezoning a $52,100 used-car lot investment for housing

The firm had invested in land with plans for a used-car dealership, but the city reclassified the site from commercial to residential, derailing their business intentions. TMS argued this decision violated their property rights. The court upheld the initial judgment, initiating the steps for formal compensation proceedings.

stories.title: A UK civil servant allegedly earned £349,378 across eight government jobs between 2020 and 2023
stories.summary: A UK civil servant allegedly earned £349,378 across eight government jobs between February 2020 and September 2023. Kashim Chowdhury, 55, reportedly held five full-time roles simultaneously and was contracted to work 183 hours a week. He is accused of fraudulently securing positions at several government departments and denies nine counts of fraud.

Their nationalities have not been reported.

stories.title: 700 supermarkets hit, millions lost: France warns refrigeration cyberattacks may persist
stories.summary: A cyberattack targeting refrigeration systems at supermarkets in France has led to significant disruptions in food supply chains. The attack, which occurred on Monday, affected approximately 700 supermarkets, causing spoilage and financial losses. Authorities warn that the cyber threats might still be active, urging retailers to enhance their security measures. Investigations are ongoing, but no group has claimed responsibility for these incidents.

For years, this bowl was displayed proudly in their home until appraisers revealed its true worth: a rare 'Ding' ware from the Northern Song dynasty valued between $200,000 to $300,000. The piece garnered attention and sold for an astounding $2,225,000 at a Sotheby’s auction in March 2013.

With its autograph and verified ownership, the jersey's value soared, especially as interest in Jordan's last championship season continues to grow, attracting avid collectors and investors alike.

Journalist Rosy, Gajendra Singh, who is associated with a news portal, and an unidentified person have been named as accused. The case has been registered under provisions of the Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act.

stories.title: ‘Advancing our Strategic Partnership’: EAM Jaishankar meets Canadian counterpart Anita Anand as India, Canada push to reset ties
stories.summary: External Affairs Minister S Jaishankar and Canadian Foreign Minister Anita Anand met to enhance bilateral relations. They discussed trade, investment, energy, defense, and education, aiming to advance the Strategic Partnership. Prime Ministers Modi and Carney also spoke to build momentum towards the India-Canada Comprehensive Economic Partnership Agreement. Canadian corporate delegation is exploring joint ventures in multiple sectors during their visit.

‘Very risky choice’: Meloni warns US-Russia diesel deal could help fund Ukraine war
stories.summary: Giorgia Meloni has expressed concerns about the US agreement with Russia regarding diesel supplies during her parliament address. She believes the deal could financially aid Russia's war efforts in Ukraine. Meloni urged the European Union to appoint a representative for negotiating peace talks with Russia. Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy criticized the agreement, stating it could further support Moscow's military actions.

stories.title: New York art teacher’s thrift-store painting bought for under $100 sells for £189,200 after 60 years
stories.summary: A remarkable transformation has occurred for a painting acquired for under $100, which has now fetched an astonishing £189,200 due to its true provenance being uncovered. Hidden for decades within a family's home, the artwork, initially misattributed, is revealed to be the work of Scottish artist Francis Campbell Boileau Cadell.

Acquired for $13.5 million in 2009, the property underwent an extensive six-year renovation. Featuring 20 rooms and luxurious amenities such as a wine cellar and soundproof theater, the sale could set a new record for townhouse prices, surpassing the $77.

stories.title: 'Your Didi is with you - today and forever!' Mamata Banerjee to detained CJP activists
stories.summary: In a message posted on X on Wednesday, Banerjee condemned the arrests of Ashutosh Ranka and Saurav Das, who were sent to judicial custody, and assured young people of her support. “Your Didi is with you - today and forever!” she wrote. The arrests came amid opposition protests in Delhi over alleged electoral irregularities and demands for the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) Gyanesh Kumar.

stories.title: 'Why are you ruining nation?' CJP's Abhijeet Dipke heckled with 'CIA agent' remark at Delhi airport
stories.summary: Dipke landed in Delhi a day after his party's co-convenors, Saurav Das and Ashutosh Ranka, surreptitiously climbed a gate at the prohibited area of Jantar Mantar to protest against Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) Gyanesh Kumar and the government, which has denotified Jantar Mantar as a designated protest site. Later, Das and Ranka were sent to 5-day judicial custody on the order of Delhi's special executive magistrate court.

stories.title: Hijack code 7500 appeared, pilots said all normal: The mystery behind Air India's Frankfurt-Delhi flight scare
Wall Street titan lists bulletproof Upper East Side mansion for $80 million; property could become the neighbourhood’s priciest
stories.summary: John Mack and his wife Christy are putting their lavish Upper East Side townhouse on the market for a staggering $80 million. Selling at this price would establish a new benchmark for townhouses in New York City. Since purchasing it in 2009, they have extensively renovated the property, resulting in a 16,000-square-foot masterpiece that boasts upscale features such as a wellness club and exclusive guest quarters.

stories.title: Erin French rebuilt her life after losing her first restaurant; her Maine eatery now receives 60,000 reservation postcards a year
stories.summary: Erin French's remarkable journey saw her battling through addiction, enduring depression, and facing a heartbreaking divorce that led to the closure of her restaurant. Returning to her roots in Freedom, she innovatively launched pop-up dining events, rekindling her culinary passion. In 2014, she triumphantly reopened The Lost Kitchen in a refurbished mill, emphasizing seasonal, locally sourced goods, with a unique postcard reservation system that draws about 60,000 requests each year.

India seeks Indo-Pacific where all countries make their own choices, protect their interests: Rajnath Singh
stories.summary: Rajnath Singh emphasised that India’s Act East policy and the vision of SAGAR (Security and Growth for All in the Region) and MAHASAGAR (Mutual and Holistic Advancement for Security and Growth Across Regions) advocate for an open and multipolar cooperation, and the nation aligns them through ASEAN-led mechanisms that are central to its Indo-Pacific vision.

From 'Indira Gandhi' to 'PM': Cabinet approves renaming of pension schemes

By prefixing these initiatives linked to pensions for the elderly, widows, and disabled individuals with 'PM', the administration seeks to modernize their appeal. Notably, the National Social Assistance Programme will be renamed PM Shayata Yojna to reinforce this updated branding strategy.

stories.summary: Weeds can significantly impact crop yield, leading to a need for effective control methods. A USDA-funded trial demonstrated that cardboard beds reduced weed coverage compared to tilled beds. Farmers found that using cardboard made weeding easier and more efficient after two growing seasons. The results from the trial showed varied crop yields when grown in different bed types.

They raise questions about whether Indian authorities can effectively monitor and control local traffic. Additionally, the organization points to possible misuse by criminal organizations and the challenges posed by a foreign service potentially flouting local laws.

'Murdering democracy': Opposition slams Centre for the arrest of CJP leaders; Dipke extends gratitude
'Abhijieet Dipke, CJP funded by US donors': Singer Mary Millben backs PM Modi; pushes for counter-movement
stories.summary: Mary Millben has alleged that US-based donors are funding individuals opposing Prime Minister Narendra Modi. She encouraged young Indians to rise up against disruptive forces and defend democracy. Millben highlighted a pattern among some US donors targeting conservative leaders globally. BJP leaders have raised questions about the funding of the Cockroach Janta Party and its founder. Dipke has denied allegations of receiving foreign funds, challenging government oversight.

stories.title: Polyethylene Microplastics And Liver Risk: Texas A&M links exposure to fatty liver signs; questions remain for human health
stories.summary: New research from Texas A&M University indicates that polyethylene microplastics may affect liver health negatively. The study observed significant signs of fatty liver disease linked to polyethylene exposure and a high-fat diet. Researchers found changes in gene activity related to fat metabolism and tissue repair. Future investigations will focus on whether these pollutants contribute to more severe liver damage.

stories.title: Two Arizona brothers, aged 10 and 12, vanished into the desert; a helicopter-assisted search found them safe after eight hours
stories.summary: On October 11, a frantic search ensued for two young brothers, Atom and Jack Ward, who vanished while playing outside. Their worried father alerted authorities when they didn't return home. A collaborative effort involving local businesses and rescue teams, along with aerial support from the Arizona Department of Public Safety, led to their discovery six miles from home, with one boy still barefoot.

stories.title: NASA’s Perseverance rover breaks Mars driving record, covering 28.1 miles in five years
stories.summary: NASA's Perseverance rover has set a new distance record on Mars, traveling 28.10 miles in its mission, eclipsing the previous record of 28.06 miles set by Opportunity in nearly 15 years. This remarkable feat, achieved over five and a half years, showcases Perseverance's advanced autonomous navigation system as it investigates ancient geological structures and collects rock samples to enhance our scientific insights.

Bomb threat in Air India Frankfurt-Delhi flight: Pilot pressed hijack code; plane diverted to Jaipur

The pilot took immediate action by activating the hijack alert code while flying over the Mumbai Flight Information Region. After a safe landing in Jaipur, the aircraft was moved to an isolated area for comprehensive security evaluations.

stories.title: 11-year-old builds 450-member water network and moss filter to tackle lead in school water
stories.summary: Nithya Tammana, a passionate young advocate, noticed rampant water wastage at home, prompting her to launch Save Drop. This initiative has attracted over 450 young changemakers dedicated to preserving water resources. Through impactful campaigns, she stresses the necessity of altering daily water conservation habits. Furthermore, she developed BioLayer, a nature-inspired water filter designed to enhance water quality, earning accolades for her contributions to environmental sustainability.

stories.summary: Many people struggle with mental health issues for over a year before seeking professional help. Surveys indicate that a notable number faced thoughts of self-harm prior to receiving support. Indicators of distress typically included anxiety, stress, mood swings, and relationship challenges. Throughout this period, individuals often turned to informal networks like friends and family for initial support, who were key in recognizing mental health struggles.

They decided to relocate the house to their purchased farmland in North Dakota. The family home, built in 1914, carries five generations of JaSondra’s family history. After overcoming several setbacks, they finally acquired the house through a family agreement. The couple is committed to preserving their family legacies through this renovation project.

stories.title: He paid $50 for a chair that later sold for $107,950
stories.summary: Justin Miller, a home design content creator, purchased a chair from Facebook Marketplace for $50. After researching, he discovered it was a rare piece made by Frits Henningsen. Sotheby’s auctioned the chair, which was restored and had an estimated value of $30,000 to $50,000. The auction saw the chair sell for an impressive total of $107,950 including premiums. Miller continues to seek valuable items on platforms like Facebook Marketplace.

This foundation focuses on promoting swimming, water safety, and healthy living for young people. Programs like 'im' aim to instill confidence and coping skills among children. The foundation has expanded to include mental health education during the COVID-19 pandemic. Partnerships with organizations ensure these programs reach diverse communities across the globe.

Residents rallied to save the historic property, raising $2.2 million to buy it back before donating it to a nonprofit foundation. Today, the site features a reconstructed childhood home and interactive historical exhibits for visitors.

stories.title: Koos Bekker’s company controls 2,700 acres in Somerset, employs 650 locals as expansion sparks debate

Many residents welcome the job opportunities, while others voice concerns about the estate's impact on community identity, land stewardship, and environmental sustainability, illustrating the complexity of fostering development without compromising local values.

The case follows Thornton’s November airport arrest over an outstanding larceny warrant. The allegations remain unresolved in court.

stories.title: Chobani founder Hamdi Ulukaya builds 400-company network to help refugees find jobs
stories.summary: Hamdi Ulukaya arrived in the United States in 1994, overcoming significant language and cultural obstacles. He founded Chobani, prioritizing the hiring of refugees to combat their employment challenges. In 2016, he initiated Tent to enhance job prospects for refugees within multiple industries. Collaborating with UNHCR, Ulukaya aims to forge connections between refugees and jobs, facilitating their economic incorporation into local communities.
